OP-GVC2-RP.title: Rank-efficient Laplacian polarization after binary GVC
OP-GVC2-RP.scope: GVC2ENV proves unrestricted GVC for constant-coefficient differential operators in two variables by Hall-envelope separation; the earlier degree-five through degree-seven calculations and the parked Hall/carry promotion program GVC2ALL are retained as independent regressions and route history. The remaining open problem in this entry is ordinary-Laplacian compression of nonseparable Image-Mathieu data: replace the third-order Dvorsky operator by a quadratic constant-coefficient operator with few auxiliary variables while preserving a mixed obstruction. The separable form f=A(zeta)P(z) is rank one, whereas SIC2C4 has coefficient-matrix rank five. DVG4 excludes the canonical one-pair quadratic completion at the second pure moment. No successful rank-efficient quadraticization or improved ordinary-Laplacian counterexample endpoint is currently proved. The historical binary narrowing chain consists of GVC2UFT, GVC2FTS, GVC2WTD, GVC2FG, GVC2CRR, GVC2F5S, GVC2D5F, GVC2D5Q4, GVC2D5Q31, GVC2D5Q2, GVC2D5U, GVC2D6Q5, GVC2D6R2, GVC2D6R3, GVC2D6R4, GVC2D6R5, GVC2D6U, GVC2D7R2, GVC2D7R3, GVC2D7H, GVC2D7U, and GVC2ENV.

OP-GVC3-MIN.title: Minimum homogeneous GVC(3) degree and Laplacian-power frontier
OP-GVC3-MIN.scope: GVC3HC gives a homogeneous ternary counterexample for Lambda=Delta^6 with deg(P)=12, and GVC3PT proves the original scoped minimum. GVC3CPS now closes the arbitrary-profile loophole in that architecture: every normalized phase-square one-profile homogeneous lift in the same three variables is P_(r,S,h), so its power is N=6r+3e+h>=6r and equality N=6 is unique at primitive winding with constant profile and no radial suspension. Thus any witness for Delta^k with 1<=k<=5 must use multiple phase profiles, odd height dependence, a different homogeneous power map, or a mechanism not generated by the cusp endpoint divisor. The global minimum remains open: find such a homogeneous witness of degree 2k<12 or prove a lower bound in a precisely declared larger architecture. GVC3IPQ excludes the complete independent-linear quartic parity repair for k=2, while GVC3PT excludes the common-linear repair. GVC3IHC additionally excludes every balanced degree-four-through-ten family made from two or three distinct harmonic summands with one isotropic coherent state in each: its first nine moments force a one-direction terminal form. GVC3FCCB treats the unique four-channel degree-eight coherent family: all coefficient faces, all direction collisions, and the four-distinct B=0 boundary are excluded exactly through moment six; the sole B!=0 chart is a global unit modulo 101,103,107 through moment seven but still awaits characteristic-zero promotion. GVC3D10F gives exact finite-field quotient-saturation units through moment seven for all five pairwise-distinct degree-ten four-of-five profiles at 101,103,107, but explicitly does not promote them to characteristic zero. GVC3D10C exactly excludes every degree-ten four-channel direction-collision stratum: 52 new characteristic-zero unit bases, combined with the 13 radially equivalent degree-eight charts, close that entire boundary. GVC3D10F5S exactly excludes the exceptional a4-pivot boundary on the rational cross-ratio slice (lambda,mu)=(2,3) through moment six. GVC3D10F5G then closes the entire localized D=0 fibre of the generic nested a3 boundary over Q at moment five, including the exceptional normal branch; cutoff-four normal lengths 12 and 18 are already classified. The residual D!=0 generic boundary, main A*B!=0 chart and excluded pivot/projective faces remain open. GVC3HCB exactly closes the zero-even-part boundary of the genuine harmonic-cubic repair, leaving two terminal planes. GVC3HCM now closes the complementary nonzero-even-part chart exactly through moment eight, proving that the complete harmonic-cubic repair contains no Delta^3 witness. The next explicit coherent targets are exact promotion of the degree-eight and degree-ten pairwise-distinct charts and a projective stratification of the generic degree-ten five-channel pivot boundary and main chart; noncoherent vectors and repeated profiles remain broader targets. For every polynomial, or formal power series in s with polynomial coefficients, satisfying F|_(s=0)=P and Delta~(F)=0, the transverse equations force partial_s F|_(s=0)=-ct+R_0(a,b,c,d) and the next s-coefficient to be -(t/2)D(R_0)+S_0(a,b,c,d). The identities Lambda^m(P^m)=0 for every m>=1 hold if and only if a linear coordinate change over k admits a strict positive integral support gap g=min(w.supp(lambda))-max(w.supp(P))>0 with both weights at most d+R. If d>=r, the Hall direction is unique and descends to k; any k-frame with that first direction admits weights u>v>0. The Hall counting proof extends to d=r. At the first common threshold for d>r, the equal-face ordering forces a strict separator just to its right. A mediant of the exact feasible-slope endpoints bounds both integral weights by d+R. Hence every nonzero multiplier Q satisfies Lambda^m(Q*P^m)=0 for m>(d+R)*deg(Q), and a concrete certificate gives m>=floor(max(w.supp(Q))/g)+1. Over QQ, rational factorization of the lowest symbol, unique Hall-candidate testing, and finite strict inequalities decide the pure premise without a moment prefix; nonrational candidates are excluded by uniqueness and conjugacy. The family Lambda=dx+dy^(d+1), P=y^d, Q=x^q has last nonzero mixed power m=(d+1)q and attains its certificate cutoff; no optimality of the general d+R bound is claimed. Completeness depends on the existing written Hall/shifted-ray/envelope proofs. The exact checker independently verifies positive certificates and finite regressions, not the universal necessity theorem. No complete formal verification or external review is claimed.

GVC2OC.title: Optimal binary GVC mixed cutoff depending only on polynomial degree
GVC2OC.scope: For every characteristic-zero binary pair satisfying the all-powers pure-vanishing premise, with nonzero P of degree d, every multiplier Q satisfies Lambda^m(Q*P^m)=0 for m>C_d*deg(Q), where C_d=1+floor((d+1)^2/4), independently of the operator degree. This coefficient is optimal for each d>=0. The integer-support lemma proves that strict positive separation of an arbitrary operator support above a polynomial support of degree at most d admits a weight with max(weight)/gap<=C_d. Its proof maximizes the normalized concave envelope gap: polynomial breakpoints have denominator at most d, while operator breakpoints give 1/gap=1/A+B/N+BC/(AN)<=1+B+BC<=C_d with positive integers A,N and B+C<=d. Sharpness is attained by Lambda=dx^e+dy^(e*j+1), P=x^(e-1)*y^j, Q=x^q, with e+j=d+1 and e*j=floor((d+1)^2/4): the last nonzero mixed power is (e*j+1)*q. Both this bound and the earlier d+deg(Lambda) bound remain valid. The universal envelope lemma and the support-certificate necessity are written proofs; the checker verifies symbolic identities, 2475 small support pairs in both orientations, 18 sharp contractions, and high operator orders. No full formal verification, external review, or literature-priority claim.

GVC2UFT.title: Uniform binary Hall localization and low-channel Bernstein pivots
GVC2UFT.scope: Using the formal Hall-localization core GVC2HLC, let Lambda have lowest positive binary symbol of order r and let d=deg(P)>r. The translated split-symbol construction and Hall's theorem imply, uniformly in r and d, that every leading pure-zero component is localized at one root of multiplicity mu and has the form (X^mu Y^(r-mu), y^(d-mu+1) C_(mu-1)); after local division every normalized excess-h operator jet lies in the two wings a<mu or a>mu+h. If A and B are nonzero binary polynomials homogeneous for the same distinct positive weights and the same positive weighted degree, all pure contractions vanish only when their Newton segments are disjoint. A prime-dilated endpoint proof also gives the shifted-ray version, so every unequal-weight common-threshold face is terminal and any defect must mix at least two faces with positive limiting density. For generic translation, the balanced radial polytope is exactly N(lambda) intersect D(P); an empty intersection or a componentwise least point proves GVC, so the Hall/carry route could retain a candidate only at two incomparable Pareto-minimal points. Homogeneous binary factorial rigidity closes every one-channel ordinary-homogeneous tie. The exact minimal Bernstein beta circuit has moments (ac+bd)^m/(m+1); its pure-zero locus is a linear Hall annihilator, while Long's bad Laurent multiplier lies outside the polynomial-multiplier cone. The first genuine higher-jet circuit also closes uniformly. For primitive operator endpoints (r,0),(0,s) and four nonzero polynomial channels on an affine parallelogram, moments one and two determine the coefficient ratio and cross-ratio; moment three is (r!)^3 E_(r,s), where E_(r,s)=T_r-T_s+(9/2)(C_s-C_r)(C_r+C_s-2), C_n=binom(2n,n), and T_n=(3n)!/(n!)^3. Exact monotonicity proves E_(r,s) nonzero for r!=s, while r=s is homogeneous split-symbol terminal. More generally every primitive two-endpoint/four-polynomial-channel circuit is terminal: at moment two every additional quadratic return is a one-channel midpoint, an already-closed centered three-level circuit, or the parallelogram; if there is no return, the remaining obstruction is (r!)^2(C_r+C_s-4), nonzero except in the homogeneous linear case. Thus a convolution surviving those intermediate reductions requires at least five active polynomial channels or at least three active operator endpoints. Finite-prefix minor inheritance already fails exactly: A=X^2-(1/3)Y^3 and P=x^2+y^3+13/30+(11/2)x+xy^3 have scalar moments M_1=M_2=M_3=0 and M_4=1205760, while every four-channel restriction fails among the first three moments. The mixed unit-line half-bridge nevertheless closes in all even cusp orders: for A=X-Y^n/n! and P=x+y^n+c+d*y^(n/2)+e*x*y^(n/2), moments two and three determine u=de and v=c*e^2, while moment four is H_n/2 with H_n=2Q_n-40C_nT_n+48T_n+81C_n^3-180C_n^2+132C_n-48. Here H_2=-480, and H_n>0 for even n>=4 because Q_n/(C_nT_n)=binom(4n,n)/binom(2n,n) is increasing from 26 at n=4. In the reduced early-entry regime, primitive return combinatorics is uniformly finite: after symmetries there are exactly two double-quadratic and twelve quadratic-cubic types, explaining the 14 matrices in the exact census and excluding a new early-entry type at a higher cusp. A transverse-lattice calculation proves that every order-four return in those types is generated by the primitive quadratic and cubic rows, so no special primitive order-four branch exists. Coefficient elimination pairs the twelve quadratic-cubic types into six formulas and leaves two double-quadratic formulas: eight explicit obstructions in the factorial weights W_(m,k). Both double-quadratic determinants are uniformly nonzero. A 932-term coefficient-positive successor certificate proves H_(0,0)(r,s)>0 for every r!=s. Coupled-ratio coefficient-positive certificates prove H_(0,3)(r,s)<0 and D_(0,2)(r,s)<0 for every r!=s. Monotone ordered-tail cones, fixed endpoint rays, and exact finite complements prove H_(0,1), H_(0,2), and H_(1,1) uniformly nonzero. On the final wedge r>s>=4, the increasing factorial product L_n*M_n/C_n^3 supplies a nonlinear cone whose 408- and 1692-term coefficient-positive expansions prove H_(1,0) and D_(0,1) nonzero. Thus all eight factorial obstructions are uniformly closed. A late-entry transfer lemma gives the complementary termination mechanism: below the first balanced-return order tau of a new channel, every scalar moment equals the core moment; if the core has a nonzero witness at p or 2p for every prime p>=p_0, Bertrand's postulate forces tau<=4(p_0+1). The exact return cone has three-dimensional signed columns, so every extreme balanced circuit uses at most four operator/polynomial variables. Two incomparable circuits over two operator endpoints use at most six polynomial channels; equality is only two disjoint centered triples attached to opposite endpoints. A good-prime dilation separates repeated circuits of unequal ordinary radial degree. At that stage the route-local target was factorial-compatible exposure of a proper equal-profile circuit packet. GVC2FTS splits any packet already promoted to a scale-compatible finite trace, while GVC2WTD shows that affine carry shells can retain isoperiodic cancellation. The unproved promotion step is parked as GVC2ALL; GVC2ENV later bypasses it and proves unrestricted binary GVC.

lessons_before.title: Separate discovery, identity replay and proof scope
lessons_before.when: Any finite search, modular experiment or certificate promotion.
lessons_before.use: Freeze inputs and bounds; verify exact identities; state the mathematical implication and its hypotheses. Record independent replay, formal proof and external review separately.
lessons_before.avoid: Interpreting a completed box, matching hash, numerical residual or good-prime success as a theorem outside its scope.
lessons_before.boundary: Source hashes establish integrity. They do not establish mathematical correctness or independent implementation.
lessons_before.reopen_when: A new exact certificate closes the missing implication.

lessons_before.title: Saturate the intended geometric open before elimination
lessons_before.when: Collision ideals, Fitting modules, boundary components or resolved Riemann–Roch modules.
lessons_before.use: Identify the boundary and wrong-thickness factors, saturate by the required open, and retain a certificate of the resulting ideal or module.
lessons_before.avoid: Counting degenerate collision factors or imposing independent rows on conditions with resolution-graph syzygies.
lessons_before.boundary: Saturation changes the geometric locus. Every excluded factor and its interpretation must be explicit.
lessons_before.reopen_when: The proposed problem uses a different open or a genuinely new boundary stratum.

lessons_before.title: Audit the exact universe, not just totals
lessons_before.when: Finite support, orbit, chart or parameter censuses.
lessons_before.use: Reconstruct the ordered universe; require one record per key; compare explicit predecessor unions with the final complement. Keep a cheap coverage audit separate from elimination replay.
lessons_before.avoid: Using aggregate counts or the complement of the last batch to certify that all earlier cases were actually closed.
lessons_before.boundary: A complete finite census remains limited to its basis, degree, roster and equivalence relation.
lessons_before.reopen_when: The universe, equivalence relation or mathematical coverage argument changes.

lessons_before.title: Use the binary closure and finite cutoff
lessons_before.when: Starting another binary GVC promotion or low-degree search.

lessons_before.avoid: Reopening the prime-dependent Hall/carry promotion route as if unrestricted binary GVC were still open.
lessons_before.boundary: The Hall/carry subtheorems remain useful; their parked promotion statement is neither proved nor needed by the closure. Ternary minimum degree and efficient polarization are separate questions.
lessons_before.reopen_when: A task explicitly concerns the historical promotion statement or a hypothesis outside the binary theorem.

lessons_before.title: Distinguish pure-moment vanishing from SIC failure
lessons_before.when: A semistable point has a long or all-order zero pure-moment sequence.

lessons_before.boundary: The old Tschirnhaus/inertia obstructions retain their architecture and full-degree hypotheses. Non-atomic canonical polynomial-bundle existence is now constructed over all permitted schemes; a naturally trivial bundle, one fixed all-scheme map, atomicity, optimal dimensions and lower generic degree are distinct requirements. Modular low-rank and finite-base restrictions retain their stated scopes. These classifications use characteristic-zero polynomial retained-signal profiles and the named compiler. Any number of controls with rank-one cubic return is closed; non-descended higher-rank return and other compilers are separate. For another auxiliary block rank-one output recovery is equivalent to geometric generic-line connectedness; no general closedness conjecture is silently assumed. Arithmetic atomicity of connected input algebras is not absolute atomicity. Common kernels are proved for all constant ranks; the full selector classification is only one-directional. Higher-rank membership in C[Z,t] is an explicit hypothesis, not a determinant consequence. The full C is not assumed finitely generated or polynomial. Marked divisor identities hold universally; effective degree and absolute atomicity use the stated characteristic-zero field hypotheses. Fixed-signal rank-two source leaves need not be affine planes. A slice does not imply local nilpotence, and stable polynomiality is not an atomicity converse. The root-feedback theorem requires characteristic-zero fields, unchanged first signals and corrections in k[u,sigma,X]. Independent r_i diagonal variables force every principal minor to vanish. Frobenius dependencies and nilpotent coefficient cycles show why positive characteristic and nonreduced bases are excluded. Transitive product-fibre conclusions require transitivity on ALL nonidentity blocks; the trace filter has an extra auxiliary orbit and changes its first signal. Scalar self-feedback rigidity is a one-block affine coefficient-line theorem with a nonzero effective direction in characteristic zero. It permits all own-source channels and rational controls with whole polynomial landing, but says only that EFFECTIVE profiles are retained-signal polynomials; common direction factors may cancel a rational signal control. Curved coefficient families and mutually changing blocks remain outside. Finite-order parameter bases are nonreduced; the formal ring k[P][[lambda]] permits unbounded source degrees and differs from k[[lambda]][P]. The two-control module identity is universal over bases with2 invertible and preserves arbitrary source dependence. Affine-r rigidity and the stable signal-field normalizer use characteristic-zero fields. Affine-r rigidity is a one-block theorem with actual identity parameters and native source jets, not a theorem about mutually changing blocks. Formal-etale source gauges are classical and work over arbitrary nilpotent base ideals; their compatible formal limit can have unbounded source degree. The source-field normalizer leaves a vertical JC(m) problem and does not classify merely retained-output maps or arbitrary coordinate changes moving that field. Formal marked source equivalence permits actual polynomial families with arbitrary generic-degree jumps; it is not a global degree or stable-class invariant. Native orbit rigidity requires characteristic zero, one retained block, polynomial module membership and coordinate operations fixing identity parameters. Its stable equivalence is restricted to source maps normalizing k(u,sigma); unrestricted source changes are outside. A polynomial-r reduction survivor has non-dividing degrees >=2; negative Laurent sectors and genuine cross-block interaction remain open. The fixed dimension-three descent certificate excludes only the old cubic factor when its remainder is nonzero. Quasi-finite saturation is a classical elementary divisor consequence, not a novelty claim. The profile-factor theorem is one block with retained identities and a literal profile first factor; arbitrary source changes remain outside. Plane completion is generic in the signal and covers only nonnegative r powers. Plane indecomposability requires an irreducible Jacobian and an embedded line; its extension to all fields requires GEOMETRIC irreducibility. It does not imply stable whole-map atomicity. A nontrivial signal-retaining factor must have a genuine intermediate boundary pole. Whole-source special-signal landing and signal-moving factors remain open. The saturation overlap has explicit prior public attribution to Trushin Proposition3.1.1. The relative cancellation theorem leaves exactly TWO generic coordinates and requires a whole embedded A1 image; three-dimensional Keller counterexamples show that one curve alone does not invert a higher-dimensional target. It uses only the curve restriction, allowing poles elsewhere. Arbitrary identity stabilization and intermediate mixing are covered by the NON-PLANE generic intermediate-fibre obstruction. This is still a necessary all-factor condition, not full absolute stable atomicity. Intermediate surfaces satisfy BOTH saturation identities, geometrically have unit rank at most1 and their etale arrows miss at most finitely many points. Their abstract shape, smoothness and tangent triviality do not construct a proper factor. Primitive-unit surface rigidity requires characteristic zero, an AFFINE smooth target, cofinite etale image and the actual node. Its whole-factor unit theorem covers arbitrary last outputs with the fixed retained signal, without native jets or Laurent-degree bounds. Proper intermediates have CONSTANT geometric units; the earlier unit-rank-at-most-one route is now CLOSED on the nonconstant side. Whole constant-level irreducibility is not a statement about all further fibres after fixing E_u. Arithmetic UFD over k(u,a) does not prove geometric factoriality. The native NON-PLANE conclusion still requires the UARELPLANE1 embedded-curve witness. The one-way unit drop bounds no later unit-free chain length. CURRENT: a PROPER native intermediate is GEOMETRICALLY UNIT-FREE, has log kappa=-infinity, and has NONZERO geometric Picard group with ZERO retained-field Galois invariants, despite arithmetic UFD. The Picard factor criterion uses the native curve witness and explicitly imported Miyanishi negative-log affine-plane criterion. The log dichotomy and invariant-class vanishing cover every actual whole retained-signal Keller map. Higher-power Danielewski surfaces m>=2 pass exact volume; u has no Keller mate for all m>=1. Required arrows, free tangent frame, global polynomial lift and canonical marks/gluing remain unconstructed. The raw spread a=z^d-u^m*v is excluded globally by its critical zero fibre; only another smooth whole model could realize the same generic surface. CURRENT CHART GATE: the WHOLE carried A1 crosses the boundary of EVERY plane chart in a proper native factor, despite all finite/formal neighborhoods being standard. Any non-plane etale target containing an open A2 yields JC(2) counterexamples on all charts; this remains CONDITIONAL and has Dubouloz2009 precedent. Higher-power Danielewski targets need compatible nonautomorphic pairs surviving at nondividing ruling degrees>=2 and a carried closed embedding meeting two root components with deg Z>=m*N-r+1. Sharp beta-integral contact maps fail geometric injectivity for EVERY m>=2; other multi-root embedded curves remain open. These deductions retain the actual native/witness two-dimensional fibre and entire-curve hypotheses. CURRENT RULING/TOPOLOGY GATE: a retained-field ruling has base A1, integral arithmetic fibres and reduced geometric fibres, hence a finite geometric A2 atlas and a JC(2) burden for proper native targets. Geometric ruling existence does NOT prove descent. The whole carried curve hits two components of some split fibre. On an ACTUAL U^N times A^h leaf both proper arrows are NONFINITE and intermediate pi1 has an abelian subgroup with index DIVIDING source degree. This is virtually cyclic for one block. Multiple fibres of any surjective connected-generic geometric map to A1 are limited to one or two doubles; the two-double case requires EVEN source degree. No silent product hypothesis for the trace receiver or Euler-integral positivity is permitted. Published Galois-invariant/unique-ruling descent already closes that special descent uncertainty: a proper native factor with such a ruling would disprove JC(2). Conditional on JC(2), every geometric ruling must have a NONTRIVIAL Galois orbit of inequivalent rulings. CURRENT DESCENT RESULT: every geometric affine-type ruling of a proper native intermediate is unique and actually descends; its additive action descends too. Conditional on JC(2), only ADDITIVELY RIGID intermediates with COMPLETE-type Galois-permuted P1 rulings remain. Their descent is OPEN. A zero Picard orbit norm does not identify the individual fibrations.
lessons_before.reopen_when: An actual atomic canonical receiver has compatible complete fibres and effective gluing, or a sharper obstruction rules out its specified architecture; alternatively a smaller degree/dimension construction is proved. An actual candidate leaves the rank-one cubic architecture, for example through non-descended higher-rank return geometry, another compiler or a non-locally-nilpotent auxiliary with constants outside the stable-polynomial criterion, satisfies its whole-source determinant identity, retains the exact complete fibre and gluing, and proves absolute atomicity. In one constant direction, an auxiliary-only canonical escape must be all-inactive and demonstrate a full constant ring outside the stable-polynomial criterion, retaining exact marked fibre and descent. For root feedback, an atomic candidate must leave the all-signal-retaining polynomial root subring class, for example using additional source channels or a changed first output, and still prove the complete marked fibre and atomicity. A proved broader curved/multi-direction or genuine cross-block construction removes the explicit formal scalar denominator on the WHOLE source, retains complete marks and gluing, and proves full-map absolute atomicity. Scalar-line degree sweeps are closed. A two-effective-control native family leaves the scalar-line and affine-r sectors through nonlinear Laurent-r dependence, or another first-output/compiler/cross-block architecture, and proves whole-source polynomial landing, exact canonical marks, gluing and full-map atomicity. A native candidate has Cout genuinely nonlinear, escapes generic profile-coordinate reduction at a non-dividing polynomial-r degree pair or in a negative Laurent sector, and proves the full marked scheme, effective gluing and absence of ALL actual polynomial factors; another compiler or changed first-output architecture remains permitted. A whole-source native construction has genuinely nonlinear Cout and exact canonical marks/gluing; any claimed factor must escape literal profile recovery and, in the polynomial-r sector, polynomial intermediate extension. A genuinely non-plane generic intermediate surface with the exact saturated field model and whole-source realization, a new curve-witness failure or another compiler must be analyzed without assuming JC(2). A proper factor realizes a NON-PLANE geometric generic retained fibre, both field degrees exceed one, and all curve, unit, saturation, divisor and whole-polynomial requirements are certified; or an actual native integration preserves complete canonical marks/gluing and excludes every such factor. A proper generic surface is geometrically unit-free with the exact arithmetic factorial ring, saturated embedded field, whole carried curve and an all-irreducible-constant-fibre intermediate signal; both whole degrees exceed one and the entire map/global marked gluing is certified. Nonconstant-unit and finite-index unit candidates are closed. Produce an actual negative-log unit-free geometrically nonfactorial intermediate with nonzero Picard group and no invariant class, the exact canonical volume and both etale arrows. The u^m*v=z^d-a families with m>=2 are explicit necessary-condition models, not permission for a bounded coefficient sweep or proof of a whole factor. Supply an actual compatible nonautomorphic Keller atlas and a WHOLE multi-root embedded line satisfying all contacts, both cofinite arrows and a different smooth whole spread, or move to a proved intermediate geometry without such a plane chart. Finite/formal neighborhoods and exact primitives alone are insufficient; JC(2) and canonical atomicity are not declared solved. Prove a compatible JC(2)-counterexample atlas in the descended-ruling class, or prove an actual failure of ruling descent retaining all field, curve, volume and whole-source constraints. Respect the nonfinite source-divisor and sheet-loss budget, the dividing-index group constraint and the orbifold multiplicity/parity gates. Full canonical marks, gluing and absolute stable atomicity remain necessary. Prove descent or exclude actual realization of the remaining COMPLETE-type Galois orbit. The affine-type descent subproblem is closed; extend by a new identification argument, not more necessary conditions.

lessons_before.title: Prove polynomiality and the determinant balance together
lessons_before.when: Constructing a boundary-cancelled or weighted suspension.
lessons_before.use: Use an explicit source–core–target valuation ledger, record divisibility at each boundary and verify the complete determinant product.
lessons_before.avoid: Treating formal pole cancellation or a rational coordinate identity as proof of a polynomial Keller map.
lessons_before.boundary: The chosen reconstruction open and divisor multiplicities are part of the construction. A relative or marked invariant is not automatically an unrestricted stable invariant.
lessons_before.reopen_when: A different ansatz supplies its own polynomiality and boundary-exhaustion certificates.

lessons_before.title: Exploit branch-value interpolation before nonlinear elimination
lessons_before.when: An RR pencil has rational double-branch values on known fibres.
lessons_before.use: Interpolate the branch line, divide by the product of the branch parameters and inspect forced denominator squares and recurrence structure.
lessons_before.avoid: Starting a generic Groebner or full coefficient solve before checking whether the marked data determine a linear interpolation problem.
lessons_before.boundary: The interpolated candidate still needs literal equation, marking, denominator and section checks; interpolation alone does not certify the endpoint.
lessons_before.reopen_when: The rational branch-value assumptions hold on the selected physical chart.

lessons_before.title: Record the degree of every quartic point map
lessons_before.when: Transporting sections through a binary-quartic Jacobian or covariant map.
lessons_before.use: Annotate the map degree and compare exact group-law images and heights before claiming a new section or saturation index.
lessons_before.avoid: Missing that a covariant transported 2P rather than P, thereby multiplying heights by four and creating a false rank/glue interpretation.
lessons_before.boundary: A rational point map and an isomorphism of pointed elliptic models are different certificate types.
lessons_before.reopen_when: The map degree, chosen origin and exact section identity are all established.

lessons_before.title: Optimize the measured dominant phase
lessons_before.when: Proposing a runtime improvement or comparing two research runners.
lessons_before.use: Separate worker startup, map construction, landscape/CVP, admission, point search and replay. Use retained ordered receipts and compare like inputs and verification work.
lessons_before.avoid: Reporting a component speedup as a whole-run improvement, or calling inherited landscape verification equivalent work to rebuilding it.
lessons_before.boundary: In the seven recorded future-V3 searches, point work accounts for roughly84–88% of wall time; eliminating all other work only yields the stated roughly1.14–1.18x ceiling with point time fixed. Curve52's bounded100-invocation pass took110.055 seconds while its independent full-landscape replay took117.552 seconds, so a shorter search is not necessarily cheaper to verify. These observations are not forecasts for other runs.
lessons_before.reopen_when: A new profile identifies a different bottleneck or a controlled comparison measures a changed component.

lessons_before.title: Separate coordinate cost from point-yield selection
lessons_before.when: Using a coordinate change, model size, or measured chart cost to choose a bounded fibre population.
lessons_before.use: Freeze deduplicated candidate populations, selection rules and cost measurements before point outcomes. Measure preparation, chart construction and worker cost separately from certified directions, and preserve the exact maps and isomorphism checks for every selected fibre.
lessons_before.avoid: Treating smaller coefficients as a rank or point-yield predictor, comparing only one component of runtime, or treating all-zero matched arms as equivalence or grounds to enlarge the same population.
lessons_before.boundary: The fibre-height experiment completed 468 charts on 31 distinct curves. Its smaller models had lower recorded cost but both arms found zero new directions. That is a bounded null result for these selection rules, not a theorem about other coordinates, families, or rank.
lessons_before.reopen_when: A separately frozen panel supplies compatible positive controls, a changed cost boundary, or a predeclared point-yield endpoint.

lessons_before.title: Keep beam truncation separate from certified CRT pruning
lessons_before.when: Using height-ranked CRT prefixes to retain candidate branches.
lessons_before.use: Record every omitted branch and use exact branch-specific lower bounds only where proved. Preserve the four-prime ordering counterexample as a regression.
lessons_before.avoid: Treating survival in a finite beam as an exhaustive sieve or assuming the ordering of branches cannot change.
lessons_before.boundary: A width-one beam ends at height1409 after discarding a branch completing at53. Minimum height is nondecreasing on a fixed branch; that does not preserve the ordering between branches.
lessons_before.reopen_when: The omitted branches have an independent exact obstruction or the task explicitly accepts a bounded beam.

lessons_before.title: Reduce fixed constructed covers and compare blind lifting against generic-only V3
lessons_before.when: Explicit extra Kummer/Selmer classes have fixed genus-one covers but their known rational lifts used a point oracle.
lessons_before.use: Freeze the classes, give a fresh-context worker only equations, retain all rational transformations, apply established degree4 minimisation/reduction, and exploit a ternary conic to pass to a reduced degree2 model. Independently check the complete coefficient and point transport and finite independence. Compare ordinary V3 from the same generic subgroup, with upstream construction, maps, search and replay costs stated separately.
lessons_before.avoid: Treating huge expanded coefficients or a degree4 height-box miss as a final search model or obstruction; treating a known-fibre blind recovery as a parameter-selection mechanism; calling the cover-only runtime the end-to-end class-route cost.
lessons_before.boundary: On MW16-05 at3/17, fixed columns6/7 reduce from2464/1766 to39/44 coefficient bits. Degree4 bounds1000/100000 miss, but conic-to-quartic reduction yields points at1/2 and3/10 at bound1000, independently certifying generic16 plus2. Fresh V3 reaches22 in6 charts and also supplies both exact fixed-class lifts. These are fixed-control results, not a general speed or parameter criterion.
lessons_before.reopen_when: An equation-derived parameter condition forces the arithmetic block, or a preregistered multi-fibre experiment accounts for class construction and recovery on common backend resources.

lessons_before.title: Measure point visibility with a blinded known-direction control
lessons_before.when: Testing whether a bounded chart policy can expose rational directions without claiming a new rank result.
lessons_before.use: Freeze the curve panel, generic basis, reduced metric, centre list, budgets and worker inputs. Withhold one known generic direction before selection and search; keep its coordinates in a separate oracle. Open that oracle only after every attempt and geometry replay finishes. Count recovery only from an exact rational group relation having a nonzero withheld coefficient.
lessons_before.avoid: Letting a withheld point, rank label, exceptional-point outcome or a later relation alter selection; calling a literal representative miss a missing direction; or reporting recovered known directions as new rank.
lessons_before.boundary: The retained ordinary-fibre control recovered all 31 withheld known directions in 372 completed charts, while the unmasked endpoint had zero new quotient gains. This establishes bounded sensitivity under that frozen geometry and exposure only; it does not measure exceptional-point incidence, establish exact rank or validate a selector on an all-new population.
lessons_before.reopen_when: A new, preregistered curve panel or a changed independent subgroup has a separate blind/oracle binding, exact relation audit and declared endpoint.

lessons_before.title: Certify a point-supplied generic section from the actual base curve
lessons_before.when: Using a fixed multi-cover base change to supply an additional generic section.
lessons_before.use: Write the actual connected base curve, not merely a quotient, and exhibit its rational point. Use good-reduction orders to obtain a torsion annihilator and verify a nonzero annihilator multiple. Then verify the lifted sections and their exact height Gram matrix; a positive Schur complement certifies the added generic direction.
lessons_before.avoid: Treating a point on a quotient as a point on the full base curve, treating a large Selmer space as a rational lift, or claiming a base generator, saturation, specialized independence or a rank upper bound without the corresponding certificate.
lessons_before.boundary: The retained V4 diagnostic has a degree-four genus-one base with a non-torsion point and a rank-19 displayed generic subgroup after base change. Its sampled fibres verify supplied points only; it is neither a specialized rank certificate nor a record-search advantage claim.
lessons_before.reopen_when: The cover equations, base point, inherited subgroup or exact height pairing changes.

lessons_before.title: Turn a target-conditioned height lattice into an explicit K3 parent
lessons_before.when: A certified point configuration suggests a generic core but its explicit parent surface is missing.
lessons_before.use: Recognize the candidate height form, choose a low-degree polarization and solve the line-incidence kernel. Verify both incidences and nonincidences, compile the residual cubic pencil with a rational origin, then measure section rank before proving heights, saturation and the Picard upper bound.
lessons_before.avoid: Counting displayed sections as independent; treating a matching lattice or equal j-invariant as a literal specialization; repeating the completed Curve302 reconstruction.
lessons_before.boundary: For Curve302, removing the unique norm-six outlier leaves 400 words for the determinant1092 form. The degree-four O+P+Q polarization supplies fifteen lines; the first seventeen displayed sections have rank fifteen, and two further conics complete rank seventeen. This is inverse construction conditioned on known exceptional points, not a prospective parameter selector.
lessons_before.reopen_when: A different target has a certified candidate generic core, a realizable low-degree polarization and an unmet geometric construction gate.

lessons_before.title: Reuse weight modules and prove quotient closure
lessons_before.when: Exact image membership for the two-slice derivation D=u*partial_x+v*partial_y.
lessons_before.use: Group expressions by target weight, compute one standard basis of the primitive module per group, then lift each query and verify D(primitive)=expression. Reuse those primitives across ideals. Build the quotient image of ker(D) by closure under u, v and w; require the frontier to become empty.
lessons_before.avoid: Rebuilding the same module for each seed or treating a finite iteration cap or arbitrary y-degree truncation as kernel-image closure.
lessons_before.boundary: A membership answer is exact only after the primitive and kernel correction tests succeed. Pure/mixed exponent windows remain bounded experiments. The 128-step guard fails if closure does not stabilize; it is not a completeness bound.
lessons_before.reopen_when: The derivation, coefficient ring, ideal or target-weight module changes; otherwise reuse the existing compiler and declared inputs.

lessons_before.title: Apply the principal and plinth-power theorems before searching
lessons_before.when: Choosing an ideal for the rank-two model LND or reusing its old conductor search queue.
lessons_before.use: First test whether the ideal contains a power of (u,v), or is nonzero principal. The plinth-power theorem LND-NPF and complete principal theorem LND-CPM give all-order safety. The five historical nonprincipal charts all contain (u,v)^3.
lessons_before.avoid: Expanding old NPL/PDP/PCD power windows or treating the rational-root ladder as the current end of the principal classification.
lessons_before.boundary: These theorems concern the stated rank-two derivation and ideal classes. Genuinely nonprincipal ideals outside plinth-power saturation, and different derivations, retain their own obligations.
lessons_before.reopen_when: An explicitly specified ideal lies outside both completed classes, with an all-order theorem or counterexample target.

lessons_before.title: Use the lowest valuation face in conductor arguments
lessons_before.when: Clearing Laurent denominators in the invariant-affine principal LND families.
lessons_before.use: Pass to the associated graded ring for the relevant prime valuation. The lowest negative face carries the required power of the carrier. Apply pure vanishing at growing moment orders to force positive valuation, which eventually clears every fixed multiplier denominator.
lessons_before.avoid: Claiming carrier divisibility for every negative Laurent coefficient: u^2*y^3 contains the coefficient w^3/u in the rational-root chart, which is not divisible by q1-w.
lessons_before.boundary: Theorems 6.8–6.16 use lowest faces and explicitly controlled denominator losses in the model LND. The stronger coefficientwise statement is false and cannot be used as a shortcut.
lessons_before.reopen_when: A new carrier has a proved associated-graded divisibility statement and a compatible denominator bound.

lessons_before.title: Keep pointwise equations after cohomological compression
lessons_before.when: Reducing the cubic or higher Danielewski contraction equations.
lessons_before.use: Compile the small de Rham flux ledger and leading pencil first, then retain the lowest nonzero coefficients of J-1 for each degree and boundary-pole profile. Use the explicit normalized cubic family in CL25 as a regression against any claim that flux plus leading face is sufficient.
lessons_before.avoid: Launching the unstructured 90-variable cubic ideal, replacing J=1 by its cohomology class, using opposite signs for P'(i) and P'(-i), or quotienting by automorphisms that do not preserve the chosen degree filtration.
lessons_before.boundary: The 11 nonconstant flux equations are necessary. The exhibited family satisfies them all but fails J=1; both boundary derivatives equal -2. A degree-bounded quotient needs filtration-preserving transformations.
lessons_before.reopen_when: A complete chart classification adds the missing pointwise conditions or proves a degree-preserving normal form.

lessons_before.title: Reuse the finite Rees atlas and finish the surface ledger
lessons_before.when: Continuing the quartic weighted graph normalization or Hilbert-polynomial calculation.
lessons_before.use: Start from the three completed side point bases, eight-cone corner atlas and exact side-to-corner packet matches. The next finite calculation records divisor classes, Rees multiplicities, polarization restrictions and normal-bundle degrees of the center curves; apply centerwise Riemann–Roch and the existing endpoint conductor corrections before one global pushout.
lessons_before.avoid: Repeating ambient normalI runs that produced no certificate, redoing the completed local principalizations, or equating matching conductor colengths with equality of quotient sheaves.
lessons_before.boundary: The modular graph multidegree and two unknown coefficients alpha/beta remain a calibration. Local normalization and a finite-model Euler-characteristic formula do not prove global normalization, flatness or equinormalization.
lessons_before.reopen_when: The actual missing surface-intersection or gluing data are supplied, or a changed model invalidates the existing atlas.

lessons_before.title: Restrict later local rows to the existing kernel
lessons_before.when: A large RR ambient has a smooth block with a small exact modular kernel.
lessons_before.use: Match ambient labels and hashes, then restrict actual sparse component rows to the small kernel. Check every rational denominator at the chosen prime and bind the independent smooth-block rank/kernel certificate. Full stacked column rank mod p then certifies the same bounded rank over QQ.
lessons_before.avoid: Rebuilding a dense stacked matrix, computing node layers after the kernel is already zero, or using a smooth-kernel record from a different pole bound.
lessons_before.boundary: A surviving modular direction is not a rational pencil. A full-rank minor rejects only the supplied ambient; it gives no exhaustive pole bound. The good-reduction consumer trusts the independently recorded smooth rank/kernel and does not reconstruct that matrix.
lessons_before.reopen_when: A different, mathematically justified ambient has a compatible smooth-kernel certificate.

lessons_before.title: Keep product divisibility distinct from a rectangular jet
lessons_before.when: A resolved normal-crossing chart reduces a global pole condition to Z^a*Y^b divisibility.
lessons_before.use: Identify the actual principal ideal before forming a quotient. Impose compatible componentwise divisibility and overlap gluing before extracting any finite residual corner. In the recorded node t^17=Z^51*Y^68 times a unit.
lessons_before.avoid: Replacing the one-dimensional quotient R/(Z^51*Y^68) with the finite length-3468 quotient R/(Z^51,Y^68), or expanding a raw ten-generator ninth-power ideal before clearing chart units.
lessons_before.boundary: A rectangle and a product impose different conditions. Pareto-leading rows are necessary conditions; equal-leading terms and unit expansions can still interact.
lessons_before.reopen_when: An exact component/gluing argument identifies a finite residual quotient without changing the ideal.

lessons_before.title: Bind replay schemas to the exact marked section
lessons_before.when: An old module or physical-target script is reused after a section-normalization correction.
lessons_before.use: Use the primitive height-24, degree-ten q8 section and the full R*h*Dy=Ny*Dx normalization. The corrected marking wrapper dispatches the 2cover implementation. The corrected QQ checker reconstructs the section from q6 points and consumes the frozen tracked component-nef target.
lessons_before.avoid: Renaming the new marking JSON to the old filename, accepting its new status in old consumers, or applying the historical degree-192 branch result to a different chord input.
lessons_before.boundary: The old consumers require the withdrawn NS-decomposition schema; the finite-module script asserts collision degree 46. Missing q6 Jacobian/zero/E7-section inputs are a recovery gap, not permission to rebuild a campaign or evidence that q8 remains unsolved.
lessons_before.reopen_when: The original inputs are recovered with matching hashes, or a separately verified schema/marking transport is supplied.

lessons_before.title: Use factor supports to avoid all pair products
lessons_before.when: A complete finite set of rational quadratic covers is tested for q_i*q_j=q_k.
lessons_before.use: First test rational quadratics by primitive integer coefficients and nonsquare discriminant. Distinct irreducible polynomial atoms rule out every nonempty product of distinct listed characters, regardless of rational scalar factors; the compact independent packet verifies all 39,147 alternate11952 and 39,120 hidden103b2 rows. For repeated or two-linear-factor supports, use endpoint/triangle support XORs and retain the full scalar: a rational ratio or product is a square exactly when its sign is positive and its reduced numerator and denominator are integer squares. This needs no integer factorization.
lessons_before.avoid: Forming hundreds of millions of polynomial pair products, treating repeated polynomial support as an equal extension without a scalar-square test, silently dropping a nonconstant branch denominator, or treating a formal variable rename as transport between two bases.
lessons_before.boundary: The compact replay verifies branch polynomials and attachment to retained priority words. Completeness of the lattice enumeration, section-lift identities and source-curve base degrees are separate proof components. The old rank-28 and q_103b2 curves have degrees 8 and 9 over alternate11952, so they are not quadratic characters there. The ten-chart smooth layer and rational-normalization genus-one row were also closed later; use their canonical boundaries before another search.
lessons_before.reopen_when: A new source has actual repeated/two-factor supports or certified new degree-two characters on the same base.

lessons_before.title: Stream the short shell and retain the quotient
lessons_before.when: The short-vector list is too large although the finite quotient and one representative per orbit are small.
lessons_before.use: Use a unimodular LLL basis with an explicit row-coordinate transport, stream Fincke-Pohst leaves, and retain parity masks, multiplicities and canonical representatives. Evaluate every accepted norm exactly and require equality with an independent exact PARI count before asserting completeness. Export representatives in the pinned frame.
lessons_before.avoid: Materializing nearly three million signed vectors just to recover 39,147 M/2M classes, or confusing LLL column transforms with row-vector coordinates.
lessons_before.boundary: Floating pruning and a generous guard are not themselves a completeness proof; exact leaf membership, uniqueness of coordinate visits and the matching exact count are essential. Lattice coverage still does not construct branch equations.
lessons_before.reopen_when: The lattice, norm bound or equivalence relation actually changes; the existing complete frame tables should be reused otherwise.

lessons_before.title: Use the disjoint graph only for equation cost
lessons_before.when: Selecting two bisections for a rank-19 biquadratic construction.
lessons_before.use: Use XOR with norm-four masks to identify all disjoint representatives when that lowers equation cost. Test Galois-character independence by the exact quadratic squareclasses and then use the appropriate lifted height theorem.
lessons_before.avoid: Using membership in the 8,895,801-pair disjoint graph as a hard filter for independent characters, or restarting its common-cover scan after complete bisection injectivity.
lessons_before.boundary: All common-cover pairs in the published smooth-bisection frame are excluded. Distinct-character biquadratic rank 19 is a separate construction; both the published pair and the recorded low-complexity pair lie outside the disjoint graph.
lessons_before.reopen_when: A different geometric objective specifically requires disjoint representatives, or genuinely new quadratic characters are supplied.

lessons_before.title: Close a failed incidence bank before enlarging a speculative carrier hypothesis
lessons_before.when: Trying to propagate a frozen exceptional Kummer block into an infinite rank-gain subfamily.
lessons_before.use: Keep the integral frame, physical zero and I2 component; enumerate signed norm 10/14 vectors with exact LDL arithmetic and label a stopped prefix incomplete. Realize actual curves through the marked trace Riemann--Roch identity and A1 vanishing. Require nonzero rational control splitting, exact cubic-field labels, a normalized fixed-line fibre product, and certified rational infinitude. Count extensions over the fixed t-line with constant squareclasses retained. Translation identifies normalized covers and pairing cannot supply a missing lift. Close a stopped bank before returning to the successful dependency.
lessons_before.avoid: Do not substitute the rank-16 height matrix for the rank-17 frame; call a lattice vector a curve; identify constant twists or arbitrary base changes; equate a genus-one point with infinitude; or choose generic corrections independently. Soluble strict classes and formula counts do not give rational bisections or independent arithmetic directions. A failure before label matching says nothing about the marked block.
lessons_before.boundary: The stopped MW16-05 prefix has 182 exact genus-zero bisections with 182 distinct extensions, all nonsplit at 3/17. Their control values are 182 rational squareclasses, without an independence claim. There is no common obstruction at the real place or primes through 1009; 21 fail by sign. Both shells remain incomplete, with 73 split residuals and candidate 171 separate. Translation and pairing cannot repair these incidence misses. No marked rank-18 family or strict/ideal transfer is constructed; the conditional theorem remains valid.
lessons_before.reopen_when: Only a new theoretical connection from the actual arithmetic dependency to a different carrier hypothesis would justify a separately scoped proposal. This bank is closed; no shell completion, enlargement or interrupted-candidate repair is scheduled.

lessons_before.title: Cancel the Jacobian of the actual source chart
lessons_before.when: A primitive-polynomial derivative is used to design a mask suspension.
lessons_before.use: Compute the chart Jacobian first. In the A4 root algebra, interpolate H^3/(4K^3L) in the four conjugate roots and factor its denominator B^2*rho*sigma. Carry the selected field generator and exact residual divisor through every change of chart.
lessons_before.avoid: Substituting 1/P'(T) for the required chart reciprocal: the derivative split preserves the four-sheet field but leaves H^6/(2*Theta*K^6*L^3) in the ordinary chart. Do not confuse coefficient gcd in a nonnormal presentation with divisorial cancellation on its normalization.
lessons_before.boundary: The localized fourfold determinant-one map still has genuine poles. Its existence does not supply a polynomial affine source; the original masks and Hhat continuation are already closed. KMFI66, via KIG28, separately closes every A4-preserving affine-space Keller construction; any unresolved selector or chart classification here is local geometry only. Wright boundary A4 states are not identified with full geometric generic monodromy.
lessons_before.reopen_when: For local geometry under a separately stated objective: A different chart or coupled source/target construction has a new exact divisor ledger and a field-recovery argument. The affine-space Keller objective requires a substantive failure of KMFI66 or changed hypotheses; a new chart, mask or divisor ledger within its hypotheses cannot reopen it.

The lattice rejection is stable under polynomial extension; the separate surface-boundary genus proof is not automatically a universal stable-cancellation theorem. KMFI66, via KIG28, separately closes every A4-preserving affine-space Keller construction; any unresolved selector or chart classification here is local geometry only. KMFI66, via KIG28, separately closes every A4-preserving affine-space Keller construction; any unresolved selector or chart classification here is local geometry only. lessons_before.title: Use independent affine-source rejection gates

The smooth rho=h model has class L^3 yet class group Z/2. Exact invariant failures can reject a candidate before a large mixed-incidence solve.

lessons_before.title: Reject CAS interpreter errors even after a success marker
lessons_before.when: A Singular subprocess is used to certify identities, factor lists or a finite census.

The many-channel RESULT adapter keeps historical program hashes and timeout records, but discards stdout on interpreter failure so downstream parsers cannot retain an apparent unit or rank.
lessons_before.avoid: Trusting returncode==0, subprocess check=True, a later PASS substring, or absence of a reported factor. An intentional ERROR followed by PASS exits zero on the locally inspected Singular 4.3.2.
lessons_before.boundary: The base guard has six small protocol tests and earlier tiny real interpreter controls. The RESULT adapter has four additional tests plus mocked many-channel/tagged integration; no GVC moment, elimination or census was replayed. The 19 many-channel substitutions preserve the AST of all mathematics, generated programs and timeouts. Historical outputs are not fresh guarded executions, and other CAS wrappers remain outside this audit.
lessons_before.reopen_when: A new interpreter version or output protocol changes diagnostic/completion behavior; cover that behavior with a tiny test before authorizing any research replay.

lessons_before.title: Calibrate local signatures against known quotient directions
lessons_before.when: A local Kummer signature rank is proposed as an exceptional-rank or Selmer predictor.
lessons_before.use: Use the rank-28 control: the generic seventeen and all twenty-eight points both have signature rank 15 in 53 coordinates, despite eleven globally independent quotient directions. At odd p compare known-image rank with v2(c_p*#E_ns(F_p)); equality certifies full local coverage. Keep the p=2 formal group separate.
lessons_before.avoid: Reading zero incremental local rank as zero global quotient gain, treating a smooth local point as everywhere-local solubility, or treating capped and timed-out lifts as obstructions.
lessons_before.boundary: Four odd places and infinity are covered; seven odd places and p=2 remain unresolved. The pilot has 60 witnesses and 24 inconclusive tests. Exact public point covers supply residual lower bound 11, but no ambient Selmer upper bound.
lessons_before.reopen_when: A complete ambient squareclass construction and all local conditions are available, or a different signature is tested against these positive controls.

lessons_before.title: Record whether visibility predicts or fits a known point
lessons_before.when: Comparing a multisection atlas against known high-rank fibres.
lessons_before.use: Freeze the atlas and cost order before targets; record genus, degree, family dimension and incidence codimension. The rigid rational-bisection span ranks are 5,3,2,1, but individually named degree-two generators number 4,0,0,0. All 38 displayed generators admit a genus-one degree-two member fitted after seeing the point, using the common norm-eight trace -P2-P5.
lessons_before.avoid: Calling a post-hoc moving-pencil interpolation predictive, equating span rank with the number of exposed named generators, or constructing millions of rational trisection equations just to fit already known points.
lessons_before.boundary: Only degree-two rational curves and the 320 deep norm-26 trisection classes are complete. The norm-20 and degree-four equation sets are samples, and degrees five/six were stopped, not excluded. The quotient is the displayed L_t/M_t, not a saturated full Mordell-Weil group.
lessons_before.reopen_when: A predeclared pencil gives a genuinely new target, or a target-directed rational multisection solves one of the remaining named-generator obligations.

lessons_before.title: Eliminate first and retain every good-reduction hypothesis
lessons_before.when: Seeking a two-node genus-two bisection with rational quadratic normalization.
lessons_before.use: Use the finite-pole chord M=M0+(l0+l1*u)h^2. In q=(u^2+a*u+b)^2*(c2*u^2+c1*u+c0), eliminate the three c coefficients from the top terms before solving the four essential variables. Intersect full quadratic squareclasses, including scalar characters, at distinct primes. Reconstruct coordinatewise only with compatible trace bases, then factor over QQ and check both section identities.
lessons_before.avoid: Dropping the scalar squareclass, trusting incompatible chart labels, promoting an empty affine multi-prime intersection to a global theorem, or treating standard CRT reconstruction as an unlimited rational-height search.
lessons_before.boundary: The recorded primes 17,23,29,31,37 and modulus 13005833 give no accepted candidates in the reconstructed boxes. Infinity, simultaneous bad reduction and larger heights remain open. The separate complete singular genus-one row gives first possible arithmetic genus at least two, not equality.

lessons_before.title: Reuse exact local lift failures and retain singular branches

Full-rank extra branches admit digit-by-digit exact lift tests. Reuse the 2423 recorded nonlifting certificates and the known-section depth-512 reconstruction control before another shell.

The retained-record auditor checks source/data integrity and coverage without rerunning arithmetic; its per-run digest cache invalidates on file changes.

lessons_before.title: Check the exact source image before tangent calculations

lessons_before.title: Separate carrier strata before number-field specialization

lessons_before.title: Preserve factorial contractions when compressing exponent lattices
lessons_before.when: Monomial compression or weighted channel matching is proposed as an all-order GVC transfer.
lessons_before.use: Prove both operator-versus-polynomial degree inequalities before replacing a contraction by matched channel counts. The cubic tagged lift forces equality and yields the explicit binomial/factorial channel sum. The weighted quartic plane instead admits unequal selections of equal weight; use its full moment equations. Keep the odd-only prime decomposition as a regression face when restoring even endpoints.

lessons_before.title: Choose elimination pivots by downstream expansion cost
lessons_before.when: A multi-channel moment system has several linear pivots or a fixed rational direction slice.
lessons_before.use: Reuse the recorded term counts before compiling another system. For the nested degree-ten boundary, the a3 pivot gives 648/7340/15300 terms versus 958/6173/34782 for a2, so the slightly larger middle equation buys a much smaller next one. On a fixed rational cross-ratio slice compile with the numeric Gram matrix before expansion.

lessons_before.title: Factor and rechart localization before retrying a large saturation

At cutoff four use the recorded residual-intersection minors and solved linear D restriction to identify where growth and thickness occur.

lessons_before.use: On the degree-ten nested chart, solve D=C*a0+R with C invertible and use cleared restrictions. Cutoff-four normal lengths 12 and 18 are already classified. At moment five the second restriction is a unit times e^20 and the third is a unit modulo e, where e=lam-mu. A finite geometric-series inverse closes the entire D=0 fibre, including the exceptional branch.

lessons_before.title: Compute all source-degree cutoffs with one incremental echelon
lessons_before.when: The same tangent space is tested at many degree cutoffs for its unique source trivializer.
lessons_before.use: Construct the tangent basis and coefficient rows of adj(DF)G once, group the rows by source degree, then insert them in descending degree order. Rank above each cutoff gives the whole filtered profile without solving a new tangent system. Reuse the retained p=32003 profiles and CSK1 exact rational seed degrees.

lessons_before.reopen_when: A characteristic-zero full-profile certificate, a new coefficient box or a precisely defined two-sided filtration is in scope.

lessons_before.title: Keep lower-order kernel choices in higher deformation obstructions
lessons_before.when: A greedy formal lift fails, or quadratic and cubic homogeneous layers are passed to a component calculation.
lessons_before.use: Retain the lower-order free kernel parameters when formulating the next obstruction. Use the known seed family as a positive control. The quartic generic compiler already records 22 normal quadrics and 305 cubic equations; its 327-generator homogeneous-layer input is retained, together with the failed primary-decomposition attempt.

lessons_before.title: Read terminal stopping reasons before treating unused adaptive capacity as work

lessons_before.use: Use the existing terminal reporter on retained checkpoints. The record-scale cohort completed all48 curves at2352 certified boxes with zero gains; every initial no-gain wave stopped its curve. The32/8/8 score strata are fully reported. Bind roster, wave proofs, stopping reasons and completed exposure before interpreting a comparison.

lessons_before.title: Preserve frozen assignments while separating changed coordinate measurements
lessons_before.when: A historical protocol source hash differs after an explicit backend amendment.
lessons_before.use: Audit population, assignment, context and budgets unchanged; permit only declared source replacements whose historical bytes match the pinned revision. Keep raw and amended-runtime checkpoints separate. The rescue audit verifies the2239 assignments and historical66 clean zeros without Sage, while reporting current readiness as NOT_CERTIFIED. Preserve the exact301-class rescue set and its separate specialized reranking. The CRT half-lattice worker likewise writes a separate pointed-runtime ledger; its frozen v3 analyzer still requires the original v3 ledger.

lessons_before.title: Normalize each local divisor before discarding a prime
lessons_before.when: An RR fake-Kummer panel rejects a place because one evaluation is nonunit or its basepoint has negative valuation.
lessons_before.use: Normalize the sextic and each divisor separately by rational prime powers. Omit only nonunit divisors; for negative basepoint valuation use the scalar-equivalent anchor1-T/T0. This recovered152 previously skipped pairs without new primes or points. At certified good reduction, compare the attained rank with the complete local dimension and independently check the fake kernel.
lessons_before.avoid: Requiring every inherited generator to be a unit, discarding a whole prime unnecessarily, or calling failure of this model reduction test intrinsic bad reduction.
lessons_before.boundary: The frozen panel closes553/640 pairs. The83 failed reduction tests and four anchor cases remain unresolved. Rational-scalar normalization is justified in the stated fake squareclass quotient; its true-image conclusion also uses the proved kernel statement.
lessons_before.reopen_when: An unresolved anchor or reduction case has a certified alternative local model, with the same class maps and completeness checks.

lessons_before.title: Reuse complete local images without collapsing the remaining global problem
lessons_before.when: A proposed RR incidence detector asks for classes outside the inherited image at an already certified place.
lessons_before.use: Reuse the553 complete good-prime images and all ten real and2-adic images: the inherited subgroup spans each. Preserve true/fake kernel data. A global comparison still needs simultaneous compatibility in a complete supported squareclass space, including unramified class contributions; the inherited combination can differ from place to place.
lessons_before.avoid: Searching for an outside-inherited class at a place already proved fully spanned, identifying local proxies with the original global fields, or replacing global completeness with trial-prime support or known rational classes. Do not identify this inherited-subgroup membership obstruction with a Sha obstruction, or treat failed feature transfer as proof that cohomology explains amplification.
lessons_before.boundary: The known rational Kummer dimension is18. A certified full Selmer dimension18 would give exact Jacobian rank18 and zero Sha[2]; a larger dimension is not automatically Sha. Prepared equation replay does not prove any local image or global Selmer group. Both frozen cases09/08 already have the simultaneous binary obstruction: individual blocks are soluble, but stacked inherited/augmented ranks are16/17. Both known true rational images have dimension18. Equal full Selmer dimensions alone would not establish differing realization; that inference also needs certified ranks. Subspace position requires specified arithmetic structure, and a full CT radical may contain divisible Sha.
lessons_before.reopen_when: A complete global algorithm or a new unresolved-place certificate supplies an obligation beyond the already closed local panels.

lessons_before.title: Test proposal recall and actual integral subgroup identity before tuning scores
lessons_before.when: A low-height or common-cover lattice candidate is proposed as a recovered generic family.
lessons_before.use: Check the full proposal ledger against the frozen masked control. The two generators peak at rank12 intersections8 and10; the second comparison covers all1928 rank12 proposals, so rescoring cannot recover an absent space. Keep the successful older graph-consensus primitive closure and its index2048 actual subgroup separate. Use Curve302's completed alternative MW17 parent for construction recovery.
lessons_before.avoid: Promoting a containing higher-rank space to exact recovery, recognizing Fermigier from index2^11 alone, or rerunning failed proposal generators to rediscover Curve302's already proved parent.
lessons_before.boundary: Any independent rank-r set in one nonzero parity class forces index divisible by2^(r-1) in its primitive closure. A projected Schur quotient is not an exact integral orthogonal complement. Neither rounded heights nor bounded proposal failure proves nonexistence.
lessons_before.reopen_when: A new generator passes a declared control at the exact requested rank and actual integral subgroup, with a separate geometric reconstruction proof.

lessons_before.title: Batch coset norms and sieve exact membership while preserving relation content
lessons_before.when: A fixed lattice proposal searches many shifted representatives or tests a large pool against candidate spaces.
lessons_before.use: Precompute shifts and their norms, then evaluate each coset with q(c+s)=q(s)+2s^T Hc+q(c) and stable ordering. Reuse an exact integer kernel: mod1009 matrix products reject nonmembers before exact integer products on survivors. Keep unit relations v_i plus or minus v_j equals v_k literal; dividing content would turn a+b=2c into a false unit edge.
lessons_before.avoid: Repeating full norm/rank calculations for every representative, treating the support-at-most-two shifted box as complete CVP, or using bounded qfminim's second field as the minimum.
lessons_before.boundary: The search explicitly minimizes returned norms. Agreement of80- and100-digit height balls is numerical evidence, not an interval-certified cutoff. verify_low_height_mw_sublattices --check rebuilds balls, minima and finite reductions; it is not a cheap metadata check.
lessons_before.reopen_when: The exact basis or proposal domain changes, or a new completeness claim requires certified numerical bounds and an appropriately scoped replay.

lessons_before.title: Keep section labels and ordinate branches fixed before stacking fibres
lessons_before.when: Finite reductions from several parameter values are stacked to prove generic independence.
lessons_before.use: Use one source-root permutation and exact rational-function ordinate branches. The Mestre adapter preserves both. The corrected13 probes have rank11; the old sorted-root and positive-square-root probes still have matrix rank13 but do not specialize one common coefficient relation.
lessons_before.avoid: Sorting section columns independently at each fibre, choosing square-root signs numerically, or treating tests that reproduce the old matrix as a valid generic proof.
lessons_before.boundary: A fixed coherent matrix of full column rank plus torsion exclusion proves the stated lower bound. Rank defects alone give neither dependence nor an upper bound. The rejected entry point now fails rather than emitting a false conclusion.
lessons_before.reopen_when: A fixed labelled section list has a new exact certificate for the stronger claimed rank.

lessons_before.title: Prove recursive section identities using explicit degree bounds
lessons_before.when: Expanded Mestre two-section residuals would create tens or hundreds of thousands of terms.
lessons_before.use: Keep the monic-square and triangular ordinate recursions. Bound the numerator degree after the declared denominator clearing, then check more distinct admissible exact values than that degree. The Fermigier component uses1141 values for bound1140; the diameter235 component uses1099 for bound1080. Retain excluded poles and the leading-square condition.
lessons_before.avoid: Treating a Hensel or Pade fit alone as a global identity, expanding residuals unnecessarily, or dropping D=w^2 after projecting to abscissa equations.
lessons_before.boundary: An identity proves an incidence component, not independence of its sections. Jacobian rank and finite jets do not settle the full component without the later exact argument.
lessons_before.reopen_when: A changed parameterization comes with a new denominator and degree proof.

lessons_before.title: Separate parameter aliases and nonminimal factors from source discrepancies
lessons_before.when: A Fermigier specialization or raw quartic discriminant appears to give a different family or bad-fibre pattern.
lessons_before.use: Reuse the exact adapter u=s/2 and retained coefficients. For Y^2=X^3-27IX-27J the raw discriminant scale is(607392u)^12, since c4_raw=1296I. The twelfth-power scalar and u factor are coordinate artifacts. The exact generic arithmetic rank12 is already proved separately.
lessons_before.avoid: Reusing the stale202464 scale, counting literal s and adapter u as unrelated candidates, or treating completed rank computations as a resolution of the paper convention.
lessons_before.boundary: Literal printed shift19754/39 and reconstruction shift39508/39 give different j-invariants; the source factor-two discrepancy remains unresolved. Benchmark GP conductor calls are not metadata checks.
lessons_before.reopen_when: Primary-source provenance explains the convention, or an explicit new coordinate map is proved.

lessons_before.title: Recover an unlabeled subgroup through exact relation components
lessons_before.when: Comparing high-rank specializations when the intended generic subgroup, section labels and source surface are not supplied.
lessons_before.use: Enumerate a declared short-vector cloud, extract additive-relation components, and prune with finite quotient ranks and height-angle compatibility. Take exact primitive rational closures after each merge, then select by held-out relation replay per added rank. Verify the final subgroup by exact integer linear algebra and elliptic-curve arithmetic.
lessons_before.avoid: Inferring a generic rank from a short-vector shell, treating numerical heights or selector outputs as a theorem, retuning after inspecting a failed target, or identifying a source surface before the subgroup survives exact replay.
lessons_before.boundary: The frozen controls recover a rank-12 Fermigier primitive closure and a rank-16 R17 component before exact completion. Two frozen target sets failed their own recurrence gates; this does not exclude another common primitive subgroup or recover a new family.
lessons_before.reopen_when: A new, independently frozen target set has declared inputs, exact subgroup endpoints and a pass condition before target outcomes are inspected.

lessons_before.title: Treat a frozen score replay as calibration, not prospective screening
lessons_before.when: Assessing a parameter score using known high-rank controls while the remaining population has no exact endpoint labels.
lessons_before.use: Freeze the score, primitive parameter domain, tie policy and evaluation budgets before ranking. Record each known control's exact position and keep all unassayed parameters explicitly censored. Use a miss to retire that score for the stated family and protocol.
lessons_before.avoid: Calling a known control a prospective holdout, assigning rank zero to unassayed parameters, reporting classifier accuracy from censored data, or launching another broad score campaign after a bounded calibration miss.
lessons_before.boundary: The Fermigier replay ranks 60,815,684 primitive parameters and finds both known controls beyond 2.7 million in every recorded ordering. It rules out those frozen local scores for this stated calibration only; it is neither a rank bound nor a general prediction result.
lessons_before.reopen_when: A new score has a separately scoped prospective protocol, genuinely withheld families, exact endpoints and a declared decision rule.

lessons_before.title: Keep a mechanism-label holdout separate from the rank target
lessons_before.when: Using finite-cover visibility or another bounded mechanism label to prioritize a total-rank search.
lessons_before.use: Freeze the population, arithmetic duplicate groups, score and review budget before labels or control outcomes are opened. Evaluate the mechanism label on its own outcome-free holdout, then separately record the once-opened rank-control result. Retire the score for the total-rank objective if it succeeds only on the mechanism response.
lessons_before.avoid: Calling bisection-gain AUC or enrichment a total-rank predictor; treating a publicly known quarantined control as a human-blind discovery; retuning after opening that control; or assigning censored bounded misses a negative rank label.
lessons_before.boundary: The frozen R17 ranker generalized to its 5,000-row bisection-label holdout but missed the rank-28 control at a one-percent budget. It establishes that the measured bisection response differs from extreme total rank in this protocol, not that bisections, learned scores, or other families cannot help a rank search.
lessons_before.reopen_when: A separately committed target has outcome-free arithmetic grouping, genuinely unopen controls and a response that matches the proposed decision endpoint.

lessons_before.title: Check the target coset before lifting a missing section
lessons_before.when: An explicit section shell has the right rank but may have nontrivial index in its saturation.
lessons_before.use: Compute the exact shell lattice and target coset in the equation marking. The A11 identity shell has index five; enumerate the marked target coset to obtain the P.O=5 bridge and reuse the short group word.
lessons_before.avoid: Lifting an arbitrary missing-rank section or the earlier P.O=4 vector: neither necessarily generates the desired target with the retained shell.
lessons_before.boundary: The pole bound and coset exclusion concern this marked lattice. The orbit12 equation was subsequently constructed; the old elimination timeout is not a remaining gate.
lessons_before.reopen_when: A different marked subgroup or target changes the exact coset problem.

lessons_before.title: Reconstruct shared coefficient scales projectively
lessons_before.when: Exact modular section coefficients have monic denominators but coefficientwise rational reconstruction stalls.
