lessons_before.avoid: Downloading a replacement input during replay, treating a URL and old hash as sufficient evidence, silently updating a public point list, or promoting a fixed finite-reduction lower bound to an exact rank or current-record claim.
lessons_before.boundary: The retained Kihara formulas at t=2 and the retained 29-point public record each support their exact stated lower bound without upstream access. They do not certify current external rankings, conditional upper bounds, a further point, or a different specialization.
lessons_before.reopen_when: The formula/model/coordinate packet, certificate criterion, or intended claim changes; preserve a new complete projection and compare it to the old packet before replaying.

lessons_before.title: Bound a six-root parent search in primitive coordinates
lessons_before.when: A known elliptic curve is absent from a bounded six-root parent census.
lessons_before.use: Record the labelled rational roots, affine scale and translation, parameter scale, and the resulting primitive integral root tuple. Set the search bound on that primitive diameter, then verify the exact model change and transported generic section.
lessons_before.avoid: Treating a miss in a normalized coordinate box as absence of a parent family, or using a matching j-invariant without an exact Weierstrass change.
lessons_before.boundary: For ICARM curve 245, the earlier diameter-300 census could not see the recovered parent because its primitive integral diameter is 731. This recognition result recovers a parent; it does not transfer the specialized rank to nearby fibres.
lessons_before.reopen_when: The proposed family has a different equivalence relation, root labelling, or primitive-bound convention.

lessons_before.title: Keep a rebuilt replay in a named successor lineage
lessons_before.when: A historical checker cannot run because its immutable source artifact or toolchain is unavailable, but a compatible exact source chain can be rebuilt.
lessons_before.use: Keep the historical program and its expected digest unchanged. Write a separate successor wrapper that asserts replacement input digests and writes a distinct schema and output path. If a new independent global proof becomes available, register it separately rather than retagging the historical record.
lessons_before.avoid: Retagging a rebuilt output as the historical artifact, relaxing a frozen input assertion, overwriting the old output path, or treating a bounded successor sieve as the missing global proof.
lessons_before.boundary: The H3 source successor and bounded quotient sieve remain distinct current replay records. The later Sage quadratic-Chabauty certificate proves the rational base independently; it does not recreate the historic Magma output.
lessons_before.reopen_when: The original inputs and runtime become available for a byte-identical historical replay, or another frozen certificate needs a successor lineage.

lessons_before.title: Close an even genus-two curve with two rank-one elliptic quotients
lessons_before.when: An even sextic y^2=a6*x^6+a4*x^4+a2*x^2+a0 has two explicit elliptic quotients with unconditional rank one and trivial torsion, and a global rational-point proof is required.
lessons_before.use: Pin a bielliptic quadratic-Chabauty implementation, use two good ordinary primes with a compatible finite height-value ordering, normalize quotient coordinates at a rational base point, close p-adic roots under the curve automorphisms, CRT their coordinates modulo p^N, then eliminate the remaining classes by exact good-reduction images.
lessons_before.avoid: Treating one p-adic pass, a bounded multiple search, or a finite reduction sieve by itself as completeness; and claiming the direct quotient-coordinate lattice is a saturated Jacobian basis when only its necessary quotient condition is used.
lessons_before.boundary: The method certifies only the displayed curve and the pinned implementation, primes, precision and finite sieve. It requires exact quotient rank and torsion certificates and does not construct a downstream surface or fibration equation. An offline replay must supply the one SHA-checked upstream source through --upstream-source; a cache miss otherwise downloads only the pinned revision.
lessons_before.reopen_when: The model, quotient maps, rank certificates, implementation hash, p-adic precision or candidate-eliminating prime set changes.

lessons_before.title: Transfer a labeled finite-reduction certificate to generic rank
lessons_before.when: Explicit sections of an elliptic family are available and one smooth rational specialization may establish a generic rank lower bound.
lessons_before.use: Verify the section identities over the function field, preserve their labels through one good specialization, select only the needed points, and stack exact E(F_p)/lE(F_p) columns until they have full rank. Add a good-reduction exclusion of rational l-torsion, then invoke specialization to transfer that selected independent subgroup to the generic fibre.
lessons_before.avoid: Sorting or changing branches separately at each reduction, treating all displayed sections as independent, or replacing the torsion check with a bounded relation search.
lessons_before.boundary: This proves only the lower bound supplied by the selected labeled sections. It gives neither generic rank equality, saturation, independence of unused companions, nor an exact conductor statement.
lessons_before.reopen_when: The family formulas, labeled section roster, specialization, reduction prime set, or torsion exclusion changes.

lessons_before.title: Keep unresolved quotient transports as literal unknowns
lessons_before.when: A finite population of specialized elliptic fibres has a mixture of exact displayed-subgroup transports and uncompiled chart-specific quotient data.
lessons_before.use: Bind the population and each marked-U chart to a profile artifact. Retain only exact transports as exact, leave every other dimension null, and select a new tranche solely by a declared arithmetic criterion such as the maximum certified specialized rank lower bound. For each selected row, require a saturated generic transport, exact specialization and group-law relations, displayed-subgroup independence, and a Smith-form quotient proof.
lessons_before.avoid: Treating a null as a zero quotient, copying a transport across PGL2 or lattice-equivalent markings, reopening a completed tranche, or using public hit counts as a success-rate denominator or priority score.
lessons_before.boundary: A displayed-subgroup quotient is not the quotient of the full Mordell--Weil group and gives no rank upper bound. The selected initial tranche is a reproducible work priority, not evidence that it has positive quotient rank or that deferred rows are unpromising.
lessons_before.reopen_when: The marked-U transport, certified rank lower bounds, population membership, or exact quotient data changes.

lessons_before.title: Require quotient-invariant local data before using Kummer information as a selector
lessons_before.when: Comparing fixed high-rank specializations for a shared local Kummer signature that might justify congruence filtering or a parameter search.
lessons_before.use: Present the displayed directions as V/R before choosing any complement. Compare only local Kummer and component data that descend through R; for each componentwise Hilbert form B, check R*B=0 before treating it as a quotient tensor. If the retained quotient-invariant signatures disagree, preserve the exact obstruction primes and terminate that selector route.
lessons_before.avoid: Building a graph from RREF nonpivot coordinates, treating the identically trivial corestricted local Tate form as a coupling signal, turning a fixed-pair mismatch into a global nonexistence theorem, or launching a parameter search merely because a local diagnostic was computed.
lessons_before.boundary: The gate concerns the stated quotient presentation and selected fibres. It proves neither a full Mordell--Weil quotient nor a rank upper bound, and it leaves mechanisms based on different invariant data open.
lessons_before.reopen_when: A different quotient-compatible invariant, a changed visible relation space, or an independently justified family-wide mathematical gate is available.

lessons_before.title: Use certified local height bounds to compare complementary models of the same pointed chart
lessons_before.when: Comparing equivalent pointed quartic models for a fixed elliptic equation and anchor, before choosing search boxes.
lessons_before.use: Compose the exact x(2P-Q) map with each parameter matrix. Bound its real norm on the soluble compact projective charts, and refine the uniform Bezout cancellation divisor using complete finite residue trees with proved nonsquare exclusions. Keep unprocessed primes and branches conservatively. For multiple minimal models, retain joint local cells and take max over cells of min over complete models. Charge construction, bounds, failed attempts, point calls and verification in the next-direction benchmark.
lessons_before.avoid: Choosing a model by coefficient size alone, confusing a smaller sufficient height bound with containment of every old search box, summing model-wise minima independently across primes, or calling a rational-address work proxy a CPU or rank-gain prediction.
lessons_before.boundary: One actual Curve302 chart supplies independently replayed bounds and three certified minimal models. The base-plus7-neighbour pair has approximately1.48033 improvement in sufficient per-box height and0.91266 address-work ratio, but no new point search or speed advantage. The finite bounds need not be optimal. The old factor-free model is a comparator, not one of the three minimal models.
lessons_before.reopen_when: A frozen next-direction comparison pays for its new preparation and then transfers to independently sourced withheld directions on other curves.

lessons_before.title: Separate cold support, uniform coverage and actual target accessibility
lessons_before.when: Benchmarking a certified height-based model selector at the supplied equation, subgroup and anchor interface.
lessons_before.use: Freeze model vocabulary and exact pair-height allocation before search; charge required support discovery and verification. After all endpoints are sealed, transport each literal winning point into every model and verify its parameter height and exact slack decomposition log(C/g)/4 plus log(S/L)/4. Keep diagnostics separate from arm costs and target-informed selection.
lessons_before.avoid: Treating cached discriminant factors as free cold preparation, hiding a preparation timeout as a point-search miss, assuming the smallest uniform bound gives the smallest coordinate for each point, or using a distinct-prime product partition for two neighbours at one prime.
lessons_before.boundary: On three Curve302 controls the baseline recovers the next direction, while all six bounded arms hit a30-second support limit and make no point calls. Twelve individual-model coordinates replay; the best uniform bound selects a smallest actual coordinate only in the first row. Finite cancellation dominates the slack. This is a three-target conditional diagnostic, not a general performance or probability statement. The same-prime pair is UNKNOWN only for the frozen formula.
lessons_before.reopen_when: A specifically revised, bounded preparation or model-selection policy addresses the measured bottleneck and receives a new complete-cost comparison; no automatic rerun or budget enlargement.

lessons_before.title: Optimize complete coverage with unequal box heights and explicit model costs
lessons_before.when: A certified complete joint-state table for equivalent models of one marked chart is already available.
lessons_before.use: At a declared elliptic-height range X, compute exact ceil((X D_i(s))^(1/4)) thresholds. Minimize a supplied monotone cost over boxes meeting at least one model threshold for every joint state. Charge activation separately from all-bank preparation, including discarded models. Check the finite optimum by independent state assignments; keep the statewise choice coupled across all places.
lessons_before.avoid: Treating minimization of a shared coverage constant as the whole cost problem, dropping discarded-model preparation, calling an equal H-squared price a CPU calibration, or using uniform coverage as a probability model for the first independent point.
lessons_before.boundary: The earlier equal-box selector already charged model count through |T|^2 D_T. On its unchanged three-model/four-state first chart, unequal heights yield an exact 0.573942907264 address-proxy ratio to the best single, or 0.599197887808 with at most two models. This does not resolve cold support timeouts or the observed targetwise finite-cancellation slack. No search was run or selector deployed into the sealed benchmark.
lessons_before.reopen_when: A bounded preparation and independently calibrated pricing policy is frozen for a new complete-cost comparison. Transfer needs independently sourced cross-curve targets; proxy optimization alone does not authorize a campaign.

lessons_before.title: Verify integral orders and the backend input contract before global Selmer arithmetic
lessons_before.when: Completing global descent on one of the two frozen large nonmonic RR sextics.
lessons_before.use: Reuse the exact pair inputs and order checkpoints. A binary-sextic order removes an artificial monic index; certify ring closure and its trace discriminant before using it for generator reduction. Reconstructing a partial order after a generator change can lose integrality away from the trial primes. Keep complete supported squareclasses, class and unit contributions, local conditions and the true/fake comparison as separate obligations. Preserve both verified orders after a generator change by adjoining their pairwise basis products. In a commutative field their product lattice is already an order. The fixed RR join has independently checked containment, integral multiplication and Newton trace discriminants of22655/37378bits for cases09/08. The third retained order is contained in that join in both cases. Gcd-refining discriminant/index divisors and using the distinct coprime-list nfinit contract gives successor order discriminants22655/28881bits; exact support decomposition and containment replay independently.
lessons_before.avoid: Treating a nonempty nfcertify remainder as a field discriminant, treating known local or rational Kummer spans as a complete global space, or using nfcertify=[] on an arbitrary basis supplied to nfinit as an independent maximality proof. The supplied-basis example X^2-20 returns[] for the nonmaximal order of discriminant80.
lessons_before.boundary: Cases09 and08 have verified model and field maps and integral orders, but no certified maximal order or global Selmer dimension. Both certification passes returned unresolved composites. The measured order sizes and failure receipts do not prove intrinsic infeasibility or equal residual dimensions. Same-fibre matching tests the marked construction, not a population rank effect. The joined orders improve the retained checkpoints but have no new maximality certificate; their size is not a field-complexity comparison. Both coprime-list nfcertify calls still return unresolved cofactors22633/28878bits, so global completeness remains open.
lessons_before.reopen_when: An exact maximal-order/support certificate or a different certified global upper-envelope method addresses the unresolved pair; reusing already completed local images alone is insufficient.

lessons_before.title: Count normalization delta with infinity and keep the high-rank parent fixed
lessons_before.when: Forcing two polynomial trace-zero bisections of arithmetic genus5 to share a quadratic cover of genus0 or1.
lessons_before.use: Write F=x^3+A*x+B and its jet conditions. At a root of multiplicity m use delta=floor(m/2), and include the missing multiplicity at infinity in the degree12 binary form. Impose one literal D in both identities. Extract repeated factors D=e^2*d before deciding the genus: residual degree2 gives a possible genus0 boundary. Reuse the height8 independence criterion when the branch avoids the parent discriminant. For a fixed constant-abscissa line, the degree33 critical-point polynomial and critical-value norm can certify its entire singularity locus by exact interpolation and a good-prime squarefreeness witness. For the complete coefficient chart, factor the difference identity with g=gcd(D,h), u=gcd(h/g,r1-r2) and v=(h/g)/u after monic normalization. Keep all15 degree allocations and nine good coordinate patches; the squarefree height cross term is4-k-2*j. On Q80 use unramified Kummer descent to eliminate the complete k=4 genus-one case before any elimination. lessons_before.avoid: Using complex conjugacy of groups to choose an arithmetic twist; requiring global integrality from a matrix that is only a local unit.
lessons_before.boundary: Determinant800 has full local2 coverage and no orientation ambiguity. This does not automatically extend to other lattices.
lessons_before.reopen_when: A different literal lattice, local level, or unresolved normalizer coset is supplied.

lessons_before.title: Separate the branch character image from the realized inherited trace norms
lessons_before.when: Seeking two correlated directions on a low-genus quadratic cover of Q80, especially after polynomial-chart exclusions.
lessons_before.use: Include O in every branch2-torsion space and compute the kernel of the sum of inherited norm characters. Reuse completed field censuses, but add short-support and code-plane joins to include zero branch values. Under the retained unramified Kummer theorem, branch-zero anti-invariants are exactly actual anti-traces. Account for rank by r=dim(Tr E(L)/2E(K))+dim(branch image). Construct two independent trace parities through the explicit torsors H_T(m)=d*s^2 on one literal d; these certify independence without numerical height fitting.
lessons_before.avoid: Inferring rank-at-most-one from a one-dimensional branch code, treating inherited trace classes as inherited new points, dividing a section formally without Kummer exactness, discarding zeros or root-free sites, extending a good-branch-reduction theorem to nodal or repeated residue branches, or calling local norm compatibility global torsor solubility.
lessons_before.boundary: The complete good-reduction degree2/4 Q80 branch code has dimension0/at-most1. All seven residual degree partitions are covered with new independent finite joins and retained higher-degree arithmetic. The rank accounting and descent are written mathematics. This closes height8/10 only in that good quartic reduction scope, and confines height10/10 to equal branch values with half-image genera(2,2) or(1,3). No MW17 points, soluble norm torsors, or infinite rank19 base are constructed.
lessons_before.reopen_when: An actual common low-genus d yields two independent realized inherited trace parities, or one plus a nonzero branch class; alternatively a justified analysis treats bad branch reduction or a different MW17 parent.

lessons_before.title: Use integral split transports and real square-two requirements before new period curves
lessons_before.when: Selecting a rationally fully marked rank19 K3 from literal ternary lattice data.
lessons_before.use: For an even primitive half-lattice with a divisibility-one isotropic vector, construct and check a unimodular U basis. If T=2(U+<2N>) withN>=5, the full Q-marked curve X0(4N) excludes it. For anisotropic T, an exhaustive square2 congruence obstruction plus exact local anisotropy excludes the real marking.
lessons_before.avoid: Treating equal determinants or rational similarities as integral split witnesses; treating successful residue tests as an integral vector or rational marking; extrapolating an arithmetic model from finite controls alone.
lessons_before.boundary: The84 split transports and36 local obstructions cover the stated retained inputs. The uniform theorem includes the full normalizer and compatible orientation. SmallN, untransported rows and congruence survivors remain outside the exclusions.
lessons_before.reopen_when: A different actual lattice, a smallN arithmetic source, or an unexcluded full rational marking is supplied.

lessons_before.title: Require the same generic halving parity at every branch fibre
lessons_before.when: A prospective low-genus quadratic cover passes branch-character conditions but still needs global trace-norm points.
lessons_before.use: Bound the realized trace-parity space by the intersection of specialization kernels M/2M -> E_b(k(b))/2E_b(k(b)). At rational branch values, stack exact finite elliptic-group quotients to certify injectivity or bound that kernel. Coefficient valuation margins extend fixed-value witnesses to certified rational congruence neighbourhoods. Test actual residue-field2-torsion separately from roots modulo one prime. Combine these two bounds with the retained unramified Kummer theorem and exact rank formula. Over a quadratic branch field, use good degree-one residue places and retain the actual section-basis coordinates; lattice-frame coordinates can differ.
lessons_before.avoid: Treating different local halving defects as a common generic parity, overlooking specialization relations, confusing local cubic roots with residue-field2-torsion, or promoting an infinite base and a compatible branch pattern to a new direction. Do not interpret a trace-parity injection as an upper bound on specialized rational fibre rank.
lessons_before.boundary: Q80 K_0 is zero, with an independent complete finite-group certificate and a fourteen-prime rational neighbourhood. The explicit infinite elliptic base t(t-2)(t-76)(t-103) gives exact generic rank17 and zero gain. All-height exclusion uses the established global unramified theorem and smooth characteristic-zero branch fibres. Other branch divisors and common-kernel global lifting remain unresolved. The fixed known-gain cover alternate-orbit-11ae6 has exact one-dimensional kernel and exact rank18 at every height; other atlas members are not closed by this one-cover check.
lessons_before.reopen_when: A branch divisor has the required common nonzero halving kernel and exact rational-function solutions on the same trace torsors, or another parent changes the arithmetic prerequisites.

lessons_before.title: Separate full period admission, effective K3 descent and divisor descent
lessons_before.when: A rank19 stable orthogonal quotient has a rational point and the full canonical arithmetic level has been identified.
lessons_before.use: Certify non-CM by a ring-class-field obstruction, glue the literal NS and T primitively, exclude marked automorphisms, then discharge invariant-line-bundle descent. For388 a lift field ramified at7411 proves non-CM; two square-minus-two classes meeting once give a degree-one zero-cycle and full divisor descent.
lessons_before.avoid: Treating a rational coarse point alone as a marked K3; treating Galois-invariant Picard classes automatically as rational line bundles; treating one rootful frame as an exhaustive absence of MW17. In the retained rootless preflight, PARI qfminim with maxvec=0 returned no stored vectors despite a nonzero count; that false-hit packet is explicitly withdrawn. Always check the total against stored representatives and a known-root control.
lessons_before.boundary: This proves an abstract full rational marking, without an equation. The later global root-energy theorem excludes MW17 on this NS; it does not retract the descent result.
lessons_before.reopen_when: A new marking changes the local level, has residual automorphisms, or lacks a divisor-descent argument.

lessons_before.title: Exclude rootless2-neighbours with a complete parity cover and norm-eight witnesses
lessons_before.when: An even positive frame has displayed roots that every rootless2-neighbour must remove.
lessons_before.use: Enumerate v modulo2F with even quadratic value and odd pairing with every old root. For each class, an explicit same-parity norm-eight vector halves to a root in its even neighbour. Check mod2 radical lifts separately at determinant-dividing prime2. Replay needs only these finite witnesses, not a complete short-vector census.
lessons_before.avoid: Assuming2 is a good prime; ignoring radical-line neighbours; mistaking a bounded neighbour miss or one-frame obstruction for a genus-wide rootlessness exclusion.
lessons_before.boundary: The pinned388 index106 frame has a rootful entire even2-neighbour shell. The subsequent global root-energy theorem separately excludes all frames of this NS; the local method alone has only its one-frame scope.
lessons_before.reopen_when: The parent frame changes, the neighbour degree changes, or a global genus argument becomes available.

lessons_before.title: Seek low-degree points on the simultaneous branch-incidence curves
lessons_before.when: A24-I1 elliptic K3 with its full geometric MW group rational is being tested for two trace directions on one low-genus quadratic cover.
lessons_before.use: Two independent trace parities require residue-field lifts of every branch to the degree16 genus57 joint-half curve. A nonzero trace plus an actual nonzero branch2-torsion value requires a lift to the degree12 genus49 mixed incidence curve. Primitive forgetful maps and Castelnuovo-Severi exclude degree-at-most4 maps to genus0 or1; Kadets-Vogt then gives a finite low-degree-point locus. Use an actual low-degree incidence point as the next arithmetic gate before solving global trace torsors.
lessons_before.avoid: Assuming that high genus alone excludes low-degree points, applying Riemann-Hurwitz to a disconnected fibre product, confusing a local modular point with a residue-field point, or treating noneffective finiteness as an empty set or a construction.
lessons_before.boundary: Full geometric parity independence,24-I1 fibres and a fixed number field are essential. The two-trace locus gives finite branch divisors and constant characters. The mixed locus restricts only its marked branch. Q80 gain conclusions retain the good131 branch-image bounds; other branch-reduction scopes and the positive endpoint remain open.
lessons_before.reopen_when: A genuine degree-at-most4 incidence point is obtained, with an exact common trace-torsor lift and the required rational or infinite elliptic base; or a different parent changes the monodromy/fibre hypotheses.

lessons_before.title: Use a root-rich auxiliary and Weyl-support norm bounds before rank17 genus enumeration
lessons_before.when: An admitted NS has a positive rank7 opposite-discriminant auxiliary containing a rank5 root system.
lessons_before.use: Find a convenient explicit auxiliary in its much smaller genus, verify its discriminant anti-isometry, and compute the projected Gram of the two remaining generators. For each complete Niemeier anchor, bound simultaneous root avoidance by minimizing 1_S^t C^-1 1_S + 1_Z^t C_Z^-1 1_Z over Dynkin supports; add bounds across orthogonal components. If every required norm sum exceeds the available trace, all frame complements are rootful.
lessons_before.avoid: Replacing the actual finite discriminant form by determinant equality; the attractive rank6 auxiliaries tried for388 have the wrong form. Do not infer global nonexistence from local neighbour misses or from the auxiliary mass search alone.
lessons_before.boundary: For388 every case fails strictly. For852 energy bounds alone leave2A7+2D5; the subsequent exhaustive two-vector/glue calculation excludes that final case. The energy reduction alone is not the global exclusion, and auxiliary genus completeness is discovery only.
lessons_before.reopen_when: Another NS discriminant form, a new arithmetic marking, or an auxiliary whose projected norms pass the bound is supplied.

lessons_before.title: Certify elementary branch relations before searching for additional halves
lessons_before.when: Trying to populate the low-degree joint-halving or mixed incidence loci from a retained generic MW basis.
lessons_before.use: Form cancelled pole and signed abscissa-equality loci and the correct long-Weierstrass torsion ordinate2y+a1*x+a3. A pair of independent zero relations supplies explicit halves O; one relation with nonzero torsion supplies mixed incidence. Use monic polynomials integral at the chosen reduction prime, followed by exact rational gcd on every modular survivor. At known pole fields, bound the full specialization kernel with finite elliptic-group quotients and retain the visible generic parity as a lower bound.
lessons_before.avoid: Using a fixed prime without checking monic integrality or degree preservation, treating y=0 as the2-torsion condition on a long model, conflating an ordinary relation with two independent parity relations, or extending a basis-only miss to all MW combinations.
lessons_before.boundary: The four retained basis-derived lists have no simultaneous elementary incidence, including infinity. All12 Q80 basis pole fields have exactly one kernel direction and no nonzero residue-field2-torsion. The initial fixed131 prototype was unaccepted and is preserved; only the rerun with integral monic reduction supports the exclusions.
lessons_before.reopen_when: A distinct exact generic combination provides an additional residue-field half, or an actual low-degree incidence point outside these fixed elementary lists is constructed. A larger unmotivated coefficient box is not a new gate.

lessons_before.title: Check j-monodromy before trying to duplicate sections by a cover symmetry
lessons_before.when: A proposed correlated-gain mechanism uses an automorphism or isogeny to turn one known new direction into another.
lessons_before.use: For a degree24 K3 j-map, certify simple c4,c6,D divisors and18 distinct additional simple critical values. Compute critical images as multiplication by j in the degree18 critical algebra and verify its squarefree characteristic polynomial. The3^8,2^12 and18 transposition branch cycles force S24 by the normal-closure argument, so a distinct equal-j generic parameter costs degree23. This controls extra automorphisms even on covers where descent to the original parameter was not assumed.
lessons_before.avoid: Assuming no parent base symmetry automatically rules out cover symmetries, overlooking collisions among critical values, confusing generic equal-j rigidity with a ban on specialized j coincidences, or using an already independent new translation as its own construction.
lessons_before.boundary: All four retained actual MW17 parents pass the S24 gate. Every quadratic-cover j-symmetry is identity or deck, and origin-preserving symmetries act by signs on an anti-invariant direction. The24-I1 full mod-ell theorem also excludes nontrivial isogeny transport over a quadratic field. Neither statement bounds arbitrary twist rank or excludes fibration-changing surface automorphisms.
lessons_before.reopen_when: A different actual arithmetic MW17 parent has a certified suitable symmetry and an invariant low-genus cover with an independent section orbit. Critical-value collisions alone are insufficient, and a new parent still requires the rational marking and full arithmetic rank evidence.

lessons_before.title: Rationalize the full rank-one Inose Mordell-Weil group by its constant sign character
lessons_before.when: A rational Inose model comes from a non-CM isogenous pair and has two rational II* fibres with torsion-free geometric MW rank1.
lessons_before.use: Write the Inose equation using rational symmetric j invariants, without demanding rational cube or square roots. The two affineE8 graphs force every trivial-lattice divisor rational. The full geometric MW generator transforms by a continuous sign character; the matching constant quadratic twist fixes it and yields full saturated rational NS.
lessons_before.avoid: Calling the untwisted model fully marked before computing its character; treating rational roots of normalized invariants as necessary; using a coarse period point alone instead of surface/divisor descent. Unneeded large coefficient factorization in the preflight was stopped and is not a prerequisite.
lessons_before.boundary: The level311 source has NS determinant622 and a rationalizing twist exists; its squareclass and section remain uncomputed. The later global root obstruction excludes MW17 on this NS, so explicit twist calculation is not needed for this goal. Higher MW rank can have Galois action that a single twist cannot trivialize.
lessons_before.reopen_when: The character is computed, a different isogenous pair supplies a source, or the geometric MW rank or fibre Galois action differs.

lessons_before.title: Resolve borderline Niemeier energy cases with centered integer pairs and equality constraints
lessons_before.when: A two-vector auxiliary trace equals the sharp residual root-avoidance lower bound instead of violating it strictly.
lessons_before.use: For A_n encode two integral-pairing vectors as n+1 distinct integer pairs centered at their mean. Enumerate centroid residues modulo integers and nearest-point distances, certify equality sets and their separate coordinate norms. Equality in a total energy bound then constrains each projected norm. On the residual D5, short dual vectors leave D4 roots whose regular-vector norm requirement can contradict the remaining budget.
lessons_before.avoid: Declaring a rootless frame from a non-strict support bound, or treating the trace alone as the full Gram constraint. Retain the auxiliary discovery and all finite equality witnesses.
lessons_before.boundary: For622, A7 has sharp bound39/4 with each equality coordinate norm39/8. Two copies plus D5 meet trace51/2, but leave D5 norms<=1 and<=5, incompatible with the D4 regular-vector bound14. All16 Niemeier cases are thereby excluded in this NS genus.
lessons_before.reopen_when: Another admitted NS or auxiliary has different discriminant form, projected Gram or residual root systems; an equality-compatible case still requires actual primitive embedding and arithmetic fibration work.

lessons_before.title: An order-four lift makes one new direction an orthogonal pair
lessons_before.when: A prospective parent has an origin-preserving base involution and a symmetry-based two-gain construction is being considered.
lessons_before.use: Require a rational lift alpha with alpha^2 equal to the quadratic deck involution. The anti-invariant group then has Q(i)-module structure, even rank and an orthogonal orbit P,alpha(P). For a rational conic over Q the intermediate base involution must have fixed-point field Q(i); normalize it to -1/t and use w^2=t^2+1. Before equivariant lattice searches, test fields of known involution-fixed points: any fixed point over a field not containing i excludes this lift on every equivariant rational fibration. Before frame or involution searches on a fully rational Picard19 K3, test the actual T for rational isotropy. If it is anisotropic, real topology excludes every base-fixed-point-free pointed involution and hence the order-four conic mechanism. For a proposed rational Fricke source at composite level N, first forget to divisors d|N whose modular curves have a complete degree-at-most-two point classification. A non-CM rational Fricke point would induce a non-CM point of degree at most2 at each such lower level; an empty lower-level locus closes the source without building its fibre.
lessons_before.avoid: Assuming an order-two parent symmetry already forces two gains, overlooking the square of its lift, substituting a low-rank control for MW17, or treating a geometric9+8 eigenspace split as an arithmetic conic lift.
lessons_before.boundary: The explicit control realizes diag(8,8) on a rational conic but has parent rank at most10. The four retained MW17 parents fail the prior S24 symmetry gate. The canonical determinant622 Inose reversal and its Q-conjugates fail the fixed-point-field gate on every constant twist; the independent global determinant622 root obstruction now excludes every MW17 frame on that surface. The complete X1092 frame gate also excludes the required pointed base involutions on all nineteen rootless frames. A genus1 base over Q cannot have the required order-four lift because its differential eigenvalue would square to-1. The retained determinant1020 rootless frame also fails: its complete PARI isometry group is {I,-I}, so no trace1 involution exists. This is one frame, not a classification of that NS. Require a success marker when running PARI: stack changes discard remaining expressions on the same line, and default parallel worker stacks can exceed a fixed memory cap. Complete determinant948 rootless J2 coverage gives involution traces -17 and {-17,-3,3}; absence of1 excludes every MW17 fibration on that NS, independently of J1 orbit enumeration, and also excludes the rational-surface8+9 symmetric-parent setup there. This global real-place gate excludes the mechanism for948,1092 and1020 without a complete1020 frame census. Isotropic T is only necessary. Other Picard ranks, incomplete rational markings and nonsymmetry constructions are not excluded. A new star510 point is an explicit exploratory input for an isotropic Inose source, but its degree-eight Fricke lift is now excluded by the complete level51 quadratic-point classification. The existing determinant1020 rootless frame has the wrong discriminant form modulo5 for the isotropic NS. Author point logs and canonical HNF model files use different bases; bind coordinates to cached forms and verify the relation through its Sturm bound before using them.
lessons_before.reopen_when: An actual arithmetic MW17 parent has a verified suitable involution with the Q(i) fixed-base field, and one nontorsion anti-invariant section is constructed on the distinguished rational conic. All parent, cover and point evidence must be explicit.

lessons_before.title: Match published positive-rank Shimura quotients only after full stable-kernel verification
lessons_before.when: A content-one ternary lattice has a squarefree reduced Clifford discriminant and a candidate full-Fricke Shimura quotient in rational-point tables.
lessons_before.use: Match literal quaternion/order data first, then prove integral normalizers exhaust the discriminant actions and all local order units are stable. Verify the canonical arithmetic level. Separate published rational-point existence from Jacobian isomorphism; verify a non-torsion point directly on the model.
lessons_before.avoid: Using a coarse quotient or a positive-rank Jacobian as a rational marked source; labelling an infinite-order elliptic point non-CM without identifying its moduli interpretation.
lessons_before.boundary: The852 full curve, intrinsic rational non-CM point, primitive NS and actual divisor descent are proved. The subsequent complete final-anchor obstruction excludes MW17 in this NS. Its arithmetic marking survives;600 other rows remain unadmitted.
lessons_before.reopen_when: A non-CM point with moduli interpretation and full descent is certified, or another literal stable curve passes these tests.

lessons_before.title: A nine-plus-eight MW split must also satisfy discriminant gluing
lessons_before.when: Considering a pointed involution on a Picard19 rootless MW17 frame for correlated quadratic gains.
lessons_before.use: Inspect the complete frame automorphism group for trace-one involutions and require (g-I)H^(-1) integral. A symplectic involution fixes the transcendental lattice, so the NS discriminant action must be trivial. Apply this cheap exact test before equation reconstruction.
lessons_before.avoid: Treating a rational eigenspace split as sufficient for a K3 involution, or reconstructing another X1092 frame to revive the order-four mechanism.
lessons_before.boundary: All nineteen X1092 rootless J2 types are covered using inherited census completeness and group orders. Five trace-one candidates fail gluing. The theorem excludes pointed base involutions but not arbitrary correlated gains or fibration-changing automorphisms. The batched PARI timeout is preserved as an engineering failure; isolated generators and exact matrix closure supply accepted evidence.
lessons_before.reopen_when: A different NS with actual arithmetic marking has a compatible lattice involution, geometric realization, the Q(i) fixed-base condition and a new anti-invariant direction.

lessons_before.title: Halving points must have the same residue field as their branch value
lessons_before.when: Using low-degree points on a primitive halving curve to construct a quadratic rank-gain cover.
lessons_before.use: Require k(P)=k(t(P)). For the trace of a smooth rational bisection, use the F1 quotient and its adjoint fixed divisor to prove uniqueness of the original rational degree-four pencil. Points obtained by varying rational t lie over larger residue fields and are not usable branch halves.
lessons_before.avoid: Treating a quartic half above rational t as a half over the branch field, confusing field equality with a number field having no subfields, or claiming finiteness from uniqueness of a rational pencil.
lessons_before.boundary: Applies to the primitive trace of an embedded smooth rational bisection on a24-I1 K3, including Q80 parity65538. Its usable degree2..4 points are P1-isolated, but elliptic quotients and isolated arithmetic points remain uncomputed. The checker verifies embedding premises and intersection arithmetic; the quotient and complete-linear-system argument is written.
lessons_before.reopen_when: An exact half with residue field equal to its base-value field is supplied outside the original rational pencil, together with the additional independent incidence and global trace lifting needed for two gains.

lessons_before.title: Finish an energy-surviving Niemeier anchor with exact dual-root labels and both D5 orientations
lessons_before.when: A primitive opposite-form auxiliary contains D5 and energy bounds leave a small number of Niemeier anchors.
lessons_before.use: Check both D5 outer diagram orientations unless an ambient extension is certified. Move the sixth vector into a residual Weyl chamber; enumerate nonnegative integral labels with its exact projected norm, regular seventh-vector lower bounds and actual Niemeier glue. Use its zero-node Weyl stabilizer to make the seventh labels positive there; exhaust dual-root vectors under exact component bounds and match both norm and pairing.
lessons_before.avoid: Treating one D5 diagram orientation as all embeddings, or substituting root-lattice coordinates for the Niemeier glue. Verify stored-vector counts equal full enumeration counts. A passed trace bound alone is neither a witness nor an obstruction.
lessons_before.boundary: For852,52 sixth label combinations per orientation reduce to13 integral vectors; all26 cases have zero seventh norm/pairing matches. This closes the last anchor and the actual NS genus, with no determinant-wide or lower maximum-rank claim.
lessons_before.reopen_when: A different admitted NS or auxiliary survives these exact constraints; a surviving vector pair still requires primitive embedding, rootless complement and arithmetic equation certificates.

lessons_before.title: Use rational tangent points for the first singular elliptic-bisection layer
lessons_before.when: Seeking genus-one quadratic covers beyond smooth bisection pencils on a24-I1 elliptic K3.
lessons_before.use: For arithmetic-genus2 images, normalize trace modulo twice the inherited MW group and pass to the quotient by T-P. Its F1 branch curve has genus9. A genuine genus-one normalization comes from a rational tangent point with exactly one contact of order2 or3; test its tangent line, integral pullback, residual quartic and rational base. For any smooth-branch cover, use h(anti-trace)=4*(p_a+3) to certify independence from a nonsquare genus ratio once the literal cover is identical. For an inherited rational contact in this layer, require h(T-2R)>=14 before interpolation. Recover a retained height-four word over Q by seven exact fibre evaluations, verify its polynomial equation, and use the intersection bound to attach it to the word; finite-field coordinates alone are insufficient. For arithmetic genus4, use a degree-three contact divisor on the F1 halving curve. Construct its Hermite lift modulo f^2 and test the three-by-two high-coefficient matrix before solving the full six jets. Rank1, homogeneous coprimality, actual incidence and a squarefree residual quartic are separate required checks. Infinite arithmetic supply would force a degree-three elliptic quotient; a contact-parameter elliptic curve is not the covering base. At equality in Castelnuovo-Severi, compare the same intrinsic adjoint line bundle on the forced smooth product model and on the ruled quotient. On F1, restriction of |2C0+F| retains C0.R as a fixed divisor; on a (3,4) curve in P1 times an elliptic curve, three explicit chart-glued adjoint sections have no common zero. Apply this obstruction before a cubic elliptic-map or Jacobian campaign.
lessons_before.avoid: Searching an unbounded two-parameter net as if rational one-node members formed a free rational family, mistaking rational singular points of the plane or dual curve for rational points of the normalization, or treating finiteness as an effective enumeration.
lessons_before.boundary: Finiteness is for arithmetic genus2 and normalization genus1 modulo inherited translations over a fixed number field. It does not exclude all such members or higher arithmetic genus. The height identity requires smooth parent branch fibres. A square height ratio proves neither dependence nor independence. Symbolic premises are checked but the geometric and Faltings arguments are written. For Q80 trace P3, the complete retained height-four shell at distance h(P3-2R)=14 has 230 oriented sections and no rational contact, including poles and infinity. Exact degree-five/degree-thirteen factors have modular no-root witnesses. This is a bounded experiment, not an all-height or all-trace exclusion. The cubic-contact constructor supplies no actual halving point. Although the genus9 Castelnuovo-Severi bound reaches equality for a degree-three elliptic quotient, its smooth product model makes |K_R-2L| basepoint-free, contradicting the fixed length-two divisor on F1. That quotient is now geometrically excluded and the arithmetic-genus4 layer is finite modulo translations. Exceptional contacts remain unenumerated; larger-degree elliptic maps and higher image genera are outside the result.
lessons_before.reopen_when: An actual eligible rational tangent point yields a literal quartic matching another independent bisection cover, with an infinite rational covering base, or a new construction addresses higher arithmetic-genus images.

lessons_before.title: Use a torsion CM orbit and one non-torsion CM orbit to specify a non-CM period intrinsically
lessons_before.when: A fully marked elliptic Shimura curve has rational torsionE[2], a four-point CM locus fixed by an inversion, and a second eight-point CM locus under residual translations and inversion.
lessons_before.use: Choose a point O in the first CM locus as origin. The first locus is exactlyE[2]; any point R in the second is non-torsion and that locus is +/-R+E[2]. Then2R is in neither locus, since2R=+/-R+T would make R or3R torsion. This gives a particular rational non-CM period without numerical CM coordinates.
lessons_before.avoid: Equating positive rank on a Jacobian with rational points on its torsor; applying the orbit argument before proving the complete CM locus and full marked group. Intrinsic coordinates are not a K3 equation certificate.
lessons_before.boundary: For1020 the full curve is510d2, CM discriminants are-3 and-163, and primitive embedding plus divisor descent prove full rational NS. A separate subsequent determinant1020 existence proof supplies the rootless frame and arithmetic MW17; this orbit method itself supplies neither equation nor frame. The source is outside the catalogue;600 historical rows remain separate.
lessons_before.reopen_when: Another full marked elliptic curve has the stated orbit and torsion data, or an explicit equation requires recovery of the intrinsic period coordinates.

lessons_before.title: Construct the second singular elliptic-bisection layer from actual quadratic contact jets
lessons_before.when: Seeking an arithmetic-genus3 bisection with genus1 normalization on a24-I1 K3.
lessons_before.use: Choose an actual degree-two contact divisor on the primitive halving curve. In F0 require the norm of its tangent slope to equal the squared secant coefficient; in F2 require slope trace twice that coefficient. Solve the four linear jet conditions, require a rank3 kernel giving an integral section, and verify the exact residual quartic and scalar. Fixed contact data determine at most one integral section by the intersection bound.
lessons_before.avoid: Replacing an actual halving-curve point by arbitrary quadratic coordinates, treating determinant zero as sufficient despite a reducible kernel, omitting diagonal contacts or infinity, or declaring an infinite rational base from a rational singular point.
lessons_before.boundary: The complete arithmetic-genus3 genus-one layer is finite over a fixed number field modulo inherited translations, not enumerated or empty. Higher image genus remains open. The exact interpolation controls are not K3 points. A matching cover of image genus1 or2 would give independent anti-traces by heights24 versus16 or20, but no match is supplied.
lessons_before.reopen_when: An actual halving-curve contact divisor passes the jet, irreducibility and residual quartic checks and matches a second verified cover with an infinite rational base.

lessons_before.title: A genuine inherited half can still force reducible contact interpolation
lessons_before.when: Using two conjugate quadratic halving points supplied by a fixed inherited section to construct an arithmetic-genus3 genus-one bisection.
lessons_before.use: Compute h(T-2R) first. The candidate quotient section intersects the inherited image in h(T-2R)/4-1; two common tangencies require at least4, hence height at least20. For exact equality fields, keep both ordinate signs. Factor a rational x-equality numerator only as needed and certify each higher-degree factor separately by a monic-integral finite-field gcd witness; verify the entire product.
lessons_before.avoid: Promoting a true halving point or a zero norm determinant to an integral carrier, dropping the sign T=+/-2R, claiming a whole-polynomial modular miss excludes factors, or applying the two-distinct-contact height bound to a diagonal point without its higher jet.
lessons_before.boundary: The fixed P1/P2 Q80 traces and O plus signed source basis supply exactly two nonpole quadratic half fields, both T=2P6 with height8 and reducible interpolation. Higher MW words, other traces, noninherited halves and diagonal contacts are not excluded. Initial26 unresolved whole-polynomial cases were resolved by factor-specific exact witnesses, not treated as positive points.
lessons_before.reopen_when: A new actual quadratic half outside the frozen bank has sufficient inherited distance height and passes integral jet interpolation, residual quartic, literal-character matching and rational-base checks.

lessons_before.title: Use root splitting for large-vector comparisons and stop genus work once a positive primitive witness suffices
lessons_before.when: A positive auxiliary has a large vector outside a high-rank root lattice and generic PARI automorphism or isometry enumeration overflows.
lessons_before.use: Split into the root lattice and its rational orthogonal complement, normalize the root Gram to Cartan, enumerate diagram actions and the small complementary automorphisms/isometries, then test integrality on the actual glued lattice. Weyl factors recover automorphism orders. lessons_before.title: Exclude low-degree constant Jacobian pairings before sparse algebra
lessons_before.when: A normalized low-degree three-variable Keller collision candidate is considered.
lessons_before.use: Reject completed supports with a nonlinear univariate coordinate or a nonconstant normal derivative on a coordinate hyperplane. In degree at most ten, a constant nonzero v^T*JF*w is excluded by a triangular source reduction to a plane map of degree at most D^2<=100 and Moh. For normalized maps search the finite bilinear direction incidence. The complete size-eight cover has 17435 univariate, 46 elementary-shear, and one hyperplane-normal-factor orbit. GLDC4 also forces a nonlinear own-variable term in each row and hence a strongly connected three-vertex dependence graph by block triangularity. Missing row or cut conditions require explicit possible repairs; lower-bound repair costs may be summed only when their atom sets are disjoint.
lessons_before.avoid: Discarding a repairable partial support because its current row is univariate or triangular; treating empty direction incidence as a counterexample; applying the D<=10 consequence at unbounded degree.
lessons_before.boundary: The univariate and hyperplane-normal-factor gates are arbitrary-degree necessities. The pairing gate imports Moh's degree-100 plane theorem. The special-form minimum four is for degree-at-most-ten counterexamples admitting a constant nonzero pairing, with a degree-seven stabilized witness; it is not an unrestricted dimension minimum.
lessons_before.reopen_when: The completed candidate passes all three gates, exceeds degree ten for the pairing reduction, or supplies a new plane theorem.

lessons_before.use: Apply GL1, then integrate the scalar Gaussian quadratic. On h(0)!=0 rational-exponential rigidity forces (h-Z*hprime)^2*(h-2Z*v)=h^3 and 2*(h-2Z*v)*r+Z*u^2=0; the root argument forces h constant or linear. On h(0)=0 evaluate the fixed point at zero and retain the separate one-sided branch. In total degree D>=2, use the sufficient 5D-3 pure-moment gate; the quartic failure locus is exactly the linear repair k0+k1*Z.
lessons_before.avoid: Restarting the closed twelve-coefficient cubic architecture, treating a finite prefix as an all-order survivor, or promoting a convenient W-linear frame to an exhaustive ternary normal form.
lessons_before.boundary: The original height-two twelve-moment gate covers its stated architecture. The additional cubic-height Riccati theorem now closes T^3 as well, with a sufficient 35-moment cubic gate. Neither theorem normalizes general W-dependent coupling into the completed family.
lessons_before.reopen_when: The candidate contains omitted cubic terms or a new exact normalization theorem expands coverage.

Use the written finite-point/Riemann-Hurwitz obstruction and the explicit polynomial residual degree bound. lessons_before.avoid: Shifting a divergent cubic Gaussian integral by a singular saddle, assuming analytic convergence, reopening the now-closed pure T^3 chart, or promoting generic degree examples into a universal bound.
lessons_before.boundary: The cubic-height architecture has a sufficient 19D-22 pure gate for D>=3. The additional affine-linear W/T coefficient cubic face is closed with a coarse 92-moment gate. The simultaneous WT/WZ^2 chart, WZT, WT^2, higher W powers and real height four or more remain outside these theorems. lessons_before.boundary: All earlier three-affine and ambient quadratic obstructions remain valid. Two directional partials generating the global unit ideal now force their unique plane to be the cotangent plane, give a globally affine free-variable form and an explicit relative coordinate inverse. The aligned rank-three quadratic kernel branch is exactly the unit-ideal plane endpoint. All affine-hyperplane normal images, under arbitrary source parameterizations, are exactly the singleton-zero orbit, the unit-ideal coordinate orbit, or the isotropic-through-center critical-line branch that forbids unit Hessian. Neither endpoint is resolved. Rank-one aligned fibre attainment is not singleton uniqueness; unaligned two-affine embeddings and nonlinear normal image hypersurfaces remain open with the unrestricted row equation. Polynomial quadratic-similitude saturation is now an additional global gate: if q composed with an ambient polynomial automorphism is a*q, undo it in the same source parameters before classifying retained projections or hyperplane images. The entire saturated three-affine class stays closed; the full-source hyperplane saturation retains exactly the old two endpoints or critical-line obstruction. Explicit unbounded words give zero affine pullbacks and nonlinear image equations while preserving a unit-Hessian quadratic source potential. Raw image nonlinearity is therefore insufficient. No universal rectification or generation of every quadratic symmetry is asserted. The output-base obstruction now includes a linear observable paired with any nondegenerate ambient quadratic, not only ambient coordinate pairs. In all stable dimensions r>=2, generic quadric factoriality and a height-one-compatible monomial filtration make the pencil and denominator arguments global, and smoothness forces the plane Keller base invertible. Thus an intrinsic nonautomorphic cotangent pair cannot have such an ambient extension, even after a certified ambient polynomial automorphism. Direct native A/B encodings of an independent Keller pair collapse to an invertible pair and a coordinate potential. Both plane endpoints and arbitrary other source-pair extensions remain open; no surface-quadric factoriality or embedding rectification is assumed. Relative critical schemes now give a separate global gate. A polynomial section over a constant two-variable base, or a base-compatible smooth curve times A1 with vertical Hessian rank one, forces gradient invertibility under unit Hessian. Consequently every base-only normal graph j=(s,t,h(s,t),H,G) under arbitrary relative free-variable polynomial automorphisms has at most one full critical point under unit Hessian, with no cotangent alignment. Its nonautomorphic members are exactly the two old endpoint source orbits. Native graph members with multiple full critical points have no relative unitization over that fixed base. Arbitrary four-variable source mixing and three genuinely free-dependent unretained coordinates remain open. One proper relative Morse component now suffices: no condition on other components is needed, and a globally proper everywhere-Morse relative projection can only have degree one. Each nonautomorphic component must therefore fail properness or contain vertical degeneracy. However each single condition separately retains exactly JC2. The universal f_M model has relative projection K and vertical Hessian -DK^T*DK, while the finite-free Fermat construction gives every K a proper relative projection with explicit monomial basis and ramification at zero. Its properness is not properness of K. Neither model automatically supplies a compatible closed ambient embedding. The two plane endpoints and unrestricted graph compatibility remain open. Uniform quadratic two-planes now have the same unique-plane rigidity under nonautomorphy as affine ones: any genuinely quadratic constant two-plane or two distinct quadratic planes closes the candidate. This classifies every fibre-affine two-affine embedding j=(s,t,b+A*w) in all base degrees. Global source generation requires a polynomial left inverse of A; generic rank is not enough. All unit-Hessian members have at most one full critical point. Arbitrary nonlinear free helpers and nonaligned potentials of free degree at least three remain open. Only the singleton-zero endpoint survives for these positive images. Actual positive linear source weights would close gradient invertibility, but image invariance alone does not supply that hypothesis after nonlinear source changes. Other nonlinear images and both plane endpoints remain open. The output-base gate now admits arbitrary degrees for both ambient observables: a smooth scheme-theoretic codimension-two complete intersection of their highest forms at infinity forces any carried Keller pair invertible. lessons_before.use: Search the surviving coefficient weights for a coprime pair and solve rv-su=+/-1 with nonnegative exponents, yielding a polynomial monomial section. lessons_before.avoid: Assuming nonlinear source invariance of Hessians, demanding a whole graph-independent curve when one first jet suffices, replacing the specialized coordinate pair by a merely Keller pair, inferring line injectivity from a singleton zero, or treating finite controls as a proof of the imported theorem.
lessons_before.boundary: All earlier three-affine and ambient quadratic obstructions remain valid. Two directional partials generating the global unit ideal now force their unique plane to be the cotangent plane, give a globally affine free-variable form and an explicit relative coordinate inverse. The aligned rank-three quadratic kernel branch is exactly the unit-ideal plane endpoint. All affine-hyperplane normal images, under arbitrary source parameterizations, are exactly the singleton-zero orbit, the unit-ideal coordinate orbit, or the isotropic-through-center critical-line branch that forbids unit Hessian. Neither endpoint is resolved. Rank-one aligned fibre attainment is not singleton uniqueness; unaligned two-affine embeddings and nonlinear normal image hypersurfaces remain open with the unrestricted row equation. Polynomial quadratic-similitude saturation is now an additional global gate: if q composed with an ambient polynomial automorphism is a*q, undo it in the same source parameters before classifying retained projections or hyperplane images. The entire saturated three-affine class stays closed; the full-source hyperplane saturation retains exactly the old two endpoints or critical-line obstruction. Explicit unbounded words give zero affine pullbacks and nonlinear image equations while preserving a unit-Hessian quadratic source potential. Raw image nonlinearity is therefore insufficient. No universal rectification or generation of every quadratic symmetry is asserted. The output-base obstruction now includes a linear observable paired with any nondegenerate ambient quadratic, not only ambient coordinate pairs. In all stable dimensions r>=2, generic quadric factoriality and a height-one-compatible monomial filtration make the pencil and denominator arguments global, and smoothness forces the plane Keller base invertible. Thus an intrinsic nonautomorphic cotangent pair cannot have such an ambient extension, even after a certified ambient polynomial automorphism. Direct native A/B encodings of an independent Keller pair collapse to an invertible pair and a coordinate potential. Both plane endpoints and arbitrary other source-pair extensions remain open; no surface-quadric factoriality or embedding rectification is assumed. Relative critical schemes now give a separate global gate. A polynomial section over a constant two-variable base, or a base-compatible smooth curve times A1 with vertical Hessian rank one, forces gradient invertibility under unit Hessian. Consequently every base-only normal graph j=(s,t,h(s,t),H,G) under arbitrary relative free-variable polynomial automorphisms has at most one full critical point under unit Hessian, with no cotangent alignment. Its nonautomorphic members are exactly the two old endpoint source orbits. Native graph members with multiple full critical points have no relative unitization over that fixed base. Arbitrary four-variable source mixing and three genuinely free-dependent unretained coordinates remain open. One proper relative Morse component now suffices: no condition on other components is needed, and a globally proper everywhere-Morse relative projection can only have degree one. Each nonautomorphic component must therefore fail properness or contain vertical degeneracy. However each single condition separately retains exactly JC2. The universal f_M model has relative projection K and vertical Hessian -DK^T*DK, while the finite-free Fermat construction gives every K a proper relative projection with explicit monomial basis and ramification at zero. Its properness is not properness of K. Neither model automatically supplies a compatible closed ambient embedding. The two plane endpoints and unrestricted graph compatibility remain open. Uniform quadratic two-planes now have the same unique-plane rigidity under nonautomorphy as affine ones: any genuinely quadratic constant two-plane or two distinct quadratic planes closes the candidate. This classifies every fibre-affine two-affine embedding j=(s,t,b+A*w) in all base degrees. Global source generation requires a polynomial left inverse of A; generic rank is not enough. Alignment follows under nonautomorphy, a rank-three helper quadratic closes unconditionally, and lower ranks force a base-only helper and the two old endpoints. All unit-Hessian members have at most one full critical point. Arbitrary nonlinear free helpers and nonaligned potentials of free degree at least three remain open. Nonlinear isotropic-ideal image graphs now have explicit global quadratic isometries to hyperplanes, with arbitrary coefficients in unchanged variables and all source parameterizations. Compatible positive linear ambient weights give a constructive recognition gate: a smooth invariant image either has an isotropic tangent normal forbidding unit Hessian, or its lower-weight nonlinear terms admit a weighted Euler shear to the nonisotropic hyperplane. Only the singleton-zero endpoint survives for these positive images. Actual positive linear source weights would close gradient invertibility, but image invariance alone does not supply that hypothesis after nonlinear source changes. Other nonlinear images and both plane endpoints remain open. lessons_before.title: Separate smooth trace isotropy, good generators and extension-field versality
lessons_before.when: Eliminating two coefficients of a universal Keller compiler, importing Hermite-Joubert results, or claiming a complexity minimum from arithmetic existence.
lessons_before.use: For N>=7 impose Tr(theta)=Tr(theta^2)=0. A point outside the trace radical makes the quadric rational, hence its primitive-and-denominator good open has points over infinite fields. Use weights5,8 in rank seven and weights5,6 thereafter. For universality over all extensions use the binary block trace form; Brassil--Reichstein makes it exact when N is invertible. The sqrt(-14) rank-seven vector and Duncan lower bound give an actual target-dimension minimum.
lessons_before.avoid: Calling a fixed-field u-invariant or number-field local-global result field-versal, accepting a scalar radical point as a good generator, treating minimum dimension as canonical descent, or using the new septic first/third-trace covariant without checking its remaining weights6,8 and denominator open.
lessons_before.boundary: Characteristic two is excluded. N>=7 is required for the displayed polynomial sections. Binary necessity is imported only when N is invertible; modular ranks retain a sufficient nonconstant-vector condition. Quadratic family sections are etale-local in general, not automatically Zariski-local. The N-6 stable-class defect is construction-specific and characteristic zero. The recent septic paper proves its characteristic-zero field-extension theorem; its wider announced finite-etale theorem is not used as a proved input.
lessons_before.reopen_when: A different compiler handles negative binary-test cases or low-rank A3 universality; a modular smooth-locus necessity theorem is proved; or a receiver forgetting the good line passes the inertia and fixed-space tests and supplies fixed-affine-space landing.

lessons_before.title: Use a common spatial bound instead of demanding h termination
lessons_before.when: A full formal quantization of a noninvertible polynomial symplectic map is available and the remaining issue is a finite Weyl realization.
lessons_before.use: Prove one finite spatial degree bound across all formal coefficients. The images then belong to a finite-PBW algebra over K[[t]], whose generic fiber is A_n(K((t))). Injective classical reduction preserves coefficient valuation, so generic surjectivity would force a classical polynomial inverse. Equivalently, seek horizontal membership of the classical point in a finite-degree full-relation scheme; ramified formal arcs suffice. The bounded-degree automorphism locus is closed using the field inverse-degree bound, and Artin approximation applies once there are finitely many spatial coefficients.
lessons_before.avoid: Requiring a terminating h series or evaluation specifically at h=1, inferring intrinsic unboundedness from a chosen formal representative, conflating the h=0 map with prescribed Frobenius center maps, or applying reduced-ring inverse bounds to nilpotent jet rings.
lessons_before.boundary: QFL2 is a conditional all-rank criterion, not a common bound for Long's map, a produced Weyl counterexample or a reduction of arbitrary DC2 to one classical seed. Exact controls verify the category distinctions; the generic-fiber and finite-type statements use written proofs.
lessons_before.reopen_when: An actual full lift admits a structural finite spatial carrier, or a gauge-invariant obstruction proves failure of every such carrier across all degrees.

lessons_before.title: Use arithmetic center compatibility to exclude complete cotangent and shear word classes
lessons_before.when: A classical symplectic map has a proved or explicitly assumed arithmetic nonlifting theorem and a proposed construction uses Keller cotangent lifts or elementary canonical changes.
lessons_before.use: Prove the Frobenius center formula for each generator and retain it under composition. Inverse-Jacobian Keller derivations have zero restricted p-th iterate, so their crystalline p-th powers have exactly the cotangent center symbols. Gradient shears are exact by the p-power formula; odd-characteristic linear canonical changes are compatible. A finite word has one common arithmetic model, independent of its degree or length.
lessons_before.avoid: Searching longer cotangent/shear words for Long after assuming the nonlifting theorem, or treating that exclusion as an obstruction to every bounded formal lift with the same h=0 reduction.
lessons_before.boundary: QFL3 is conditional on the October2026 preprint's arithmetic nonlifting theorem. It excludes the specified arithmetic-compatible class only; general polynomial symplectic coordinate changes and bounded formal lifts without prescribed arithmetic support are not included.
lessons_before.reopen_when: The external theorem changes, or a proposed construction demonstrably changes the required arithmetic center map or lies outside the stated generator class.
