lessons_before.title: Test trace invariants on iterated collision-axis points before seeking a singular frame
lessons_before.when: A normalized bounded-degree collision family is conjugated by a parameter-dependent linear matrix fixing e1.
lessons_before.use: Evaluate trace JH(t*e1) and trace JH(H(t*e1)) at a fixed rational t. These are polynomial functions of map coefficients and invariant under every such conjugation. A pole at the proposed endpoint excludes any finite coefficientwise frame limit, even if individual characteristic polynomials along the straight collision axis stay finite. Check full Laurent polynomials independently from the original map and derivatives.
lessons_before.avoid: Treating failed diagonal scaling as an obstruction to all frames; assuming finite trace and characteristic coefficients on the straight axis suffice to make an arbitrary frame possible; revisiting a route after an invariant pole has closed it.
lessons_before.boundary: KFRAME3 excludes both endpoints of one specified nonzero-target pair family: trace JH(2e1) has leading864*k^2 at infinity and trace JH(H(2e1)) has leading -49460507836416/k^3 at zero. Natural and canonical-axis diagonal tests are retained as discovery evidence. This does not exclude other pair families or finite-parameter support drops and does not alter [10,48].
lessons_before.reopen_when: The collision pair family changes, extra parameters co-vary, or the permitted transformations go beyond linear conjugation preserving the normalized collision axis.

lessons_before.title: Classify all mates of a quadratic scalar operator before searching partner orders
lessons_before.when: A finite Weyl lift reduces to scalar differential operators over an algebraic coefficient curve, with an exact order-two member or a unit quadratic member over a differential valuation ring.
lessons_before.use: Use QSO2 to write every mate as A(P)+Q1 with differential-constant A and order-one Q1. Its all-hierarchy proof derives integer indicial exponents from commuting KdV flows and formal selfadjointness, so odd orders at least three are excluded uniformly. If the quadratic leading coefficient is a valuation unit, subtract even powers integrally; an odd reduction of order at least three is impossible for every generic partner order. For a bounded full Long lift with exact R, the actual retained S,T localize to orders2,3, so S must acquire momentum order at least three.
lessons_before.avoid: Increasing only T's order while keeping S quadratic in the exact-R bounded class; treating a finite resonance census as an all-order proof; searching more coefficient degrees, poles, genera or covers within the excluded category; conflating the degree-five QRT seed with Long's actual scalar orders.
lessons_before.boundary: QSO2 assumes scalar finite-order operators over a generic algebraic coefficient function field. Every positive even partner order is possible via Airy plus a polynomial in P. The valued statement requires differential stability and a unit quadratic leading coefficient. Formal series with unbounded coefficient degrees need not be generically algebraic. No bounded normalization fixes a general deformed R, and no theorem keeps S quadratic in every bounded full lift. QPA1 further excludes every low-order source normalization of the completed exact-R fiber image, not only the displayed S,T pair; a new source shear cannot restore an order at most two there. QPL1 is an explicit full polynomial-coefficient formal Long lift with all six relations, fixed momentum orders0,2,3,5 and a scalar quadratic energy. Its PI coefficients have unbounded spatial support and lie outside the generic algebraic coefficient category. Thus full global admission and finite scalar orders do not remove that field hypothesis. Its S coefficient degrees8n-1 prove growth of this family, not of every formal representative. QPH1 constructs a full finite two-by-two phase representation but its left rank is two, not QMC1 rank one, and its second classical branch has an X=0 pole. Its phase form has no algebraic branch summand for any nonconstant finite polynomial g_h, by absolute irreducibility of a nonsingular polynomial connection; the original quadratic case also has a weighted order2/3 proof. Formal extraction gives a second global Long lift with exact S coefficient degree10n-1 and momentum order n. A linear-g example has a different finite scalar realization despite phase nonsplitting, so this excludes the chosen phase construction, not every algebraization or full quantum representative. QKR1 supplies an all-rank cyclic-cover budget r>=(1-1/e)N+irr_0; N>2r excludes cyclic power splitting and, with one finite puncture, all finite covers. Boundary delta factors add inverse-Fourier rank. A genuinely splitting all-degree family S=g(a)+2v has inverse rank deg(g)+1, but its quadratic Long branch fails QSO2. QVM1 excludes every finite mate, on all finite coefficient covers, when S has v-leading term v*H(a), deg H>=2 and root-multiplicity gcd one, with arbitrary lower-growth terms. The candidate v*(2+h*a^3)+4a-3r*a^2 passes N6/r3 and branch extraction but fails this all-order mate test. Proper-power H, different leading faces and nonpositional first images remain outside it. No actual Long carrier follows. QVL1 transports repeated roots to nonlinear ordinary infinity limits and closes all proper-power v-linear repairs when lower coefficients are bounded. Together with QVM1, every leading H of degree>=2 is excluded in that entire Laurent class, with arbitrary finite partner order and algebraic coefficient covers. Euler limits and finite Newton support certificates give further tests. A remaining exact-R scalar Long model in the v-linear rational Laurent class has H degree<=1 and inverse-Fourier rank at least four, by QSO2 and a positive infinity Newton contribution. The family 2v*(1+h*a)^k+4a-3ra^2 is excluded for every k>=2, even though k3 passes N6/r3 and branch extraction. Nonlinear-limit commuting Darboux algebras cannot supply a scalar generator, but other operators in larger idealizers remain outside that assertion. Other leading faces, fractional positive lower growth for nonprimitive H, H degree<=1 and nonpositional first images remain open. QZM1 gives a zero-mode cokernel test with finite-cover trace retraction and covariance under actual finite algebra automorphisms, provided the module is transported too. A new position localization can kill the vector and is not justified by trace. It excludes v*(lambda*a+mu)+G(a) for every nonconstant polynomial G and every finite scalar mate order or algebraic coefficient cover. Combined with QVL1, the pure separable class v*H(a)+G(a) with both H and G nonconstant is closed; the leading-linear rank-four cubic and derivative-tuned cubic are excluded. QPC1 subsequently closes the H-constant nonlinear-G case by a universal p-power coefficient. The complete pure polynomial v*H(a)+G(a) Long form is therefore excluded, including every finite momentum degree and coefficient cover. Additional negative-v corrections, genuine mixed coefficients, other leading faces and deformed first images remain outside this classification. Conditional global pair transport clears c(R) and requires [R,T]=0; it neither admits every chart formula nor identifies QRF2 with this new class. QPC1 also gives linear trace descent for a fixed operator mate and the necessary matrix-fiber condition chi_S derivative zero. Scalar p-centrality requires central degree p and fails for general phase matrices; no arbitrary carrier exclusion follows. QAD1 supplies an arbitrary-scalar mixed-coefficient admission test: nonzero Adler periods exclude even bounded-above PDO mates, whereas finite differential existence is exactly constant-linear membership in the full almost-commuting defect span. It identifies a characteristic-zero residue proportional to QPC1 gamma_n. Vanishing periods construct only a PDO mate, as the harmonic control demonstrates; neither an h-pole dressing nor a finite defect prefix supplies a finite full carrier. This does not compare arbitrary Fourier completions, identify QRF2 or cover nonscalar matrix actions. The finite leading-divisor gate is stronger than the first PDO period test: if gcd(operator order, all leading-coefficient zero/pole orders)=1, the entire base low-order commutator image is zero by finite power subtraction. This excludes every nonconstant squarefree polynomial leading coefficient, with arbitrary mixed lower terms and all finite coefficient covers. Prime operator orders over K(v) require a scalar times an nth power leading coefficient. The separate rational leading PDO equation Qprime-(Hprime/(n*H))*Q=v tests algebraic primitive exactness; its squarefree degree>=3 exclusion strengthens to PDO mates. A passing leading condition remains necessary, and nonscalar matrix carriers are not classified. QST1 separates rational and spectral admission. Any nonzero Adler period excludes the entire rational operator division ring and makes the universal spectral class nontorsion; the G(a)+mu*v first period is explicit in all degrees. This blocks every rational conjugate and the corresponding actual rank-one projective pair orbit without a scalar free frame. Fixed rational mate equations descend through finite algebraic coefficient covers by monic-denominator Galois averaging. Constant-coefficient G has instead a critical-value torsion annihilator and a rational mate. Zero Adler periods are insufficient for rational admission: a torus residue excludes harmonic/Euler functional classes even with arbitrary operator denominators and identity spectators. Finite primitive-divisor and ordinary infinity exclusions must not be silently promoted to rational ones. No arbitrary moving spectral coefficient localization, nonlinear Galois descent or universal Long rational normalization is proved.

lessons_before.title: Check left finiteness at infinity for the chosen algebraic graph model
lessons_before.when: Formal graph quantization or algebraization supplies a coherent or holonomic bimodule whose completion is free from the left.
lessons_before.use: Require an effective left lattice for the chosen model. The explicit localization q=1-t^2*x has strict left-module chain A*q^-k, but q becomes invertible in every parameter jet. Its cyclic graph is coherent and generically holonomic, so those properties alone do not close the finite-realization gap. Use QPG1 central patching after proving generic finite projectivity and an admitted C-frame; if the generic module is rank-one free, its integral frame follows automatically. For generic rank-one full actions, QVA1 now supplies C-admission from Gauss-regularity and the intended shadow; it need not be assumed separately.
lessons_before.avoid: Inferring generic left finite generation from formal left freeness, coherence, holonomicity or smooth diagonal support at the special fiber; declaring intrinsic nonalgebraizability from a bad chosen model.
lessons_before.boundary: QGM1's completed graph is formally inner-equivalent to the regular graph and has a left-free alternate algebraization. The failure concerns effectivity of an arbitrary algebraization; the desired existence of a good model for Long remains unknown. QSC1 proves Cent_classical(R,S)=K[R,S] and commutativity of the full formal joint centralizer for every commuting Long deformation, including nonpositional first images. Faithful finite/corner and QMC1 full-carrier endomorphism algebras inherit commutativity. Global spectral Koszul classes exactly test the two individual conjugates; if they vanish, one algebraic curvature class exactly tests flat completion. All spectral fibers can pass while the global class fails, and a formally exact curvature can have nonzero rational double residue. If both matrix positions are scalar, normalized matrix trace scalarizes a full completion without degree growth. This does not scalarize genuinely matrix-valued positions or free a projective carrier, identify QRF2, or construct a finite Long lift. QFC1 gives a positive algebraic completion theorem conditional on actual centralizer module finiteness and integral individual mates. Its connection argument removes supports escaping to t=1/h, where a finite module can be h-divisible despite zero special fiber. This is not a theorem that a formally free graph model has a finite-left algebraization. QGC1 now removes the closure saturation gap under actual admission. The correct ordinary-parameter classical graph makes divided left/right differences preserve every finite valuation-level residue lattice, and some level is full by Ore clearing. Equivariant split-abelian carriers of the correct torsion-free special rank can instead be repaired by finite character shifts, for every parameter order. Genuine constant-cover Weyl carriers show that saturation itself is false even with all right relations and the correct identity graph. The ideal A_R*x+A_R*t shows why special torsion and set-theoretic graph support are insufficient. No formal-existence-to-finite-carrier theorem or obstruction to the ordinary rank-one Long graph is inferred. QIR1 removes lattice ambiguity only after the rational full action is fixed. Its generic full finite lattice is unique, and rank-one special graph lattices differ by central parameter powers, for every ramification order. A formally equivalent action can be rationally different, so a bad formal algebraization still proves no intrinsic nonlifting. QTC1 gives an intrinsic nonfinite boundary of a natural construction, conditional on an original finite carrier: its source-balanced tensor with the target dual reduces to the classical self-product. The off-diagonal projection is nonfinite for every noninvertible etale self-map of affine space in characteristic zero. This is a failure of reverse-composition admission, not a contradiction to the original carrier or evidence of generic nonfiniteness by itself. QRA1 supplies finite global matrix models whose special module has rank greater than one and a ramified spectral cover. Their finite action is real, but the intended rank-one Long graph does not follow. Exact physical primitive admission at the zero-energy divisor forces a nonintegral inverse. Leading factorization alone is not enough: power companions need a nonzero quantum correction which releases the primitive. QFR1 detects a punctual class erased by localization. QUR1 repolarizes the single monic physical normalization to a rank-two connection and excludes its regular formal lift at every ramification order, including sub-quantum mixing. Its exact q-local and z-local full connections require poles. This does not give an intrinsic obstruction for the different smooth rank-one Long graph. QPG1 supplies central patching once a finite projective generic action has an actual rank-one C-frame, C=Ahat[1/t], with regular full graph images. No bound on positive spatial support of that overlap frame is needed. Coherence or completed division-ring equivalence does not supply generic finiteness or C-admission. Finite algebraization existence is equivalent among full formal lifts of one classical map after finite exact shears and inner module isomorphisms; chosen representatives can still have unbounded coefficients. QVA1 removes a separately proved C-frame once the generic action is finite projective of rank one and Gauss-regular with the intended shadow. The saturated initial ideal and full Hamiltonian residue frame force formal freeness. QGM1 still fails generic left finiteness. A rational full tuple with a polynomial classical shadow can also lack a finite invariant generic carrier, as the noninteger logarithmic control shows.
lessons_before.reopen_when: A boundary or lattice theorem proves left finiteness for the selected algebraization, or a gauge-invariant criterion controls the existence of some good algebraization.

lessons_before.title: Use the relative critical determinant before searching another nonlinear parameter word
lessons_before.when: A graph potential is reparameterized by an actual polynomial automorphism of its retained duals over one free-base variable.
lessons_before.use: Transport the whole relative critical scheme by the inverse and restrict the Hessian determinant there. The nonlinear chain-rule correction vanishes modulo the relative gradient ideal, so the determinant changes only by a field unit square. For y=R(x,p) use the exact curve 2*x*R+3=0, its critical-value derivation and -32*L*N^2*x^6*R_p^2*delta^2(D). For affine-in-p y=a*p+b, the universal denominator and infinity orders close every degree without a word search. HC4MYGR0/1/2/3 add closed affine critical-component geometry and the generic-fibre Euler calculation, closing arbitrary nonlinear y boundary-root graphs and opposite x=a(y)*p+b(y) with a(0) nonzero. HC4MYGS0/1/2/3 add the preserved whole critical target-line map, an all-degree pole classification and the Chau/Orevkov plane-degree obstruction, excluding every nonzero-a opposite affine-p graph and reducing the full family to its base-only unit-ideal endpoint. HC4MYGN0/1/2/3 add empty-critical-scheme/Euler, initial Newton-face and finite smooth ramification gates, closing every separated y=a(x)*P(p)+b(x) in all degrees without Tang. lessons_before.title: Require algebraic dual nonvanishing and an actual scalar polarization
lessons_before.when: A bounded formal lift or coherent graph model is being used to claim finite left realization or apply a scalar differential-order obstruction.
lessons_before.use: For an algebraically torsion-free rank-one module over a noetherian Ore domain, prove Hom_A(M,A) nonzero; this is equivalent to left finite generation. Track algebraic versus completed duals and the boundary inverse-limit class. For scalar reduction, prove existence of a finite algebraic normal form with actual local nilpotence and the required order profile. Use QPG1 central patching after proving generic finite projectivity and an admitted C-frame; if the generic module is rank-one free, its integral frame follows automatically. For generic rank-one full actions, QVA1 now supplies C-admission from Gauss-regularity and the intended shadow; it need not be assumed separately.
lessons_before.avoid: Inferring local nilpotence from nilpotence in every parameter jet, inferring raw order preservation from boundedness, replacing an algebraic dual section by a formal one, or applying finite-generation claims without checking rank one and torsion-freeness.
lessons_before.boundary: QEF1's degree-one canonical shear has topologically nilpotent but not locally nilpotent graph constraint, and QGM1 has zero algebraic dual with nonzero completed dual. These chosen models or representatives have better normalizations, so no intrinsic nonliftability follows. A free left frame remains an extra condition. The bad boundary model is simple and holonomic generically, so standard graph-module simplicity does not repair algebraic dual nonvanishing. QIR1 makes a finite full rank-one graph carrier projective over K[[t]] itself. This does not make it free. A fixed rational full action has a unique generic full finite lattice; a rational frame makes its right matrices polynomial exactly when that lattice is free. A formal dual or formal comparison does not supply the required rational frame. QPG1 replaces a separate integral lattice construction by central patching if the generic module is finite projective and its full action has an admitted rank-one frame over C=Ahat[1/t]. Generic rank-one freeness then implies integral freeness. Formal dual nonvanishing or a division-ring intertwiner alone still does not supply those inputs. QVA1 moves the substantive existence test to a finite generic rank-one invariant carrier with the intended Gauss shadow. Its full regular action automatically produces a formal C-frame, then QPG1 patches integrally. Rational pairs p+a*r(x),x show finite generic generation remains nonautomatic: admission requires r=Hprime+fprime/f, with polynomial H and rational f.
lessons_before.reopen_when: A nonzero dual section actually descends with effective boundary control, or a proved algebraic normalization realizes the scalar hypotheses for every relevant gauge class.

lessons_before.title: Remove redundant carrier directions before further cubic degree reduction
lessons_before.when: A stable cubic reduction introduces many auxiliary carrier variables.
lessons_before.use: Compute how top coordinates and all retained carrier outputs depend on carrier directions. Retain independent combinations, apply the same linear change to the corresponding targets, and check whether complementary outputs become identity coordinates plus polynomials of retained inputs. If so, source shears remove those directions exactly without raising retained degree. Verify the complete symbolic determinant using an explicitly checked nilpotent carrier-block inverse, and transport full collision points.
lessons_before.avoid: Calling every coordinate-graph slice cubic; conflating ordinary degree with generic fibre degree; comparing term counts across different collision normalizations; claiming a beam search or failed family of target corrections proves minimum dimension.
lessons_before.boundary: The exact17/58 and13/42 constructions remain verified, but BCR2 and BCRDB1 already supplied12-variable cubic maps. BCRDB1's count40 dominates both experiments; KCUB3 improves that established map to an integral36-term form. These older construction routes are historical method evidence, not current size improvements. All bounded beam, slice and rational-line limits remain local rather than optimality proofs. KCUB29 now closes all raw linear carrier-relation subspace graphs of the savedK in the standard highest-pivot parametrization, including simultaneous and cross-weight relations:13 raw occurrences are sharp in the whole class and fixed-dimension degree minima match the literal subsets. Minimal4/5/7-dimensional degree6/5/4 families have sharp15/17/23 terms. General nonlinear graph parametrizations, later target repairs and affine output sparsification remain outside this result.
lessons_before.reopen_when: A further construction uses fewer than12 variables, improves the36-term target under comparable cubic/tangent normalization, or supplies a genuinely additional property absent from BCRDB1/KCUB3.

lessons_before.title: Check inertia, fixed spaces and actual affine landing before using quotient dimension
lessons_before.when: Building a canonical finite-etale Keller receiver, extending the compiler quotient, substituting target-dependent coefficients, or claiming a smaller affine map from a stack atlas.
lessons_before.use: Use the trace-filter receiver when whole affine-space geometric source fibres and a canonical bundle self-map suffice. Unit, multiplication and trace glue over arbitrary Z[1/(2N)!]-schemes, including nonreduced bases; source and target are the same specified bundle. UAROOTSYM1 groups these into equivariant orbit factors; a transitive action on all blocks has complete fixed-target fibre T0^N and cannot give the natural N-label cover. UASELFCTRL1 closes one affine coefficient line with arbitrary own-source polynomial controls, and even rational controls if the WHOLE output map extends polynomially: only retained-signal effective profiles survive. UASELFLAUR1 supplies the exact nonlinear response and reciprocal-Riccati/pole proof. UASELFFORMAL1 provides all-order formal marked deformations and a genuine source denominator as the concrete next integration gate. UANATIVE2GEN1 replaces every finite native list by two unique effective source controls without changing the map. UAAFFINER1 closes all one-block affine-r controls and gives a fixed-size determinant equation for the nonlinear remainder. UASIGFIELD1 identifies stable signal-field normalizers as weighted compiler scalings plus vertical Keller maps. UAETALEGAUGE1 says the marked finite/formal examples are unique source coordinate changes, with necessarily unbounded source degrees in the explicit scalar family. UAQFSAT1 supplies polynomial descent for any dominant quasi-finite affine-space self-map. UANATIVEORBIT1 classifies the full native profile-coordinate orbit: affine Cout, generic affine-pair reducibility and signal-field-respecting stable profile equivalence all give the unique shear ideal (a^5*c^3). Its finite polynomial-r degree reduction closes the whole quadratic sector. UACUBICDESC1 tests an actual old cubic factor by reducing each output to its three fixed field-basis coefficients; no target-degree ansatz is needed. UAPROFFACT1 upgrades the native profile orbit to complete rational factor rigidity: recovery through ANY retained profile forces its unique target shear, by the already imported published HC4MYGL0 line theorem. UAPLANEATOM1 makes every such completion plane-indecomposable and excludes signal-retaining whole factors whose intermediate coordinates also extend across its hyperbola. UARELPLANE1 cancels a plane Keller target whenever the final curve is a closed embedding, with no boundary-extension hypothesis. UASIGFACT1 closes EVERY native signal-retaining whole factorization, including negative Laurent-r sectors. UAINTERSURF1 replaces the former pole gate by the exact generic intermediate surface under arbitrary stabilization mixing: noninvertible target stages require a NON-PLANE fibre with the stated smooth complete-intersection, tangent, curve, unit, divisor and saturation constraints. UAPRIMUNIT1 closes the cofinite etale surface class with primitive source unit. UAUNITFACT1 uses published whole polynomial root closure to make every nonconstant geometric unit primitive and invert the source stage. A proper arbitrary stabilized native intermediate is therefore GEOMETRICALLY UNIT-FREE and non-plane, has arithmetic UFD ring and an all-irreducible-constant-fibre whole signal component. At every chain cut the unit lattice is either full Z or zero, dropping once at the first noninvertible prefix. UALOGVOL1 closes all nonnegative-logarithmic intermediates after a noninvertible source stage, by the actual r^2 whole-volume multiplier and log pullback on boundary resolutions. UAGEOPIC1 then forces NONZERO geometric Picard group for proper native factors, while its retained-field Galois invariant subgroup is ZERO by rational-point-normalized descent. UADANVOL1 excludes every ordinary smooth Danielewski exponent-one surface by a volume period; higher exponents have an explicit regular primitive. UAPLANECHART1 tests the ENTIRE carried line against EVERY open A2 chart: containment in any one inverts the whole target. Formal etaleness still makes all its finite/formal neighborhoods standard. UADANCHART1 exposes exact simultaneous Keller gluing on the classical Danielewski atlas, a JC(2)-level burden, nondividing ruling degrees and multi-root contact constraints. Its sharp beta-integral contact family fails geometric injectivity in every exponent. UAARITHRULING1 turns ANY actually descended affine-line ruling into a finite geometric plane atlas: arithmetic fibres are integral and geometric fibres reduced. A proper native factor would give JC(2) counterexamples and its whole curve must hit two components of one split fibre. UAPRODUCTTOPO1 uses source Euler characteristic1 and pi1=Z^N on actual product leaves to exclude finite proper stages and force a finite-index abelian intermediate subgroup with index dividing source degree. UAMLFACTOR1 identifies the trivial-geometric-ML branch exactly with target invertibility in the native class. UAAFFDESC1 PROVES uniqueness and descent of every geometric AFFINE-type ruling: center at the rational point, take a nonzero weighted Galois trace in its stable coordinate line, and contract the actual volume to obtain a retained-field additive action.
lessons_before.avoid: Inferring an affine-space source from a coarse quotient or a fieldwise trivialization; testing only tangent modules; asserting that the rank-N marked fibre determines degree-M monodromy; or retaining an unproved open landing gate for the constructed trace bundle model. Do not search larger polynomial degrees in these closed rank-one cubic-return or retained-output coupling classes, or confuse a cyclic dependence graph with the removal of an intermediate field. Do not replace a non-descended Schur matrix by an ordinary time Jacobian without proving descent, or confuse generic covering degree with total coordinate degree. Do not deepen root-only polynomial profile degrees while retaining every first signal, equate ordinary nilpotence with vanishing of all principal minors, or read apparent coefficient-list cycles before effective cancellation. Do not freeze the scalar response at coefficient zero, infer polynomial integration from every finite Keller jet or a full formal series, or treat a rational source-open formula as an entire affine map. Do not add more native indices as independent control channels, infer map-degree bounds from the normal-form indices, treat finite/formal source-coordinate existence as a polynomial family, or confuse sigma composed F with a retained first output. Do not treat nonlinear-r B output or arbitrarily high marked contact as a new stable class: explicit whole polynomial target shears already have both. Do not infer atomicity from a nonzero cubic descent remainder, or replace native polynomial-module membership by the source jets alone. Do not reopen the conditional native degree-greater-than-one after-profile branch: it is now empty. Do not deepen searches for polynomial plane decompositions of the completed native map, apply the Keller line theorem directly to its nonconstant Jacobian, or infer stable full-map atomicity from plane indecomposability. Do not reopen the former intermediate boundary-pole route: it is now closed in the entire signal-retaining class. Do not identify a generic intermediate fibre with A2 without proof, assume abstractly isomorphic source surfaces imply trivial factor degrees, or treat a generic etale formula as a whole polynomial factor. Do not reopen the nonconstant-unit intermediate branch or allow a proper finite-index unit lattice in a whole Keller factor. Do not substitute a generic J_d surface cover for whole power descent, remove the retained node, infer geometric factoriality from arithmetic localization, or claim that a unit-free surface has been excluded. Do not reopen nonnegative-log surfaces, geometrically factorial proper native factors or invariant geometric divisor classes. Do not import the finite torus-domination classification into our nonfinite maps, use the obsolete two-surface log-zero list, or turn an exact primitive into an etale plane pair. Higher-power primitive formulas and lattice models do not construct either arrow. Do not identify the raw singular retained-base spread with an actual whole Keller intermediate. Do not turn standard formal curve neighborhoods into a global plane chart, glue plane automorphisms into a non-plane etale target, or call the classical chart-to-JC(2) reduction new. Do not substitute local contacts for the whole closed embedded curve, or search increasing degrees inside the excluded beta-integral family or low/divisibly reducible ruling sector. Do not replace geometric ruling existence after finite extension by descent to K0, transfer arithmetic UFD across that extension, or accept multiple geometric components with multiplicity>1 in a descended ruling. Do not fill a nonfinite surface completion with finitely many points, infer positive Euler integral from nonnegative sheet loss, or apply product-leaf topology to a changed-signal receiver without proving its actual generic fibre. Do not reopen excluded orbifold patterns or the odd-degree two-double sector. Do not treat a unique or Galois-invariant ruling as an unresolved non-descent escape. Do not leave affine-type Galois permutation as an open escape. Do not infer uniqueness from two arbitrary COMPLETE-type rulings, or average different ruling coordinates without checking the generic fibre: the exact trace control is Gm.
lessons_before.boundary: Dimension3N+3, generic degree3^(N+1), coordinate degree4N and volume dimension3N+4 are existence bounds, not minima. V_A can be nontrivial over a scheme. Non-atomicity is proved, while atomic canonical realization remains open. An invariant natural frame is obstructed by faithful split inertia; existential bundle freeness on prescribed bases is separate. The published fixed-scheme all-family no-go still applies. These classifications use characteristic-zero polynomial retained-signal profiles and the named compiler. Any number of controls with rank-one cubic return is closed; non-descended higher-rank return and other compilers are separate. For another auxiliary block rank-one output recovery is equivalent to geometric generic-line connectedness; no general closedness conjecture is silently assumed. Arithmetic atomicity of connected input algebras is not absolute atomicity. Common kernels are proved for all constant ranks; the full selector classification is only one-directional. Higher-rank membership in C[Z,t] is an explicit hypothesis, not a determinant consequence. The full C is not assumed finitely generated or polynomial. Marked divisor identities hold universally; effective degree and absolute atomicity use the stated characteristic-zero field hypotheses. Fixed-signal rank-two source leaves need not be affine planes. A slice does not imply local nilpotence, and stable polynomiality is not an atomicity converse. The root-feedback theorem requires characteristic-zero fields, unchanged first signals and corrections in k[u,sigma,X]. Independent r_i diagonal variables force every principal minor to vanish. Frobenius dependencies and nilpotent coefficient cycles show why positive characteristic and nonreduced bases are excluded. Transitive product-fibre conclusions require transitivity on ALL nonidentity blocks; the trace filter has an extra auxiliary orbit and changes its first signal. Scalar self-feedback rigidity is a one-block affine coefficient-line theorem with a nonzero effective direction in characteristic zero. It permits all own-source channels and rational controls with whole polynomial landing, but says only that EFFECTIVE profiles are retained-signal polynomials; common direction factors may cancel a rational signal control. Curved coefficient families and mutually changing blocks remain outside. Finite-order parameter bases are nonreduced; the formal ring k[P][[lambda]] permits unbounded source degrees and differs from k[[lambda]][P]. The two-control module identity is universal over bases with2 invertible and preserves arbitrary source dependence. Affine-r rigidity and the stable signal-field normalizer use characteristic-zero fields. Affine-r rigidity is a one-block theorem with actual identity parameters and native source jets, not a theorem about mutually changing blocks. Formal-etale source gauges are classical and work over arbitrary nilpotent base ideals; their compatible formal limit can have unbounded source degree. The source-field normalizer leaves a vertical JC(m) problem and does not classify merely retained-output maps or arbitrary coordinate changes moving that field. Formal marked source equivalence permits actual polynomial families with arbitrary generic-degree jumps; it is not a global degree or stable-class invariant. Native orbit rigidity requires characteristic zero, one retained block, polynomial module membership and coordinate operations fixing identity parameters. Its stable equivalence is restricted to source maps normalizing k(u,sigma); unrestricted source changes are outside. A polynomial-r reduction survivor has non-dividing degrees >=2; negative Laurent sectors and genuine cross-block interaction remain open. The fixed dimension-three descent certificate excludes only the old cubic factor when its remainder is nonzero. Quasi-finite saturation is a classical elementary divisor consequence, not a novelty claim. The profile-factor theorem is one block with retained identities and a literal profile first factor; arbitrary source changes remain outside. Plane completion is generic in the signal and covers only nonnegative r powers. Plane indecomposability requires an irreducible Jacobian and an embedded line; its extension to all fields requires GEOMETRIC irreducibility. It does not imply stable whole-map atomicity. A nontrivial signal-retaining factor must have a genuine intermediate boundary pole. Whole-source special-signal landing and signal-moving factors remain open. The saturation overlap has explicit prior public attribution to Trushin Proposition3.1.1. The relative cancellation theorem leaves exactly TWO generic coordinates and requires a whole embedded A1 image; three-dimensional Keller counterexamples show that one curve alone does not invert a higher-dimensional target. It uses only the curve restriction, allowing poles elsewhere. Arbitrary identity stabilization and intermediate mixing are covered by the NON-PLANE generic intermediate-fibre obstruction. This is still a necessary all-factor condition, not full absolute stable atomicity. Intermediate surfaces satisfy BOTH saturation identities, geometrically have unit rank at most1 and their etale arrows miss at most finitely many points. Their abstract shape, smoothness and tangent triviality do not construct a proper factor. Primitive-unit surface rigidity requires characteristic zero, an AFFINE smooth target, cofinite etale image and the actual node. Its whole-factor unit theorem covers arbitrary last outputs with the fixed retained signal, without native jets or Laurent-degree bounds. Proper intermediates have CONSTANT geometric units; the earlier unit-rank-at-most-one route is now CLOSED on the nonconstant side. Whole constant-level irreducibility is not a statement about all further fibres after fixing E_u. Arithmetic UFD over k(u,a) does not prove geometric factoriality. The native NON-PLANE conclusion still requires the UARELPLANE1 embedded-curve witness. The one-way unit drop bounds no later unit-free chain length. CURRENT: a PROPER native intermediate is GEOMETRICALLY UNIT-FREE, has log kappa=-infinity, and has NONZERO geometric Picard group with ZERO retained-field Galois invariants, despite arithmetic UFD. The Picard factor criterion uses the native curve witness and explicitly imported Miyanishi negative-log affine-plane criterion. The log dichotomy and invariant-class vanishing cover every actual whole retained-signal Keller map. Higher-power Danielewski surfaces m>=2 pass exact volume; u has no Keller mate for all m>=1. Required arrows, free tangent frame, global polynomial lift and canonical marks/gluing remain unconstructed. The raw spread a=z^d-u^m*v is excluded globally by its critical zero fibre; only another smooth whole model could realize the same generic surface. CURRENT CHART GATE: the WHOLE carried A1 crosses the boundary of EVERY plane chart in a proper native factor, despite all finite/formal neighborhoods being standard. Any non-plane etale target containing an open A2 yields JC(2) counterexamples on all charts; this remains CONDITIONAL and has Dubouloz2009 precedent. Higher-power Danielewski targets need compatible nonautomorphic pairs surviving at nondividing ruling degrees>=2 and a carried closed embedding meeting two root components with deg Z>=m*N-r+1. Sharp beta-integral contact maps fail geometric injectivity for EVERY m>=2; other multi-root embedded curves remain open. These deductions retain the actual native/witness two-dimensional fibre and entire-curve hypotheses. CURRENT RULING/TOPOLOGY GATE: a retained-field ruling has base A1, integral arithmetic fibres and reduced geometric fibres, hence a finite geometric A2 atlas and a JC(2) burden for proper native targets. Geometric ruling existence does NOT prove descent. The whole carried curve hits two components of some split fibre. On an ACTUAL U^N times A^h leaf both proper arrows are NONFINITE and intermediate pi1 has an abelian subgroup with index DIVIDING source degree. This is virtually cyclic for one block. Multiple fibres of any surjective connected-generic geometric map to A1 are limited to one or two doubles; the two-double case requires EVEN source degree. No silent product hypothesis for the trace receiver or Euler-integral positivity is permitted. Published Galois-invariant/unique-ruling descent already closes that special descent uncertainty: a proper native factor with such a ruling would disprove JC(2). Conditional on JC(2), every geometric ruling must have a NONTRIVIAL Galois orbit of inequivalent rulings. CURRENT DESCENT RESULT: every geometric affine-type ruling of a proper native intermediate is unique and actually descends; its additive action descends too. Conditional on JC(2), only ADDITIVELY RIGID intermediates with COMPLETE-type Galois-permuted P1 rulings remain. Their descent is OPEN. A zero Picard orbit norm does not identify the individual fibrations.
lessons_before.reopen_when: A candidate improves these explicit bounds or proves atomicity with whole-source polynomial landing, complete marked fibre and compatible descent; a different receiver must state which stronger trivialization or symmetry data it provides. An actual candidate leaves the rank-one cubic architecture, for example through non-descended higher-rank return geometry, another compiler or a non-locally-nilpotent auxiliary with constants outside the stable-polynomial criterion, satisfies its whole-source determinant identity, retains the exact complete fibre and gluing, and proves absolute atomicity. In one constant direction, an auxiliary-only canonical escape must be all-inactive and demonstrate a full constant ring outside the stable-polynomial criterion, retaining exact marked fibre and descent. For root feedback, an atomic candidate must leave the all-signal-retaining polynomial root subring class, for example using additional source channels or a changed first output, and still prove the complete marked fibre and atomicity. A proved broader curved/multi-direction or genuine cross-block construction removes the explicit formal scalar denominator on the WHOLE source, retains complete marks and gluing, and proves full-map absolute atomicity. Scalar-line degree sweeps are closed. A two-effective-control native family leaves the scalar-line and affine-r sectors through nonlinear Laurent-r dependence, or another first-output/compiler/cross-block architecture, and proves whole-source polynomial landing, exact canonical marks, gluing and full-map atomicity. A native candidate has Cout genuinely nonlinear, escapes generic profile-coordinate reduction at a non-dividing polynomial-r degree pair or in a negative Laurent sector, and proves the full marked scheme, effective gluing and absence of ALL actual polynomial factors; another compiler or changed first-output architecture remains permitted. A whole-source native construction has genuinely nonlinear Cout and exact canonical marks/gluing; any claimed factor must escape literal profile recovery and, in the polynomial-r sector, polynomial intermediate extension. A genuinely non-plane generic intermediate surface with the exact saturated field model and whole-source realization, a new curve-witness failure or another compiler must be analyzed without assuming JC(2). A proper factor realizes a NON-PLANE geometric generic retained fibre, both field degrees exceed one, and all curve, unit, saturation, divisor and whole-polynomial requirements are certified; or an actual native integration preserves complete canonical marks/gluing and excludes every such factor. A proper generic surface is geometrically unit-free with the exact arithmetic factorial ring, saturated embedded field, whole carried curve and an all-irreducible-constant-fibre intermediate signal; both whole degrees exceed one and the entire map/global marked gluing is certified. Nonconstant-unit and finite-index unit candidates are closed. Produce an actual negative-log unit-free geometrically nonfactorial intermediate with nonzero Picard group and no invariant class, the exact canonical volume and both etale arrows. The u^m*v=z^d-a families with m>=2 are explicit necessary-condition models, not permission for a bounded coefficient sweep or proof of a whole factor. Supply an actual compatible nonautomorphic Keller atlas and a WHOLE multi-root embedded line satisfying all contacts, both cofinite arrows and a different smooth whole spread, or move to a proved intermediate geometry without such a plane chart. Finite/formal neighborhoods and exact primitives alone are insufficient; JC(2) and canonical atomicity are not declared solved. Prove a compatible JC(2)-counterexample atlas in the descended-ruling class, or prove an actual failure of ruling descent retaining all field, curve, volume and whole-source constraints. Respect the nonfinite source-divisor and sheet-loss budget, the dividing-index group constraint and the orbifold multiplicity/parity gates. Full canonical marks, gluing and absolute stable atomicity remain necessary. Prove descent or exclude actual realization of the remaining COMPLETE-type Galois orbit. The affine-type descent subproblem is closed; extend by a new identification argument, not more necessary conditions.

lessons_before.title: Use actual affine critical components and generic-fibre Euler to close nonlinear graph classes
lessons_before.when: A relative critical scheme contains a closed A1 component, possibly even when every computed critical determinant is the same nonzero constant.
lessons_before.use: Under hypothetical nonautomorphy project Tang planes to the single free base. Rank zero has only vertical critical components and generic coordinate fibres of Euler one. Rank one identifies its entire critical scheme with a plane Keller coordinate fibre, where an actual A1 component is rectified and line injectivity gives an inverse. For y=R(x,p) count the two explicit Euler strata to obtain1+r>=2. For opposite affine-p graphs use the boundary line and the separately dominating critical curve. Reducibility then forbids unit Hessian. HC4MYGS0/1/2/3 add the preserved whole critical target-line map, an all-degree pole classification and the Chau/Orevkov plane-degree obstruction, excluding every nonzero-a opposite affine-p graph and reducing the full family to its base-only unit-ideal endpoint. HC4MYGN0/1/2/3 add empty-critical-scheme/Euler, initial Newton-face and finite smooth ramification gates, closing every separated y=a(x)*P(p)+b(x) in all degrees without Tang. HC4MYGM0/1/2/3 remove the whole finite polar and singular locus, require a full polynomial Bezout certificate and complete critical curve, impose an exact reciprocal conductor budget on escapes, and state the necessary entire abstract Keller-fibre realization. HC4MYGW0/1/2/3 add a genus-free whole-curve Euler/pole budget, algebraic differential descent, all quadratic p closure and a whole unbounded-degree family excluded despite passing local critical gates. HC4MYGY0/1/2/3 compare every Euler jump and one entire reciprocal-root product, closing the full positive-p y chart and leaving exactly its base-only nonautomorphic unit-ideal endpoint. HC4MYGX0/1/2/3 extend the global method to opposite nonlinear graphs, closing all simple-boundary and no-escape configurations and forcing at least six distinct critical roots in any remaining nonautomorphic mechanism. HC4MYGZ0/1/2/3 now compare the exceptional base-zero fibre and close both entire positive-p base charts, including every opposite escape; both whole p-only families retain only the base-only unit-ideal nonautomorphic endpoint. HC4MYHA0/1/2/3 extend the closure to every y=R(x,p,q) independent of old r: a general cylindrical-trace criterion combines with the all-degree plane polynomial G=P*(F^2-1)+Q*F and its square suspension, without a generic irreducibility or critical-projection assumption. HC4MYHB0/1/2/3 now use an isolated trace point and its Milnor intersection length to remove the generic-base Euler hypothesis for power-saddle traces. They close all r graphs under full (y,p,q) automorphisms fixing x and all hyperplane coordinate-triple pullbacks, including genuine old-r-dependent y graphs with unit-affine r boundary. HC4MYHC0/1/2/3 now retain the whole Hodge polynomial of one trace fibre. The positive t coefficient excludes rank zero, and genus/puncture coefficients force actual A1 Keller-fibre components in rank one. This closes arbitrary univariate-plus-saddle traces, nonlinear polynomial-coordinate r boundaries and branched trace triples, without isolated-point or generic-base data. HC4MYHD0/1/2/3 now count the whole value fibre by affine-dual row ranks, closing every one-affine-dual-direction y graph and every non-r opposite direction in arbitrary graph/coefficient degree. The pure-r opposite exception has no positive Hodge coefficient; its complete critical Hessian reduces remaining nonautomorphy to the two existing plane endpoints, without asserting a converse realization. HC4MYHE0/1/2 now compare two parallel whole trace Hodge profiles: one pure trace forces rank zero under nonautomorphy, whereas H(U)+V*a(U,W) of positive W degree and deg H>=2 cannot have a nonpositive pure signature. This closes arbitrary q-independent r boundaries with one constant nonzero-base slice. HC4MYHE3 also closes unibranch one-place boundary curves, including singular cusp powers, without that second slice. HC4MYHF0/1 now replace orientation-specific trial with the intrinsic plane: two distinct jointly affine planes force an inverse by an elementary proof, while the covectors admitting one pure trace form exactly the unique-plane annihilator under nonautomorphy. Three independent pure directions close every degree with no sign condition; two determine three concrete directional Hessian identities and otherwise retain the exact JC2 endpoint. HC4MYHF2 makes complete profiles count and reconstruct the reduced quotient fibre, preserving the two distinct unresolved ideals. HC4MYHG0/1 now use full critical schemes, critical Hessian values and entire value fibres to survive every polynomial source automorphism. Zero-boundary base graphs and split one-variable degrees at least three cannot acquire unit Hessian after any full source mixing. HC4MYHG2 identifies all full-source base-only graph orbits and the fixed degree-six p graph with the existing coordinate/unit-ideal and quadratic/singleton-zero endpoints. No new graph-degree or source-word search is warranted inside those full orbits, and neither endpoint is solved. HC4MYHH0/1 now normalize arbitrary finite reduced coefficient fibres by local orientation and three determinant-one base shears. Every nonautomorphic finite-critical cotangent candidate is right-equivalent to the explicit degree n+1 inverse-derivative template. HC4MYHH2 identifies full-source unitization for n>=2 with one relative SL2 row equation, without solving it or producing a graph embedding. All reference templates already meet the fixed-function critical/Hodge necessary conditions, so future work needs a global row/properness or embedding restriction rather than another such invariant or native-degree sweep. HC4MYHI0/1 now apply the classical global single-generator Keller criterion: one common extra reconstruction polynomial forces an inverse, while hypothetical nonautomorphic HC4 requires exactly two relative generators. HC4MYHI2 closes every embedded realization of the exact universal A=F, B=xF+yG encoding, regardless of the remaining dual function. HC4MYHI3 closes all target-dependent affine-dual output-base embeddings, including rank drops away from the image. These are genuine all-degree embedding obstructions, not a solution of the unrestricted row equation or a statement that every graph has the required global reconstruction. HC4MYHJ0/1 remove every restriction on the dual map over a fixed plane Keller output base. Disjoint constant-unit conjugate hypersurfaces form one polynomial pencil; primitive nonconstant coefficient content removes the target denominators, and smoothness makes the relation derivative a scalar unit and forces generic degree one. Thus (K(z),H(z,w)) cannot be a closed hypersurface embedding for nonautomorphic K, for arbitrary source-dependent nonlinear H. Changing only matrix descent, dual degree or embedded fibre shape is no longer a remaining direction. The exact stable additional-generator minimum is r+2, and the intrinsic cotangent pair cannot extend to ambient coordinates in A5. Arbitrary graph embeddings need not have that physical-base interpretation. HC4MYHK0/1 now make the mixed-projection boundary exact: for k linear outputs, ell their intersection dimension with the cotangent pair, the additional-generator minimum is N-k+ell under nonautomorphy. The pure-one-component lower bound uses the classical plane stable-coordinate implication; the full-pair lower bound is HC4MYHJ1. All other A5 completions are explicit source-recovery constructions, so embedding existence alone cannot close them. Keep the fixed potential identity and marked covector transfer separate. Noncoordinate directional derivatives also identify exactly the unique cotangent plane. HC4MYHL0/1 now use the fixed-potential common-zero-base trace to close every rank-one mixed gradient realization, while preserving the correct abstract embedding classification. The free eta coefficient is (-Q_s*P+P_s*Q)/J, and nonlinear composite degree makes P divide P_s, forcing a triangular pair. Only the full-eta-rank centered gradient-base stratum survives. HC4MYHL2 adds the exact distinguished-critical-value transfer and a global necessary Euler square equation, neither of which is a properness proof or a completed embedding. HC4MYHM0/1/2 now straighten the entire ambient function to lambda_star+L*T^2+N*y*Z+2*N*x*W with an explicit polynomial inverse. Every literal graph in every constant affine direction is closed under unit Hessian by the quadratic-plus-one-square or ternary quadratic trace criterion. Check four affine-linear retained normal projections before further degree work. Preserve the actual source parameterization: full source orbits of two fixed normal graphs already contain exactly the two unresolved plane endpoints. The transverse square equation alone is not universally obstructive because constant noncritical D always passes it. HC4MYHN0/1 now lower the ambient affine projection gate from four to three, including all degenerate quadratic kernels and fully nonlinear remaining coordinates. Restricted source planes expose one-extra-generator Keller recovery, while the other cases give a triangular component or affine-line fibre. There is a genuine unit-Hessian example with exactly three affine retained projections, so this strengthens the graph theorem. Two-affine normal embeddings already realize both distinct conditional endpoints with actual polynomial inverses, and no full two-affine closure or JC2 equivalence is claimed. HC4MYHO0/1/2 now separate complete endpoint branches in the two-affine geometry: a unit two-directional-partial ideal forces a unique vertical cotangent plane and an explicit relative coordinate; aligned nondegenerate kernel rank three is exactly the unit-ideal endpoint. All affine-hyperplane normal image types are classified under arbitrary source reparameterizations into the old singleton-zero/coordinate orbits or a forbidden critical-line case. lessons_before.boundary: QHI1 is valid in every Weyl rank for finitely generated torsion-free rank-one modules and is invariant under algebraic changes of fractional realization. It is not an invariant of every algebraization in one formal class. Its explicit charge-one idealizer excludes a scalar Weyl pair with one Bernstein degree at most two and an arbitrary partner, but leaves pairs with both degrees at least three and general rank-two actions unresolved. The full right action and parameter descent are still required for Long. QKR1 supplies an all-rank cyclic-cover budget r>=(1-1/e)N+irr_0; N>2r excludes cyclic power splitting and, with one finite puncture, all finite covers. Boundary delta factors add inverse-Fourier rank. A genuinely splitting all-degree family S=g(a)+2v has inverse rank deg(g)+1, but its quadratic Long branch fails QSO2. QVM1 excludes every finite mate, on all finite coefficient covers, when S has v-leading term v*H(a), deg H>=2 and root-multiplicity gcd one, with arbitrary lower-growth terms. The candidate v*(2+h*a^3)+4a-3r*a^2 passes N6/r3 and branch extraction but fails this all-order mate test. Proper-power H, different leading faces and nonpositional first images remain outside it. No actual Long carrier follows. QVL1 transports repeated roots to nonlinear ordinary infinity limits and closes all proper-power v-linear repairs when lower coefficients are bounded. Together with QVM1, every leading H of degree>=2 is excluded in that entire Laurent class, with arbitrary finite partner order and algebraic coefficient covers. Euler limits and finite Newton support certificates give further tests. A remaining exact-R scalar Long model in the v-linear rational Laurent class has H degree<=1 and inverse-Fourier rank at least four, by QSO2 and a positive infinity Newton contribution. The family 2v*(1+h*a)^k+4a-3ra^2 is excluded for every k>=2, even though k3 passes N6/r3 and branch extraction. Nonlinear-limit commuting Darboux algebras cannot supply a scalar generator, but other operators in larger idealizers remain outside that assertion. Other leading faces, fractional positive lower growth for nonprimitive H, H degree<=1 and nonpositional first images remain open. QPD1 uses QHI1's scalar degree-zero idealizer theorem to deduce scalar units, without any symbol transversality or free-frame conclusion. It then proves spectral denominator clearing through rank-one Morita equivalence. A charge-one rational commutant u and rational mate -(2u)^-1*v clear by u^2 although neither is in the actual idealizer, whose actual position centralizer is the cusp L[u^2,u^3]. QCI1 gives a different elementary admission test in every finite generic module rank, without projectivity or gcd normalization: bounded Bernstein powers of a rational matrix plus a full finite invariant Weyl lattice force a scalar polynomial relation. A matrix with a Weyl mate cannot meet that condition. This excludes diagonal rational F_m=x^(1-m)*p/m for every m>=2, in every rational matrix frame and after identity padding. It does not extend the rank-one polynomial-symbol theorem to arbitrary higher-rank matrix entries: ((0,x^-1),(0,0)) is nilpotent and preserves the explicit finite free lattice generated by (x,0),(0,1). QIR1 adds an all-degree algebraic admission constraint: no proper nonzero left ideal is preserved by a full polynomial Weyl tuple. A full rational action admitting a finite lattice is polynomial in some division-space frame exactly when that lattice is free. This does not exclude full tuples with genuine rational idealizer entries or infer generic symbol transversality from a special classical frame. QPG1 upgrades a proved generic rank-one free frame of a finite full graph carrier to an integral free frame automatically. Thus QHI1 full right-symbol transversality, when genuinely established, closes the remaining frame step without a separate parameter-compatible filtration. The special classical graph does not itself establish that generic transversality. QVA1 proves the valuation counterpart of QHI1: normalized initial t-ideals are preserved by all right residue Hamiltonians. A full polynomial symplectic residue frame forces C-freeness and formal B-freeness, rather than generic finite-PBW freeness. This automatically closes the QPG1 overlap-frame step for a finite generic rank-one Gauss-regular action, without inferring a generic Bernstein frame from its classical shadow.

lessons_before.when: A high-degree Hamiltonian correction is removed from a polynomial canonical pair in order to seek a lower-degree full symplectic or Weyl map.
lessons_before.use: Determine the full polynomial joint centralizer or a Poisson quotient that bounds its symplectic rank. For quantum candidates, a nonzero finite-dimensional polynomial eigenspace yields a matrix representation of the centralizer and a stable PBW-growth obstruction. Distinguish ordinary polynomial fiber translations from actual canonical changes; for the cubic Long core their shifts are canonical exactly for H in K[R]. For a Hamiltonian linear in momenta, scalar polynomial invariants of its base vector field give a Poisson character on the whole centralizer by zero-momentum evaluation.
lessons_before.avoid: Treating an exact canonical pair as automatically completable to a full frame, dropping Long's H while retaining R, assuming adding spectator pairs removes the fixed-core obstruction, or extending the resonant normal-order quantum statement to every ordering.
lessons_before.boundary: QCC1 excludes D0 as any component, and hence the fixed cubic pair (R,D0), globally in all polynomial degrees and under stabilization. It rules out a canonical normalization from corrected Long D to D0 even when R changes. Its quantum result applies to D0+(3*m/2)*h*q for nonnegative integer m via a finite eigenspace; the symmetric shift -9*h*q/4 is outside that family. Other cubic pairs with a genuinely different D, the corrected Long map and spatially rational or formal completions remain outside this exclusion. A zero or infinite eigenspace alone gives no quantum obstruction.
lessons_before.reopen_when: A genuinely different full cubic representative, a bounded scalar-anomaly tuple retaining the corrected data, or a complete finite-eigenspace proof for another candidate operator is available.

lessons_before.title: Keep exceptional torsion and full admission when transporting a quantum fiber pair
lessons_before.when: A correction or canonical transport in Long's R centralizer is tested on generic fibers, or a fiber translation fixing the positions is proposed as a full canonical gauge.
lessons_before.use: Rewrite R/2=x*(1+x*y), b=B/3 and theta=x^2*d_x-(1+2*x*y)*d_y. Reduce F*(4*y^2*dx+(2*x*y-1)*dy) by the complete weight normal form. Vanishing of the whole normal form is equivalent to a global polynomial primitive for the vertical correction and to extension of b to b+F as a full polynomial canonical map fixing x,y. This applies exactly to the quantum Ore algebra as well. For an admitted full Long lift, the quantum fiber translation b to b+h^N*F preserves admission exactly when the whole class vanishes. Maintain the fourth image and all full relations during correction; F=1 leaves the admissible locus at any selected N while preserving exact partial relations.
lessons_before.avoid: Replacing global primitive membership by vanishing generic periods, checking fibers individually, assuming smoothness gives torsion-free relative cohomology, or using an arbitrary fiber automorphism as a global canonical transformation. lessons_before.boundary: The relative H is D_r/D_r*(r*partial_r), with an exceptional delta submodule and quotient K[r]. The explicit classes y^n*d(1+x*y) have exact r-torsion order n and are invisible on every fiber. The criterion fixes the base positions and a vertical correction class. For every N>=1 and polynomial F it completely decides formal fourth-image admission after the specified h^N fiber translation of an admitted Long triple. It neither covers arbitrary moving-position transformations nor excludes Long's full formal gauge class. The admitted starting tuple need not have bounded degree, and without a common bound on the correction coefficients, coefficientwise global exactness does not establish bounded primitives. QGR1 supplies the sharp primitive bound once the correction has a common degree bound.

lessons_before.title: Exhaust the bounded fixed-R gauge group before seeking higher-order changes
lessons_before.when: A finite polynomial canonical change preserving Long's R, a bounded centralizer gauge, or degree growth in its global Hamiltonian primitive is proposed.
lessons_before.use: The factorization r=x*(1+x*y) and additive operator order force every finite endomorphism of the R centralizer preserving r to fix x,y and translate b by F. Full fixed-R Weyl endomorphisms are exact gradient automorphisms. Test F with QRP1's complete global normal form. If the class vanishes, remove r-power pivots from the primitive: its degree is exactly deg(F)-1. Uniformly bounded globally exact corrections therefore have uniformly bounded full extensions and inverses. Use the explicit monomial division F=theta(G)+Q to compute the normalized primitive and the canonical global remainder. Every reduction lowers residual degree by two; Q is supported on y^j and x^(2j+1)*y^j and vanishes exactly for globally exact inputs. No degree sweep or separate linear system is needed.
lessons_before.avoid: Searching larger operator orders for hidden mixed-position fixed-R gauges, treating a formal R-preserving flow as finite, or confusing a map whose first image is R with a map fixing the polynomial observable R.
lessons_before.boundary: The all-degree classification is in rank two for finite PBW images, including scalar series K[[h]]. Arbitrary formal h-adic gauges can move positions while fixing R and have unbounded spatial degree. Admission equivalence for all bounded centralizer changes assumes an admitted Long starting tuple and identity classical gauge. No bounded reachability between every pair of full lifts, bounded normalization of a deformed first image, or bounded Long lift is proved. The bounded observable r+c(h) has a bounded mate and a formal normalization, yet generic irreducibility forbids every bounded target automorphism sending it to reducible r. A bounded source translation removes the scalar shift, so retain the distinction between target-only and two-sided changes. QFG1 classifies the larger finite-momentum formal fixed-R category: positions may move by a formal cotangent base, with global admission j*F=theta(G). Every finite fiber order is preserved. A bounded exact-R target therefore needs a unique comparison with unbounded momentum in at least one position image. Exact R and the Euler connection K do not exclude this: explicit global arbitrary-contact invariant flows have that behavior while their transported full frames remain unbounded. No bounded-target-specific impossibility follows. QPG1 unrestricted finite-jet reduction does not enlarge the exact fixed-R stabilizer: the finite polynomial shears matching a full formal comparison need not fix R. It gives finite algebraization equivalence for full lifts of one classical map after allowing such changes and inner formal module isomorphism. It supplies no bounded representative or exception to QGR1 within the fixed-R category.
lessons_before.reopen_when: A full bounded carrier is constructed, a bounded gauge comparison covers arbitrary admitted lifts or moving-R changes, or a different algebraization gives an actual full relation and common-degree certificate.

For Long, Delta_r=V(A)+8*Delta/(5r) obstructs every algebraic primitive by a nonzero holomorphic elliptic differential, eliminating all positive conjugate degrees at once. The remaining genus-one orbits force locally nilpotent Hamiltonians into the first-coordinate and spectator algebra. Its Poisson rank bounds independent commuting directions to one below the number needed for a full positional form, in every stabilization.
lessons_before.avoid: Assuming a mixed target canonical change or more identity pairs can restore a cotangent form, using ordinary polynomial equivalence to transport a Weyl realization, replacing the nonzero elliptic differential class by nonisotriviality, or extending intrinsic local nilpotence from an image to the ambient ring without proof.
lessons_before.boundary: QHR1 excludes one full positional/cotangent normal form after arbitrary polynomial canonical source and target changes, even wild ones and every identity stabilization. It does not exclude every composition of several noninvertible cotangent factors interleaved with canonical maps. The regular formal quantum corollary assumes both changes and inverses have invertible polynomial classical reductions; parameter-pole changes are separate. lessons_before.title: Separate completed quantum degree from generic division degree and global polynomial finiteness
lessons_before.when: A formal lift, elliptic isogeny, finite division extension or completed graph model is proposed as a route to a bounded full Weyl realization.
lessons_before.use: Compute the classical function-field degree first. A residue basis lifts to a basis of the completed quantum division extension on both sides. For actual degree-D finite PBW images, independent-set PBW growth bounds the generic indices by D^(2n), and residue independence bounds them below by the classical degree. Equality with the completed degree is exactly finite generation of the actual valuation lattice over the image valuation ring. Check this extra condition rather than infer it from completion. Long has full completed degree three even when its first image deforms; the generic indices of every bounded full lift are at least three. Use the retained full polynomial identity family (generic degree3, completed degree1, bound12) as a necessary control for any descent claim.
lessons_before.avoid: Inferring generic degree three from Long's classical three-isogeny or formal lift; treating index symmetry as degree preservation; equating finiteness of a valuation lattice, a finite division extension and finite generation of the ambient Weyl algebra over its image; or assuming exact full relations and bounded forward images prevent rank loss on completion.
lessons_before.boundary: The completed-degree theorem, individual index bounds and lattice criterion are written self-contained proofs. Equality of the two generic indices uses the cited 2026 index-symmetry preprint. The explicit full polynomial failure has rank at least three; rank-one arbitrary-degree failures have rational coefficients and positional classical maps. They do not refute a Long-specific equality theorem. Even proving generic index three would not construct or exclude a bounded lift. The valuation lattice is not the finite PBW graph module, and finite generation of the ambient Weyl algebra over its image would instead force invertibility. QMC1 removes the generic rank-one free-frame prerequisite only for an intermediate matrix conclusion: a finite-left R-flat full h-Weyl graph carrier has generic projective rank one, and Stafford stabilization gives a non-surjective Mat_2(A_n) endomorphism when the classical field degree exceeds one. A scalar A_n lift still needs a free frame or another construction. Its rational action retains the classical degree without fixing R; both generic division indices are finite but need not equal their completed value. The full right action remains indispensable, as the explicit QPF1 compression defect shows. No such Long carrier is constructed, and the separate arithmetic-support hypotheses are not inferred. QST1 separates rational and spectral admission. Any nonzero Adler period excludes the entire rational operator division ring and makes the universal spectral class nontorsion; the G(a)+mu*v first period is explicit in all degrees. This blocks every rational conjugate and the corresponding actual rank-one projective pair orbit without a scalar free frame. Fixed rational mate equations descend through finite algebraic coefficient covers by monic-denominator Galois averaging. Constant-coefficient G has instead a critical-value torsion annihilator and a rational mate. Zero Adler periods are insufficient for rational admission: a torus residue excludes harmonic/Euler functional classes even with arbitrary operator denominators and identity spectators. Finite primitive-divisor and ordinary infinity exclusions must not be silently promoted to rational ones. No arbitrary moving spectral coefficient localization, nonlinear Galois descent or universal Long rational normalization is proved. QFC1 requires module finiteness of the actual joint centralizer over the commuting images. Finite division indices or finite fraction-field degree do not imply that hypothesis. Once actual individual conjugates exist, generic centralizer module finiteness forces integral polynomiality and full flat completion. The planar rescaled cotangent boundary would imply JC2 if that finiteness were asserted universally. QET1 studies the commutative centralizer field H over L(F_i), distinct from full noncommutative division indices and their h-completed degrees. Finite generation plus actual mates gives etaleness; with scalar units, a birational or Galois centralizer field forces polynomiality. The rank-three QNI1 centralizer has non-Galois degree three. Neither a completed field comparison nor leading-symbol birationality determines the actual centralizer field. QET1 also removes actual parameter poles under the polynomial classical centralizer hypothesis, with no finite-generation or field-degree assumption: individual mates have unique finite polynomial polar parts. Subtraction preserves any integral curvature exactly, so an actual generic flat tuple with regular positions descends to a finite integral flat tuple and can match a prescribed classical flat frame. Only h is inverted; rational spatial/operator denominators and arbitrary completed series remain outside this descent. QTB1 embeds the actual centralizer fraction field in the h-completed position field and identifies its horizontal constants without finite generation. Taylor valuations control every finite intermediate and forbid Galois factors. These are commutative position-field statements; no equality with whole noncommutative generic/completed indices is inferred. QPD1 identifies the full rational commutant of a complete commuting tuple in a rank-one projective Weyl order with the fraction field of its actual commutants. The needed spectral denominator exists without a free frame. This centralizer saturation does not identify generic and completed whole Weyl division indices or make rational mates actual. QCI1 relates the formerly distinct centralizer and whole indices: for an actual full tuple, H/C is finite and N_l=d*M_l, N_r=d*M_r after adjoining all rational position commutants. Under the Long formal/classical centralizer hypotheses, the intermediate ring still completes to the image and M_l,M_r>=3. Thus nontrivial d>=3 forces N_l,N_r>=9. This does not import generic left/right equality or construct a minimal-index lift. QCI1 now gives actual rational residual extensions F_m=x^(1-m)*p/m,T_m=x^m with generic and completed indices m. For the F_m position, d=1 and M=m; source exchange gives d=m and M=1. Their diagonal actions admit no finite lattice in any positive generic rank by bounded Bernstein powers. Thus a rational residual degree3 exists, but field degree alone does not supply a finite Weyl carrier. QGD1 identifies the entire generic/completed gap for a finite group quotient W=D^G: keep all r conjugate valuation branches, then both generic indices are |G|=r*delta and the selected completed image is the fixed ring of the valuation stabilizer H, of order delta. The residue cover must be Galois even when G has parameter poles. Long therefore has no direct finite quotient model in any degrees. This does not identify the general index gap with valuation branches outside the finite-group setting. QGC1 now proves the relative closure index equals its residue degree for an equivariant finite carrier with special rank equal to that residue degree: finite-presentation rank specialization and QGD1 force |H|=delta and all group elements to preserve the valuation. This is a relative Dtilde/D statement, not equality of Long whole indices [D:W]. Split-abelian character shifts then repair nonsaturation; ordinary-parameter graph admission alternatively supplies finite full valuation-level lattices without equivariance or index equality. Universal saturation is false, as genuine constant-cover Weyl carriers demonstrate. QTC1 makes both generic indices and the completed degree multiplicative under forward tensor composition of full finite carriers. For either side N/delta multiplies, so a strict generic/completed gap cannot be removed by composing further admitted finite carriers. This does not apply a group inverse to a noninvertible formal identity lift or justify finite admission of a carrier/dual reverse tensor. The actual QNI1 k-fold iterates give generic indices3^k, completed degree1 and forward degree at most12^k in every rank at least three, with arbitrary identity contact and formal innerness at contact order at least two. No rank-two example or bound independent of k is inferred.
lessons_before.reopen_when: A Long-specific global boundary or valuation-lattice theorem constrains the generic division extension, or an actual bounded full higher-order carrier supplies images to which these invariants can be applied.

lessons_before.title: Normalize a whole cubic orbit in covariance space and prove a finite exclusion through exhaustive torus charts
lessons_before.when: A singular homogeneous cubic has a simple linear normal form, but its Gaussian metric varies under general linear changes and a full moment basis is expensive.
lessons_before.use: Give an elementary invertible normal-form reduction, then retain the full symmetric Gaussian covariance rather than silently making the change orthogonal. Prove a diagonal automorphism torus scales the entire polynomial, and normalize covariance entries only on the nonzero branches where that action applies. Cover every zero-entry branch explicitly. Eliminate M2 using a constant nonzero coefficient, clear denominators before native CAS input, and prove that a determinant power belongs to the finite remaining moment ideal in each chart. Reuse a completed standard-basis checkpoint from a later timed-out job with the full job still incomplete. Test small determinant powers before a high-power reduction. Derive sharp witnesses from exact Wick lattice balance and parity, not a long numerical prefix.
lessons_before.avoid: Treating an arbitrary GL normal form as Gaussian orthogonal coordinates, assuming positive-semidefinite covariance for complex coefficients, dropping a=0/b=0/d=0 branches, using a modular saturated unit as a rational proof, or calling the first-nine-zero cusp an all-order Gaussian-moment counterexample. Avoid native ring/polynomial variable-name collisions; preserve the invalid replay and its corrected version.
