lessons_before.title: Demand global reconstruction and exclude exact cotangent or output-base encoding upgrades before increasing degrees
lessons_before.when: A universal plane Keller substitution is proposed as a genuine graph embedding, or an ambient hypersurface encoding is meant to carry the gradient outputs with one remaining coordinate.
lessons_before.use: Reproduce the classical single-generator theorem from the hypersurface relation: vanishing relative differentials make its T derivative a polynomial unit, hence a scalar, and characteristic zero makes the relation linear. Thus one global additional reconstruction polynomial over Keller outputs forces an inverse. In the exact A=F, B=xF+yG encoding, a single physical fibre gives (F,G-4F,h), closing every embedded nonautomorphic upgrade in arbitrary degree. For j=(K(z),M(K(z))*w+v(z)), the smooth closed image hypersurface has dual normal equal to a unit scalar times the target matrix cross product; the strict dual-degree comparison makes it linear and forces birational, hence invertible, K. The proof allows target rank drops away from the source image. HC4MYHJ0/1 remove every restriction on the dual map over a fixed plane Keller output base. Disjoint constant-unit conjugate hypersurfaces form one polynomial pencil; primitive nonconstant coefficient content removes the target denominators, and smoothness makes the relation derivative a scalar unit and forces generic degree one. Thus (K(z),H(z,w)) cannot be a closed hypersurface embedding for nonautomorphic K, for arbitrary source-dependent nonlinear H. Changing only matrix descent, dual degree or embedded fibre shape is no longer a remaining direction. The exact stable additional-generator minimum is r+2, and the intrinsic cotangent pair cannot extend to ambient coordinates in A5. Arbitrary graph embeddings need not have that physical-base interpretation. HC4MYHK0/1 now make the mixed-projection boundary exact: for k linear outputs, ell their intersection dimension with the cotangent pair, the additional-generator minimum is N-k+ell under nonautomorphy. The pure-one-component lower bound uses the classical plane stable-coordinate implication; the full-pair lower bound is HC4MYHJ1. All other A5 completions are explicit source-recovery constructions, so embedding existence alone cannot close them. Keep the fixed potential identity and marked covector transfer separate. Noncoordinate directional derivatives also identify exactly the unique cotangent plane. HC4MYHL0/1 now use the fixed-potential common-zero-base trace to close every rank-one mixed gradient realization, while preserving the correct abstract embedding classification. The free eta coefficient is (-Q_s*P+P_s*Q)/J, and nonlinear composite degree makes P divide P_s, forcing a triangular pair. Only the full-eta-rank centered gradient-base stratum survives. HC4MYHL2 adds the exact distinguished-critical-value transfer and a global necessary Euler square equation, neither of which is a properness proof or a completed embedding. HC4MYHM0/1/2 now straighten the entire ambient function to lambda_star+L*T^2+N*y*Z+2*N*x*W with an explicit polynomial inverse. Every literal graph in every constant affine direction is closed under unit Hessian by the quadratic-plus-one-square or ternary quadratic trace criterion. Check four affine-linear retained normal projections before further degree work. Preserve the actual source parameterization: full source orbits of two fixed normal graphs already contain exactly the two unresolved plane endpoints. The transverse square equation alone is not universally obstructive because constant noncritical D always passes it. HC4MYHN0/1 now lower the ambient affine projection gate from four to three, including all degenerate quadratic kernels and fully nonlinear remaining coordinates. Restricted source planes expose one-extra-generator Keller recovery, while the other cases give a triangular component or affine-line fibre. There is a genuine unit-Hessian example with exactly three affine retained projections, so this strengthens the graph theorem. Two-affine normal embeddings already realize both distinct conditional endpoints with actual polynomial inverses, and no full two-affine closure or JC2 equivalence is claimed. HC4MYHO0/1/2 now separate complete endpoint branches in the two-affine geometry: a unit two-directional-partial ideal forces a unique vertical cotangent plane and an explicit relative coordinate; aligned nondegenerate kernel rank three is exactly the unit-ideal endpoint. All affine-hyperplane normal image types are classified under arbitrary source reparameterizations into the old singleton-zero/coordinate orbits or a forbidden critical-line case. New directions beyond those endpoints require nonlinear normal image hypersurfaces. No unaligned two-affine closure or singleton uniqueness from mere attainment is claimed. HC4MYHP0/1 now require checking the whole polynomial quadratic-similitude saturation, since explicit genuine nonlinear images can have zero affine pullbacks while their unchanged source potential is a closed quadratic. HC4MYHQ0/1 enlarge the output-base obstruction to linear-quadratic ambient observables through a global quadric filtration, without requiring ambient coordinate completion or fibre rectification. HC4MYHR0/1 now test relative critical sections and curve products and classify every base-only quadratic graph under unrestricted relative free-variable automorphisms, without alignment and with at most one full critical point under unit Hessian. HC4MYHS0/1/2 add a one-component proper-Morse closure and exact universal JC2 boundaries for the two separate conditions, with an explicit arbitrary-dimensional finite-free monomial-basis construction. HC4MYHT0/1 add uniform quadratic-plane rigidity and the entire fibre-affine two-affine embedding classification, with alignment forced and all base matrix degrees unrestricted. HC4MYHU0/1 now rectify isotropic-ideal image graphs explicitly and classify every compatible positive-weight invariant image into the singleton orbit or a degenerate critical-point obstruction, without assuming equivariance in actual source coordinates. HC4MYHV0/1 now test arbitrary-degree ambient output observables by a global filtered criterion and a smooth scheme-theoretic complete intersection at infinity, with the Picard input explicit. HC4MYHW0/1 replace factoriality by torsion-free abelian divisor-class monodromy and replace height-one graded domains by geometrically integral affine fibres; HC4MYHW2/3 close r=1 quadric pairs, specified degenerate ranks and all cyclic Danielewski powers. HC4MYHX0/1 preserve arbitrary finite monodromy descending from a regular polynomial parameter; HC4MYHX2 closes all constant-coefficient Danielewski P(z) and every T*Y+xy-B(T,z) suspension in every degree, beyond the earlier abelian class-action gate. HC4MYHY0/1 now close normal finite monogenic root covers and every monic two-parameter Danielewski output by root transitivity; HC4MYHY2 imposes a global nonmonogenicity gate on every nontrivial finite Keller normalization. HC4MYHZ0/1/2 supply the finite leading-fibre gate and independent abelian-root gate for nonmonic outputs, with exact localized-unit defect. HC4MYIA0/1/2 upgrade the unconditional nonmonic gate to finite nilpotent root/class groups and arbitrary common-prime radical depth. HC4MYIB0/1/2 add arbitrary Galois-intermediate exclusion, the exact global normalization-boundary basis, and subnormal class-stabilizer closure beyond nilpotent actions. HC4MYIC0/1/2 add combined leading-order factor divisibility, rational-label critical-curve geometry and new unrestricted-parameter S3 cubic closures. HC4MYID0/1 refine critical units to factor-specific supports and all subset rank budgets, closing a new square-discriminant S3 family with arbitrary leading multiplicity. HC4MYID2 closes reduced singleton critical units with nonconstant separation, including the cubic two-simple-leading-level case. HC4MYID3 closes the fixed cubic by a polynomial second chart omitting a hyperbola and consequently the entire specified two-simple-level square-critical class. HC4MYIE0/1/2 supply the intermediate-pole necessity, cyclic derivative surface, normal monic rescaling and unrestricted square-free-leading cubic closure. HC4MYIF0/1/2 constrain every source factorization, close square-free-leading quartics and supply a field-degree and nonnormal-order obstruction for the remaining unequal pair. HC4MYIG0/1/2 add reduced-pencil rational monodromy, one-exception polynomial parameters and all-degree scaled and reciprocal-scaled one-variable output closures. The same mechanism now closes rational scalings and rational affine input with polynomial output translation, including all sparse two-positive-term outputs without a gcd condition. HC4MYIH0/1/2 add the strict projective multiplicity bound, exact affine-in-V exception certificate and all-degree mixed-critical-value expansion outputs. HC4MYII0/1/2/3/4 add plane intermediate-branch geometry, unrestricted rational affine parameters, actual-inertia quotient certificates, all nonadjacent pure-power binomials and every cubic output. HC4MYIJ0/1/2/3 add relative central-series descent, actual product-cover preservation with arbitrary parameter monodromy, and the all-degree finite-critical-pole binomial certificate. HC4MYIK0/1/2/3 add parameter-cover unit norms, integral algebraic monic models, a direct critical-value valuation lemma and unrestricted plane polynomial-output closure. HC4MYIL0/1/2 add generative factor transfer, exact fixed-multiplier class lattices and all-degree multivariable suspension closure with full global filtration. HC4MYIM0/1/2/3 add parameter-extension irreducibility, moving-row invariant vanishing, an exact content-fibre criterion and uniform adapted global frames. The IM3 determinant-one parameter matrix covers moving B, multivariable monic-leading b and arbitrary affine root terms, with a separate primitive-content check. The IM3 frame admits every strict joint degree-gap remainder; its univariate leading-divisibility corollary allows all lower P coefficients. HC4MYIN0/1 replace the former global-frame requirement by rank-two reflexive pencil descent and close every primitive disjoint moving suspension. HC4MYIO0/1/2 extend to arbitrary independent coefficient fields and overlapping polynomial directions; monic and polynomial-Bezout leading overlap outputs have uniform generic filtrations. HC4MYIP0/1/2 use moved relative additive actions instead of positive generic filtrations, and force every surviving overlap image into the multiplier-variable invariant subring. HC4MYIQ0/1/2 descend any univariate generic helper, close every one-helper admitted overlap including nonprimitive content, and reduce HC4 survivors to two-helper invariant plane curves. HC4MYIR0/1/2 close multiplier-zero images in all helper counts and every admitted two-helper overlap in every stable dimension; the complete admitted HC4 overlap family is now closed. IS0/1/2 identify the full JC2 content of an unconditional residual-free extension, including an exact source-correlated class lattice and actual unit-Hessian embeddings with an always invertible constructed gradient. IT0/1/2 give intrinsic finite-energy and inverse-Hessian certificates and a mixed three-direction criterion before any ambient output construction. IU0/1/2 exploit actual free projections and the zero-section first jet, closing critical-value traces and testing the global immersion obligation in a universal noncritical construction. IV0/1/2 separate complete compensation identities from codimension-one source recovery and provide a canonical Legendre-hypersurface normality gate. IW0/1/2 close every constant trace through an infinite-order integral middle-cycle obstruction, with arbitrary helper degrees. IX0/1/2 separate arbitrary quadric plane classes from actual radical-curve recovery and close coordinate-composite or smooth/nonparametric descended nonconstant traces. IY0/1/2 close contractible full-preimage curves and descended cusps, and impose the exact generic-pencil boundary-defect certificate on the remaining multibranch cases. IZ0/1/2 match the intrinsic generic genus on all one-place zero curves and close every rank-one descended trace, including all internally multibranch cases and positive-power rational descent. JA0/1/2 force the actual disjoint extra-prime/unit/boundary configuration and bound its one-place part; scalar extra units close the selected one-place case.
lessons_before.avoid: Replacing global algebra generation by field generation, generic-chart recovery or monogenic zero-fibre data; inferring relative generator count from five ambient versus four gradient coordinates; dropping closed embedding, characteristic zero or the source-unit condition; calling the classical Formanek criterion new; treating the exact two-generator minimum as an absolute embedding dimension; applying the target-descended matrix argument to a source-dependent or nonlinear dual map.
lessons_before.boundary: All earlier three-affine and ambient quadratic obstructions remain valid. Two directional partials generating the global unit ideal now force their unique plane to be the cotangent plane, give a globally affine free-variable form and an explicit relative coordinate inverse. The aligned rank-three quadratic kernel branch is exactly the unit-ideal plane endpoint. All affine-hyperplane normal images, under arbitrary source parameterizations, are exactly the singleton-zero orbit, the unit-ideal coordinate orbit, or the isotropic-through-center critical-line branch that forbids unit Hessian. Neither endpoint is resolved. Rank-one aligned fibre attainment is not singleton uniqueness; unaligned two-affine embeddings and nonlinear normal image hypersurfaces remain open with the unrestricted row equation. Polynomial quadratic-similitude saturation is now an additional global gate: if q composed with an ambient polynomial automorphism is a*q, undo it in the same source parameters before classifying retained projections or hyperplane images. The entire saturated three-affine class stays closed; the full-source hyperplane saturation retains exactly the old two endpoints or critical-line obstruction. Explicit unbounded words give zero affine pullbacks and nonlinear image equations while preserving a unit-Hessian quadratic source potential. Raw image nonlinearity is therefore insufficient. No universal rectification or generation of every quadratic symmetry is asserted. The output-base obstruction now includes a linear observable paired with any nondegenerate ambient quadratic, not only ambient coordinate pairs. In all stable dimensions r>=2, generic quadric factoriality and a height-one-compatible monomial filtration make the pencil and denominator arguments global, and smoothness forces the plane Keller base invertible. Thus an intrinsic nonautomorphic cotangent pair cannot have such an ambient extension, even after a certified ambient polynomial automorphism. Direct native A/B encodings of an independent Keller pair collapse to an invertible pair and a coordinate potential. Both plane endpoints and arbitrary other source-pair extensions remain open; no surface-quadric factoriality or embedding rectification is assumed. Relative critical schemes now give a separate global gate. A polynomial section over a constant two-variable base, or a base-compatible smooth curve times A1 with vertical Hessian rank one, forces gradient invertibility under unit Hessian. Consequently every base-only normal graph j=(s,t,h(s,t),H,G) under arbitrary relative free-variable polynomial automorphisms has at most one full critical point under unit Hessian, with no cotangent alignment. Its nonautomorphic members are exactly the two old endpoint source orbits. Native graph members with multiple full critical points have no relative unitization over that fixed base. Arbitrary four-variable source mixing and three genuinely free-dependent unretained coordinates remain open. One proper relative Morse component now suffices: no condition on other components is needed, and a globally proper everywhere-Morse relative projection can only have degree one. Each nonautomorphic component must therefore fail properness or contain vertical degeneracy. However each single condition separately retains exactly JC2. The universal f_M model has relative projection K and vertical Hessian -DK^T*DK, while the finite-free Fermat construction gives every K a proper relative projection with explicit monomial basis and ramification at zero. Its properness is not properness of K. Neither model automatically supplies a compatible closed ambient embedding. The two plane endpoints and unrestricted graph compatibility remain open. Uniform quadratic two-planes now have the same unique-plane rigidity under nonautomorphy as affine ones: any genuinely quadratic constant two-plane or two distinct quadratic planes closes the candidate. This classifies every fibre-affine two-affine embedding j=(s,t,b+A*w) in all base degrees. Global source generation requires a polynomial left inverse of A; generic rank is not enough. Alignment follows under nonautomorphy, a rank-three helper quadratic closes unconditionally, and lower ranks force a base-only helper and the two old endpoints. All unit-Hessian members have at most one full critical point. Arbitrary nonlinear free helpers and nonaligned potentials of free degree at least three remain open. Nonlinear isotropic-ideal image graphs now have explicit global quadratic isometries to hyperplanes, with arbitrary coefficients in unchanged variables and all source parameterizations. Compatible positive linear ambient weights give a constructive recognition gate: a smooth invariant image either has an isotropic tangent normal forbidding unit Hessian, or its lower-weight nonlinear terms admit a weighted Euler shear to the nonisotropic hyperplane. Only the singleton-zero endpoint survives for these positive images. Actual positive linear source weights would close gradient invertibility, but image invariance alone does not supply that hypothesis after nonlinear source changes. Other nonlinear images and both plane endpoints remain open. The output-base gate now admits arbitrary degrees for both ambient observables: a smooth scheme-theoretic codimension-two complete intersection of their highest forms at infinity forces any carried Keller pair invertible. The leading regular sequence supplies a common filtered basis and height-one graded domains, while the explicitly imported smooth complete-intersection Picard theorem supplies generic factoriality. Generic factoriality alone and smooth reduced support do not suffice; Pi=(x,xy+z^2) has an exact denominator failure. Arbitrary extensions need not have the required leading forms. Singular, nonreduced or excess-dimensional infinity intersections and both plane endpoints remain open. Generic factoriality is now relaxed by HC4MYHW0/1: torsion-free abelian divisor-class monodromy suffices, since Keller function fields contain no nontrivial abelian Galois intermediate field and all conjugate component classes then become zero. Geometric integrality of affine height-one fibres suffices for global primitive saturation even with nonconstant fibre units or reducible graded rings. The earlier r=1 exclusion for nondegenerate linear-quadratic output pairs is removed by HC4MYHW2, without calling the quadric surface factorial; degenerate restricted-rank-at-least-three quadratics close too. HC4MYHW3 closes cyclic Danielewski output pairs in every power m>=2, including nonreduced ordinary leading schemes and generic nonfactoriality outside every older smooth-infinity frame in the HC4-size first type. Nonabelian class actions, torsion, nonintegral height-one fibres, uncovered ranks and infinity schemes and both plane endpoints remain open. The nonabelian boundary is now narrower: HC4MYHX0/1 prove that a nowhere-critical polynomial parameter is relatively algebraically closed in the source field, using an explicit classical closed-polynomial import. A class action descending from a finite cover of that one parameter retains its full possibly nonabelian group under Keller base change, so the component classes become principal. This does not make all special parameter fibres irreducible or the whole Keller extension trivial. HC4MYHX2 closes every constant-coefficient nonconstant Danielewski P(z), with arbitrary root group, and every suspended T*Y+xy-B(T,z) with arbitrary two-variable B and all degrees. The earlier nonabelian-P(z) and suspended-coefficient escape proposals are retired. Genuinely two-parameter unsuspended monodromy, torsion, nonintegral height-one fibres, other missing filtrations and both plane endpoints remain open. HC4MYHY0 now preserves irreducibility of every normal finite monogenic cover under Keller base change, in every dimension and degree. All conjugate constant cross-resultants and integral roots rule out inertia crossing; explicit purity and finite-cover comparison inputs make the quotient trivial. HC4MYHY1 closes every two-parameter P(T,z) with nonzero constant leading z coefficient: root transitivity, without full splitting-group preservation, makes the invariant root-divisor classes zero. HC4MYHY2 forbids a globally monogenic finite normalization for any nontrivial Keller intermediate field; a nonautomorphic plane normalization needs at least two additional global algebra generators. Generic primitive elements do not provide normal monogenic models. Nonconstant leading coefficients, nonnormal monic presentations, nonglobally-monogenic normal finite algebras, other embeddings and both plane endpoints remain open. HC4MYHZ0 computes the exact torsion-free localized-unit defect as the sum of the reduced full-fibre component lattices at the zeros of a(T). HC4MYHZ1 preserves normal monogenic root-cover irreducibility on that vertical open when just those finitely many full K1-fibres are irreducible. The remaining finite etale generic-affine-line quotient is a finite Galois parameter extension, eliminated using HC4MYHX0; the explicitly imported Riemann-Hurwitz formula proves the constant-field descent. HC4MYHZ2 consequently closes every nonmonic P(T,z) under that finite-fibre gate. Independently, abelian generic root monodromy closes all such P without the fibre hypothesis, including every z degree one or two and arbitrary translated powers a(T)*(z-b(T))^m+c(T). A remaining nonautomorphic realization in this family needs both nonabelian generic root monodromy and positive localized-unit defect at a leading-coefficient zero. Generic parameter regularity does not supply the finite-fibre hypothesis, and etale affine curve maps are not automatically finite. The audited Tian-Sun 2024 claims are excluded as proof inputs. Both plane endpoints and unrestricted HC4/JC2 remain open. HC4MYIA0 upgrades the cyclic obstruction to full preservation of every finite nilpotent Galois target group under Keller base change in every dimension: a proper source image lies below a normal cyclic prime quotient, which would give a forbidden intermediate field. HC4MYIA1 therefore permits finite nilpotent class monodromy in the filtered output criterion. HC4MYIA2 closes every nonmonic xy-P(T,z) with nilpotent generic root group without a special-fibre assumption, including arbitrary-depth common-prime radical compositions and every composition of arbitrary quadratics. The explicit nonmonic quartic T*(z^2-T)^2 has nonabelian D8 group and is newly closed even without K1=0 irreducible. The remaining branch in this full family needs both nonnilpotent generic root monodromy and positive localized-unit defect at a leading zero. Arbitrary solvable groups do not follow: an S3 order-two subgroup escapes all normal prime-index containers. General wreath embeddings are primary context, not an additional proof import; the restricted common-prime construction is proved directly. Both plane endpoints and unrestricted HC4/JC2 remain open. HC4MYIB0 now excludes every finite Galois intermediate target-field extension inside a complex Keller field, in every dimension and without a group restriction: a visible index-one place reaches all primes by Galois conjugacy, then explicit purity and finite-cover inputs force triviality. This does not assert arbitrary full splitting-group preservation. HC4MYIB1 identifies the finite plane normalization class group exactly as the free group on the omitted boundary divisors; a torsion or globally factorial normalization forces the inverse. Local factoriality alone is insufficient. HC4MYIB2 closes the filtered output criterion when divisor-class stabilizers are subnormal in an arbitrary finite class-action image; normal class stabilizers suffice even for nonnilpotent groups. The Hurwitz lattice gives an explicit nonnilpotent class-module certificate, without an asserted ambient realization. The S3 root-lattice order-two stabilizer is not subnormal and remains a genuine boundary. Within nonmonic xy-P(T,z), positive localized-unit defect and nonnilpotent monodromy remain necessary unless another retained gate closes the case. Both plane endpoints and unrestricted HC4/JC2 remain open. HC4MYIC0 now constrains every source root-factor degree by m/gcd(m,q_1,...,q_k) when leading-drop coefficient orders lie above the single-slope chords; coprime combined orders give irreducibility and close the carried output in arbitrary z degree without a special-fibre or monodromy hypothesis. HC4MYIC1 clears a rational root to a polynomial label with an exact vertical-Jacobian identity. The constructed polynomial map omits its normalized critical curve, so the explicit qualitative Jelonek-Lason nonproperness input forces each critical component to have affine normalization A1. Independently a square-free leading coefficient dividing the next coefficient excludes rational roots. HC4MYIC2 consequently closes nonmonic cubics if a is square-free and divides b, or if the critical discriminant D=b^2-3ac has square-free part of degree at least two. This includes new S3 families with unbounded T degree and no special-fibre hypothesis. The remaining cubic branch requires a rational label, positive localized-unit defect, S3 group, D of square-free degree at most one, and failure of the independent no-pole gate; D=0 was already cyclic and closed. Critical and root discriminants are distinct, and no-rational-root is not irreducibility in arbitrary higher degree. Both plane endpoints and unrestricted HC4/JC2 remain open. HC4MYIC1 also gives a quantitative critical-branch unit budget: if the normalized derivative Q_U has ell distinct rational roots over C(T), monicity puts them in C[T], and the corresponding polynomial labels u-beta_i(f) are localized source units with linearly independent classes modulo C(f)^*. Hence the exact localized-unit defect sum_(a(c)=0)(r_c-1) is at least ell. For a cubic with D=b^2-3ac a nonzero square, the two distinct rational critical roots force defect at least two. This counts rational critical roots, not every root after a parameter-field extension, and does not close the residual by itself. HC4MYID0 now gives precise allowed supports for all irreducible normalized critical factors over C(T), not only rational branches: H_i(f,u) can vanish only above leading levels with H_i(c,0)=0. Independence gives every subset rank inequality, so extra defect at an excluded level cannot help. An empty support, equivalently gcd(a,H_i(T,0))=1, excludes a rational root in every degree without a special-fibre hypothesis. HC4MYID1 closes cubic square-critical-discriminant outputs whenever gcd(a,b-H)=1 or gcd(a,b+H)=1, including arbitrary pure-power leading multiplicities with b nonzero at the sole leading zero and the explicit S3 family T^q*z^3+z^2-(2R+T^q*R^2)*z/3+d. No new external theorem is imported. A surviving square-discriminant cubic needs nonempty support for both branches and the subset defect budgets; when gcd(a,b)=1, two separate reducible full f-fibres are required. The two-level coefficient control T*(T-1)*z^3+z^2-4*z/3 passes this necessary support test and is not closed by it. No higher-degree irreducibility is inferred from no rational roots. Both plane endpoints and unrestricted HC4/JC2 remain open. HC4MYID2 adds a global singleton-support pencil obstruction: two reduced rational critical units, each supported at one leading level, force their polynomial critical branches to differ by a nonzero constant. Mutual divisibility modulo the reduced units and ordinary polynomial degrees prove this in arbitrary degrees. In the cubic case a square-free leading coefficient with at most two zeros and gcd(a,b)=1 makes the two populated critical units reduced by the valuation-two Jacobian identity. Thus a nonconstant square critical gap H closes the output even when the support gcd test passes. The old coefficient control T*(T-1)*z^3+z^2-4*z/3 is now closed. A new residual has a=T*(T-1), b=1-2T, c=4/3, H^2=1 and constant critical gap; it is not closed by this argument. Repeated leading multiplicities require a separate reducedness audit. Both plane endpoints and unrestricted HC4/JC2 remain open. lessons_before.title: Test energy-constrained quantization by relative elliptic cohomology before enlarging supports
lessons_before.when: An elliptic-isogeny quantization is proposed to preserve a cubic energy, reparametrize it by a univariate rational series, or deform a curve differential module through a central reduction.
lessons_before.use: Separate the flat algebra deformation from the map deformation. The Hamiltonian Ore algebra has a flat two-parameter PBW family and a localized Weyl central reduction. For the actual normalized three-isogeny, linearize the commutator as a divergence equation and the energy relation as a prescribed Hamiltonian derivative. Rational logarithmic gauges fixing b remove first-order tangential changes. On the generic elliptic level, the second-order compatibility class is -5/(72*b^2)*[x dx/y], independent of every univariate energy correction. Therefore the natural-energy commutator must appear at h order2 or3, exactly3 for even lifts, in every rational spatial degree. Use the explicit unrestricted escape jet to check that energy motion, rather than formal lifting itself, is being obstructed.
lessons_before.avoid: Inferring a nonlifting theorem from a fixed-energy obstruction, keeping the energy in its old centralizer while only raising partner orders, treating a flat deformation of algebras as a deformation of their isogeny module, assuming a rational logarithmic gauge has bounded degree, or extending the arbitrary-first-order rational theorem to every algebraic coefficient cover without proof.
lessons_before.boundary: The theorem uses the normalized rational Moyal fiber and applies to exact-R full formal Long lifts after scalar parameter rescaling. It imposes no common spatial or scalar-order bound, but does not cover nonpositional R deformations or target changes moving the distinguished energy. The second-order class survives finite algebraic fiber covers; the full parity-free theorem is stated only for rational coefficients. Formal pairs exist by unrestricted homotopy and escape via genuinely transverse energy corrections. The flat diagonal central reduction does not construct a compatible module map, the fourth image, or global admission. QPL1 is an explicit full polynomial-coefficient formal Long lift with all six relations, fixed momentum orders0,2,3,5 and a scalar quadratic energy. Its PI coefficients have unbounded spatial support and lie outside the generic algebraic coefficient category. Thus full global admission and finite scalar orders do not remove that field hypothesis. Its S coefficient degrees8n-1 prove growth of this family, not of every formal representative. QGD1 adds an independent constraint on a noncentral-energy bridge: its full Long division image cannot be a finite ambient symmetry fixed ring, even when symmetries move the parameter valuation. Energy motion remains necessary by QEM1 but does not establish finite admission. An S3 Galois closure with an intermediate subgroup-fixed source is not excluded by this direct-quotient theorem. QGC1 requires no exact quantum energy relation and now no original saturation under graph or equivariant admission. Ordinary-parameter identified graph actions admit a finite full valuation-level residue lattice. At arbitrary parameter order, an equivariant quadratic closure with the correct torsion-free special rank is repaired by two central parameter shifts and is excluded by interior ramification. Energy motion still does not establish finite admission. Direct nonsymmetric carriers and matrix actions outside the natural division closure remain open. QRA1 makes b noncentral by adjoining an explicit surface Euler connection and gives a global logarithmic model, but x,y remain commuting coefficient positions. This is not the QEM1 physical isogeny pair with [y,x]=h. Energy noncentrality alone therefore does not provide the missing compatible map. An exact primitive Y=XW with the physical Weyl pair would force X to be a unit; the special norm -4b prevents it globally. Broken quantum primitive relations remain a distinct possible escape. QFR1 gives a punctual physical-plane obstruction distinct from QEM1 generic elliptic de Rham nonexactness. QUR1 excludes all ramified regular lifts of that single monic normalization via a rank-two connection, even with changed energy and primitive. Neither excludes the ordinary rank-one forward Long graph.

lessons_before.use: Use the joint uncentered quadratic-linear Gaussian exponential to encode pure moments by D=det(I-2tA) and H=l^T*adj(I-2tA)*l. Extract the diagonal coefficients with their exact factorial factor. Prove the finite coefficient assertion on the entire D/H parameter space using exhaustive independent L and Q rescalings; verify explicit rational Bezout certificates as cleared-denominator integer identities. For sharpness, certify a proper finite coefficient algebra on a distinct-eigenvalue open set and prove Gaussian realizability by partial fractions. Use actual polynomial automorphisms, including unipotents, for refined tangent bounds.
lessons_before.avoid: Using the centered quadratic trace factor for a homogeneous uncentered quadratic, equating finite moment samples with all-order identities, applying det A!=0 assertions to split quadratics without a separate argument, confusing length28 with28 distinct points, or treating arbitrary invariant coefficients as a Gaussian witness without a realization proof. lessons_before.title: Reduce the whole torus-curvette sector before tackling characteristic gcd chains
lessons_before.when: A smooth affine one-line K=R plane completion has regular-coordinate order r>=2 and complementary pole q coprime to r, or a quartic iterated-knot cover has irreducible atoroidal source and marked exterior with primitive odd cyclic homology. This also applies when r divides q and the largest support index j not divisible by r is coprime to r, including all prime r.
lessons_before.use: Take the actual Laurent charts, choose Bezout toric coordinates, and prove full omitted-line contact m=q-r+2 with the reference jet. Keep the puncture through R6 and the m free blowups: the end is (qr+m)-surgery on T(q,r), with primitive dual knot, atoroidal closed source and atoroidal exterior. Nonzero central-fiber homology, prime decomposition and Poincare give actual radial irreducibility; peripheral Waldhausen then identifies the filled pair. In the quartic proof replace the lens requirement by closed atoroidality. Repeated original cone factors obstruct a primitive regular fiber for every third filling. lessons_before.title: Use sign-paired infinities and invariant quotient values to close a quartic boundary
lessons_before.when: A weighted coefficient model requires a finite cover to express independent invariants, with an even first quotient and odd tail quotients.
lessons_before.use: Include the finite-cover Jacobian factor and independently compare the quotient formula to the full original-source determinant. Complete the first quotient to an even quartic. Smoothness follows from the determinant; the sign involution exchanges both infinities. Oddg has equal pole orders there, and rho=h/g^3 is invariant, so its infinity values agree. Subtract their common value and compare total zero degree8m+2 to finite pole degree6m. After the product branch reduction, use exact cleared identities for every coefficient stratum. Reconstruct all transverse linear constraints, retain parity, remove a constant cubic tail by a polynomial target shear and use coefficient orders and nonresonant polynomial operators to exclude the residual univariate forms. For a linear-first family, a generic plane inverse can descend overK[a] by uniqueness of a formal inverse with unimodular linear part.
lessons_before.avoid: Treating the mixed-weight invariant ring as a free polynomial ring without a covering factor; reusing a one-infinity pole count at only one of two poles; assuming independent infinity values can be subtracted simultaneously; discarding the extra factor of a generic full-field lift; inferring global exclusion from eight fixed first-coefficient samples; claiming arithmetic replay formalizes curve theory or re-proves the imported plane theorem.
lessons_before.boundary: KCUB17 closes the complete16-slot weight(2,-1,-3) degree<=7 Keller model. The written paired-infinity proof forcesP*T=0, two replayed identities use69 multiplier monomials,maxdegree7, and complete parity/degree reductions close the remaining branches. The f=1 family has degree<=5 overK(a), with a precise Nakai-Baba prime/degree4 import and formal-inverse argument. The original20/30-second query failures and unused generic/full fixed-slice experiments remain retained. No construction bound changes and no global minimum is closed. KCUB18 subsequently closes the complete weight(1,-1,-3) class through degree7 by a highest-transverse-degree split and seven exact identities. All original timeout/UNKNOWN records remain unchanged.
lessons_before.reopen_when: Change weights, ordinary degree, polynomial-coordinate class or the construction/special form. Do not rerun unchanged models in any of the four completed degree<=7 weight sectors. Cubic dimensions below12, terms below36, cubic-linear dimension below89, normalized3D support below48, and raw support below13 outside the closed sector remain distinct open directions.

lessons_before.title: Straighten the whole ambient function and close every affine graph direction before expanding source parameterizations
lessons_before.when: A Meng--Yang graph or embedding is proposed after nonlinear ambient changes, or an all-degree obstruction is sought without increasing graph coefficients.
lessons_before.use: Use the retained HC5T1 Bezout frame and C0 normalizer, then the shear Z=z+y*(6v^2+15v+4)*t and translation T=t+M/(2L). This gives a genuine ambient polynomial automorphism and the full identity Psi=lambda_star+L*T^2+N*y*Z+2*N*x*W. For a literal affine graph, a nonisotropic normal direction completes to quadratic plus one square, while an isotropic direction leaves a nondegenerate ternary quadratic hyperplane trace. Elementary jointly-affine-plane arguments after Tang force a triangular Keller inverse in both cases. A constant rank-four normal projection affine-linear in the actual source parameters is sufficient. General encodings remain a five-generator quadratic representation problem. HC4MYHN0/1 now lower the ambient affine projection gate from four to three, including all degenerate quadratic kernels and fully nonlinear remaining coordinates. Restricted source planes expose one-extra-generator Keller recovery, while the other cases give a triangular component or affine-line fibre. There is a genuine unit-Hessian example with exactly three affine retained projections, so this strengthens the graph theorem. Two-affine normal embeddings already realize both distinct conditional endpoints with actual polynomial inverses, and no full two-affine closure or JC2 equivalence is claimed. HC4MYHO0/1/2 now separate complete endpoint branches in the two-affine geometry: a unit two-directional-partial ideal forces a unique vertical cotangent plane and an explicit relative coordinate; aligned nondegenerate kernel rank three is exactly the unit-ideal endpoint. All affine-hyperplane normal image types are classified under arbitrary source reparameterizations into the old singleton-zero/coordinate orbits or a forbidden critical-line case. New directions beyond those endpoints require nonlinear normal image hypersurfaces. No unaligned two-affine closure or singleton uniqueness from mere attainment is claimed. HC4MYHP0/1 now require checking the whole polynomial quadratic-similitude saturation, since explicit genuine nonlinear images can have zero affine pullbacks while their unchanged source potential is a closed quadratic. lessons_before.title: Classify finite-momentum formal fixed-R gauges and keep the unbounded-momentum comparison open
lessons_before.when: Comparing a putative bounded exact-R Long lift with QPL1, extending a formal centralizer gauge to its fourth image, or testing whether the Euler connection forces the PI form.
lessons_before.use: Use multiplicative operator order in X*(1+X*Y)=r to force finite-order position images to remain positional. Factor them with f in h*K[x,y][[h]], compute the formal-unit Jacobian j, and write the centralizer image as j^-1*b+F. Full extension and fourth-image admission are equivalent to global coefficientwise exactness j*F=theta(G). All finite b orders are preserved in this category. The unique formal comparison with a bounded exact-R target must therefore have unbounded momentum in a position image. Use the global Hamiltonian H=I^2, I=(X^3*w+w*X^3)/2, as a control: its arbitrary-contact flow fixes R and K exactly but has unbounded momentum.
lessons_before.avoid: Extending QGR1 position-fixing rigidity from finite spatial support to all formal gauges, assuming exact R and K force finite momentum, or using one unbounded transported frame as all-representative nonlifting.
lessons_before.boundary: The full classification assumes both position images have uniformly finite momentum order, but allows unbounded position degree and puts no initial bound on b. The necessary momentum escape concerns bounded exact-R targets; nonpositional first images are outside it. The invariant flows themselves give unbounded frames, not bounded candidates or counterexamples to a bounded-target-specific theorem. Universal statements have written proofs and finite exact controls, without independent or external review. QPG1 compares unrestricted full formal lifts by a finite exact polynomial shear word followed by an inner formal unit; inner conjugacy alone is equivalent to agreement modulo t*a(t). Its intermediate shear words need not fix R, and its inner unit can have unbounded spatial and momentum support. It preserves existence of a good formal-module algebraization, not the raw momentum bounds of a representative or the fixed-R hypotheses here.
lessons_before.reopen_when: A property of an actual bounded target controls its unique comparison beyond the finite-momentum category, an invariant survives unbounded-momentum formal transport with the full boundary lattice, or a bounded full carrier is constructed.

lessons_before.title: Recognize the unique relative submersion plane and classify affine image relations before exploring nonlinear two-affine encodings
lessons_before.when: A two-affine normal embedding has a unit ideal of two directional partials, a cotangent-aligned constant-fibre description, or an affine relation among its five normal coordinate pullbacks.
lessons_before.use: Under unit Hessian a global unit ideal (f_u,f_v) excludes the rank-two and rank-one projections of Tang plane W to the chosen base; only the vertical plane remains, with f=D+uF+vG and (F,G)=(1). A base Bezout certificate gives an actual relative inverse. A closed aligned rank-three kernel fibre cannot be constant over a coefficient zero: a ternary quadric is either a singular cone or has E=T^2+T, never A2; the converse unit-ideal embedding is explicit. For an affine hyperplane image compute nu=ell*H^(-1)*ell^T and its offset: nonisotropic gives the singleton orbit, isotropic off-center gives the coordinate/unit-ideal orbit, and isotropic through-center gives a forbidden critical line. These are all-degree global reductions. HC4MYHQ0/1 enlarge the output-base obstruction to linear-quadratic ambient observables through a global quadric filtration, without requiring ambient coordinate completion or fibre rectification. HC4MYHR0/1 now test relative critical sections and curve products and classify every base-only quadratic graph under unrestricted relative free-variable automorphisms, without alignment and with at most one full critical point under unit Hessian. lessons_before.avoid: Using generic or individual fibre submersions as a global unit ideal; asserting cotangent alignment for every two-affine embedding; dropping closed embedding from constant-fibre dimension comparison; treating rank-one origin attainment as singleton uniqueness; claiming either plane endpoint solved by hyperplane-image classification; exploring higher source degrees in an already exact endpoint branch.
lessons_before.boundary: All earlier three-affine and ambient quadratic obstructions remain valid. Two directional partials generating the global unit ideal now force their unique plane to be the cotangent plane, give a globally affine free-variable form and an explicit relative coordinate inverse. The aligned rank-three quadratic kernel branch is exactly the unit-ideal plane endpoint. All affine-hyperplane normal images, under arbitrary source parameterizations, are exactly the singleton-zero orbit, the unit-ideal coordinate orbit, or the isotropic-through-center critical-line branch that forbids unit Hessian. Neither endpoint is resolved. Rank-one aligned fibre attainment is not singleton uniqueness; unaligned two-affine embeddings and nonlinear normal image hypersurfaces remain open with the unrestricted row equation. Polynomial quadratic-similitude saturation is now an additional global gate: if q composed with an ambient polynomial automorphism is a*q, undo it in the same source parameters before classifying retained projections or hyperplane images. The entire saturated three-affine class stays closed; the full-source hyperplane saturation retains exactly the old two endpoints or critical-line obstruction. Explicit unbounded words give zero affine pullbacks and nonlinear image equations while preserving a unit-Hessian quadratic source potential. Raw image nonlinearity is therefore insufficient. No universal rectification or generation of every quadratic symmetry is asserted. The output-base obstruction now includes a linear observable paired with any nondegenerate ambient quadratic, not only ambient coordinate pairs. In all stable dimensions r>=2, generic quadric factoriality and a height-one-compatible monomial filtration make the pencil and denominator arguments global, and smoothness forces the plane Keller base invertible. Thus an intrinsic nonautomorphic cotangent pair cannot have such an ambient extension, even after a certified ambient polynomial automorphism. Direct native A/B encodings of an independent Keller pair collapse to an invertible pair and a coordinate potential. Both plane endpoints and arbitrary other source-pair extensions remain open; no surface-quadric factoriality or embedding rectification is assumed. Relative critical schemes now give a separate global gate. A polynomial section over a constant two-variable base, or a base-compatible smooth curve times A1 with vertical Hessian rank one, forces gradient invertibility under unit Hessian. Consequently every base-only normal graph j=(s,t,h(s,t),H,G) under arbitrary relative free-variable polynomial automorphisms has at most one full critical point under unit Hessian, with no cotangent alignment. Its nonautomorphic members are exactly the two old endpoint source orbits. Native graph members with multiple full critical points have no relative unitization over that fixed base. Arbitrary four-variable source mixing and three genuinely free-dependent unretained coordinates remain open. One proper relative Morse component now suffices: no condition on other components is needed, and a globally proper everywhere-Morse relative projection can only have degree one. Each nonautomorphic component must therefore fail properness or contain vertical degeneracy. However each single condition separately retains exactly JC2. The universal f_M model has relative projection K and vertical Hessian -DK^T*DK, while the finite-free Fermat construction gives every K a proper relative projection with explicit monomial basis and ramification at zero. Its properness is not properness of K. Neither model automatically supplies a compatible closed ambient embedding. The two plane endpoints and unrestricted graph compatibility remain open. Uniform quadratic two-planes now have the same unique-plane rigidity under nonautomorphy as affine ones: any genuinely quadratic constant two-plane or two distinct quadratic planes closes the candidate. This classifies every fibre-affine two-affine embedding j=(s,t,b+A*w) in all base degrees. Global source generation requires a polynomial left inverse of A; generic rank is not enough. Alignment follows under nonautomorphy, a rank-three helper quadratic closes unconditionally, and lower ranks force a base-only helper and the two old endpoints. All unit-Hessian members have at most one full critical point. Arbitrary nonlinear free helpers and nonaligned potentials of free degree at least three remain open. Nonlinear isotropic-ideal image graphs now have explicit global quadratic isometries to hyperplanes, with arbitrary coefficients in unchanged variables and all source parameterizations. Compatible positive linear ambient weights give a constructive recognition gate: a smooth invariant image either has an isotropic tangent normal forbidding unit Hessian, or its lower-weight nonlinear terms admit a weighted Euler shear to the nonisotropic hyperplane. Only the singleton-zero endpoint survives for these positive images. Actual positive linear source weights would close gradient invertibility, but image invariance alone does not supply that hypothesis after nonlinear source changes. Other nonlinear images and both plane endpoints remain open. lessons_before.title: Use finite-left full graph descent before requiring a scalar free frame
lessons_before.when: An algebraic full quantum graph carrier is sought but its rank-one free frame is unresolved, or a finite projective corner is proposed as a substitute for full right actions.
lessons_before.use: Require a finite-left R-flat h-Weyl bimodule with the identified classical graph, not just a coherent bimodule or formally free left completion. Generic projectivity follows from the cited finite-left bimodule lemma and the classical presentation forces rank one. Use a nonzero algebraic dual section to transport the rational right action: it has the same residue map and completed degree delta. Left and dual growth filtrations bound both finite generic indices below by delta. Stafford stabilization makes two copies free, so delta>1 forces a non-surjective Mat_2(A_n) endomorphism. A finite idempotent with admitted corner generators and scalar graph reduction is an explicit sufficient certificate. Test compression defects before claiming those generators satisfy Weyl relations. Use QPG1 central patching after proving generic finite projectivity and an admitted C-frame; if the generic module is rank-one free, its integral frame follows automatically. For generic rank-one full actions, QVA1 now supplies C-admission from Gauss-regularity and the intended shadow; it need not be assumed separately.
lessons_before.avoid: Treating a matrix result as a scalar A_n endomorphism, requiring a scalar frame before recognizing progress from an actual full algebraic carrier, assuming projectivity supplies a right action, substituting central curve energy for noncentral Weyl data, or applying prescribed arithmetic-support nonlifting from classical reduction alone.
lessons_before.boundary: This is a carrier criterion and a matrix realization theorem, not a constructed Long carrier. The scalar route retains its generic or parameter-compatible rank-one frame gate. Generic projectivity uses Kanel-Belov-Fedorov Lemma3.1 without its separate arithmetic-support hypothesis; generic two-copy freeness uses Stafford Theorem3.6. Neither external theorem is independently replayed. Finite-left carrier generation does not imply finite generation of the different valuation lattice governing equality of generic and completed division degree. The positive control is the identity graph; the QPF1 compression is a negative control. QPH1 constructs a full finite two-by-two phase representation but its left rank is two, not QMC1 rank one, and its second classical branch has an X=0 pole. Its phase form has no algebraic branch summand for any nonconstant finite polynomial g_h, by absolute irreducibility of a nonsingular polynomial connection; the original quadratic case also has a weighted order2/3 proof. Formal extraction gives a second global Long lift with exact S coefficient degree10n-1 and momentum order n. A linear-g example has a different finite scalar realization despite phase nonsplitting, so this excludes the chosen phase construction, not every algebraization or full quantum representative. QFT1 extends the phase exclusion to every minimal rational pre-Fourier line with h-regular coefficient and classical polynomial degree at least three, including logarithmic amplitudes and moving rational poles. Its one-puncture monodromy criterion is uniform over all finite covers in rank at least three. A true rank-two split and generic-rank-two/formal-rank-one degeneration mark the boundary: higher generic pre-Fourier rank and separately audited nonminimal constituents remain possible. No actual Long carrier follows. QKR1 supplies an all-rank cyclic-cover budget r>=(1-1/e)N+irr_0; N>2r excludes cyclic power splitting and, with one finite puncture, all finite covers. Boundary delta factors add inverse-Fourier rank. A genuinely splitting all-degree family S=g(a)+2v has inverse rank deg(g)+1, but its quadratic Long branch fails QSO2. QVM1 excludes every finite mate, on all finite coefficient covers, when S has v-leading term v*H(a), deg H>=2 and root-multiplicity gcd one, with arbitrary lower-growth terms. The candidate v*(2+h*a^3)+4a-3r*a^2 passes N6/r3 and branch extraction but fails this all-order mate test. Proper-power H, different leading faces and nonpositional first images remain outside it. No actual Long carrier follows. QVL1 transports repeated roots to nonlinear ordinary infinity limits and closes all proper-power v-linear repairs when lower coefficients are bounded. Together with QVM1, every leading H of degree>=2 is excluded in that entire Laurent class, with arbitrary finite partner order and algebraic coefficient covers. Euler limits and finite Newton support certificates give further tests. A remaining exact-R scalar Long model in the v-linear rational Laurent class has H degree<=1 and inverse-Fourier rank at least four, by QSO2 and a positive infinity Newton contribution. The family 2v*(1+h*a)^k+4a-3ra^2 is excluded for every k>=2, even though k3 passes N6/r3 and branch extraction. Nonlinear-limit commuting Darboux algebras cannot supply a scalar generator, but other operators in larger idealizers remain outside that assertion. Other leading faces, fractional positive lower growth for nonprimitive H, H degree<=1 and nonpositional first images remain open. QZM1 gives a zero-mode cokernel test with finite-cover trace retraction and covariance under actual finite algebra automorphisms, provided the module is transported too. A new position localization can kill the vector and is not justified by trace. It excludes v*(lambda*a+mu)+G(a) for every nonconstant polynomial G and every finite scalar mate order or algebraic coefficient cover. Combined with QVL1, the pure separable class v*H(a)+G(a) with both H and G nonconstant is closed; the leading-linear rank-four cubic and derivative-tuned cubic are excluded. QPC1 subsequently closes the H-constant nonlinear-G case by a universal p-power coefficient. The complete pure polynomial v*H(a)+G(a) Long form is therefore excluded, including every finite momentum degree and coefficient cover. Additional negative-v corrections, genuine mixed coefficients, other leading faces and deformed first images remain outside this classification. Conditional global pair transport clears c(R) and requires [R,T]=0; it neither admits every chart formula nor identifies QRF2 with this new class. QPC1 also gives linear trace descent for a fixed operator mate and the necessary matrix-fiber condition chi_S derivative zero. Scalar p-centrality requires central degree p and fails for general phase matrices; no arbitrary carrier exclusion follows. QAD1 supplies an arbitrary-scalar mixed-coefficient admission test: nonzero Adler periods exclude even bounded-above PDO mates, whereas finite differential existence is exactly constant-linear membership in the full almost-commuting defect span. It identifies a characteristic-zero residue proportional to QPC1 gamma_n. Vanishing periods construct only a PDO mate, as the harmonic control demonstrates; neither an h-pole dressing nor a finite defect prefix supplies a finite full carrier. This does not compare arbitrary Fourier completions, identify QRF2 or cover nonscalar matrix actions. The finite leading-divisor gate is stronger than the first PDO period test: if gcd(operator order, all leading-coefficient zero/pole orders)=1, the entire base low-order commutator image is zero by finite power subtraction. This excludes every nonconstant squarefree polynomial leading coefficient, with arbitrary mixed lower terms and all finite coefficient covers. Prime operator orders over K(v) require a scalar times an nth power leading coefficient. The separate rational leading PDO equation Qprime-(Hprime/(n*H))*Q=v tests algebraic primitive exactness; its squarefree degree>=3 exclusion strengthens to PDO mates. A passing leading condition remains necessary, and nonscalar matrix carriers are not classified. QSC1 proves Cent_classical(R,S)=K[R,S] and commutativity of the full formal joint centralizer for every commuting Long deformation, including nonpositional first images. Faithful finite/corner and QMC1 full-carrier endomorphism algebras inherit commutativity. Global spectral Koszul classes exactly test the two individual conjugates; if they vanish, one algebraic curvature class exactly tests flat completion. All spectral fibers can pass while the global class fails, and a formally exact curvature can have nonzero rational double residue. If both matrix positions are scalar, normalized matrix trace scalarizes a full completion without degree growth. This does not scalarize genuinely matrix-valued positions or free a projective carrier, identify QRF2, or construct a finite Long lift. QST1 separates rational and spectral admission. Any nonzero Adler period excludes the entire rational operator division ring and makes the universal spectral class nontorsion; the G(a)+mu*v first period is explicit in all degrees. This blocks every rational conjugate and the corresponding actual rank-one projective pair orbit without a scalar free frame. Fixed rational mate equations descend through finite algebraic coefficient covers by monic-denominator Galois averaging. Constant-coefficient G has instead a critical-value torsion annihilator and a rational mate. Zero Adler periods are insufficient for rational admission: a torus residue excludes harmonic/Euler functional classes even with arbitrary operator denominators and identity spectators. Finite primitive-divisor and ordinary infinity exclusions must not be silently promoted to rational ones. No arbitrary moving spectral coefficient localization, nonlinear Galois descent or universal Long rational normalization is proved. QFC1 supplies a positive full-corner completion gate if a finite corner already has commuting positions, integral individual conjugates and actual centralizer module finiteness. It does not construct that corner or prove its finite-left graph hypotheses. Generic module finiteness suffices, but a scalar Bernstein symbol filtration cannot be assumed for an arbitrary projective idealizer. QET1's etale/Galois centralizer route extends to a projective endomorphism algebra only after verifying its actual centralizer is finitely generated, its fraction field finite over the images and no nonconstant base polynomial is a unit. Scalar Weyl unit and dimension bounds cannot be silently transferred to an arbitrary idealizer. No new corner or full Long graph is supplied. QET1 also removes actual parameter poles under the polynomial classical centralizer hypothesis, with no finite-generation or field-degree assumption: individual mates have unique finite polynomial polar parts. Subtraction preserves any integral curvature exactly, so an actual generic flat tuple with regular positions descends to a finite integral flat tuple and can match a prescribed classical flat frame. Only h is inverted; rational spatial/operator denominators and arbitrary completed series remain outside this descent. QTB1 removes the centralizer finite-generation requirement from the birational and Galois-factor route, including another actual algebra only after its algebraicity, horizontal constants and base-unit condition are verified. Scalar Weyl units and radical descent under constant extension are not automatically transferred to a projective idealizer. No new finite corner or full Long carrier is constructed. QPD1 verifies scalar units, centralizer algebraicity and horizontal constants automatically for rank-one finite projective Weyl endomorphism orders, and clears rational commutants by spectral denominators. QTB1 tests therefore apply without a scalar free frame or centralizer finite generation. Actual commutativity is still needed, supplied for Long by QSC1. Generic projectivity of a full carrier retains QMC1's explicit external theorem; no carrier is constructed. QCI1 applies to the rank-one projective order of a full carrier without a scalar free frame. The coefficient-saturated division tower has N=d*M with residual M>=3 for Long, and d>1 forces N>=9. A coefficient-field-only realization or rational target polarization of the fixed positions is impossible. This does not exclude arbitrary higher-rank matrix positions, identify QIM1 curve fields with H or supply a finite carrier. QCI1 supplies an arbitrary-positive-rank lattice obstruction independent of projectivity: a rational matrix with bounded Bernstein powers can preserve a full finite Weyl lattice only when it is algebraic over the scalar field, and then it has no Weyl mate. The rational residual degree3 pair (x^-2*p/3,x^3), diagonally repeated and conjugated by any rational matrix frame, is therefore excluded in every finite rank. Negative-degree nilpotent matrices can preserve finite lattices, so arbitrary matrix entries and different representations are not excluded. QGD1 applies inside the rank-one division realization of a full Long carrier without a free scalar frame. Its full image W cannot be D^G for any finite group of ambient division automorphisms, whether or not the group preserves a finite order or the h-valuation. The whole automorphism group Aut_W(D) is finite of order g, divides both generic indices, and each index is at least3g. This excludes a direct symmetry-quotient carrier, not arbitrary genuinely matrix-valued right actions or a larger Galois closure with an intermediate subgroup-fixed source. QGC1 now excludes the natural larger Long closure with the intended admission without assuming saturation. The ordinary-parameter classical graph gives finite full valuation-level lattices. For a finite group closure with special rank delta and no S-torsion, generic rank comparison forces group order delta and valuation invariance; split characters then give a finite saturated repair. Long relative quadratic group is necessarily order2, so this covers every parameter ramification. The ordinary rank-one Long graph remains allowed. General matrix repairs and special modules with torsion or excess rank are not silently admitted as the closure field. QIR1 upgrades generic to integral projectivity for every parameter order and makes the finite normalized corner equations necessary and sufficient for a full graph carrier. One elementary stabilization normalizes the special idempotent without a formal inverse. In a fixed rational action there is only one generic full finite lattice; rank-one integral graph models differ by central powers. No Long corner or scalar free frame is supplied. QTC1 composes actual finite corners by entrywise block substitution, with product matrix size and degree bound. Generic indices and completed degrees multiply, so strict index excess cannot cancel. A carrier dual is finite on the target right side; composing over the source need not stay finite on the target left. For noninvertible classical maps the evaluation kernel has a nonfinite off-diagonal special fiber. No Long carrier is supplied by this operation. QRA1 gives genuine full matrix Weyl actions from any finite free polynomial-coordinate map, including ramified companions of every size with degree at most2. Their special left rank is the cover degree. The regular generic action is irreducible and cannot rationally compress to rank1 or admit the commuting matrix units needed to extend this same action to a matrix algebra endomorphism. Full generator relations in a larger matrix algebra alone are therefore not a QMC1 counterexample. The global monic elliptic A2 action is an explicit rank3 control. QFR1 finite-jet frames already exclude ordinary and order-two physical lifts of its special monic module. QUR1 excludes every parameter order for that single module, even after changing its parameter-flat algebraic left model. Its repolarized rank-two proof is not a theorem for arbitrary higher multiplicities or added summands. No rank-one Long carrier is supplied. QPG1 glues a finite projective generic full action to its admitted rank-one formal graph over C=Ahat[1/t], producing an actual integral finite carrier. If the generic left module is free of rank one, the integral carrier is already free; no additional parameter-frame theorem is needed. A nonfree generic projective class still separates the matrix conclusion from scalar realization. No generic Long action or C-frame is supplied. QVA1 gives an exact generic construction gate: finite projective rank-one full action plus Gauss-regular intrinsic Long shadow. Its valuation-ideal proof produces C-freeness and QPG1 supplies the integral finite carrier. Generic rank-one freeness gives the scalar lift; generic nonfreeness retains the matrix result. Neither a rational full tuple alone nor the new criterion constructs the missing generic Long action.
