lessons_before.title: Use universal monodromy and isotropy before constructing a finite canonical receiver
lessons_before.when: Constructing canonical marked etale receivers, comparing fixed universality with input-wise descent, or trying to identify quotient source and target.
lessons_before.use: For finite homogeneous receivers keep the pair/self-map distinction, connected-isotropy obstruction and disconnected-isotropy costs. Torus quotients have exact finite strong prime-power degrees and symmetric ceiling4. When a nonfinite whole-affine canonical receiver is required, UACANFIB1 now supplies an all-rank polynomial vector-bundle self-map with full S_N marked fibre. UACANVOL1 states its explicit decomposition; neither homogeneous-pair topology nor generic monodromy automaticity proves atomicity at a smaller marked boundary rank. UAPARALLEL1 closes arbitrary polynomial profiles in all retained first outputs: every block subset has a polynomial factor even with cycles. UAWEILATOM1 gives exact ground-field stable length from the field-component count of A after the chosen base extension. The one-direction joint theorem remains complete. UAMULTIKER1 extends the exact common kernel C[Z] to every return rank. UABASICTIME1 factors selectors proved to lie in C[Z,t], even for nonlinear time Keller maps and cyclic nilpotent matrices. UAMARKEDDEF1 preserves the complete marked restrictions by vanishing ideals in a retained first output, giving atomic auxiliary maps of every generic degree d>=3 and preserving any prescribed finite-order thickening and canonical receiver deformations which still factor. UARETURNESC1 gives actual non-descended rank-two and full-rank escapes from the old cubic factor; full canonical atomicity still needs a separate proof. UAROOTDAG1 closes arbitrary polynomial corrections in all retained signals and source roots X_i=x_i*q_i: Keller forces the exact self equation and an effective DAG. UAROOTFACT1 gives polynomial order-ideal models and absolute stable atomic block stages even for some genuinely non-descended rank-two selectors. UAROOTSYM1 groups these into equivariant orbit factors; a transitive action on all blocks has complete fixed-target fibre T0^N and cannot give the natural N-label cover. UASELFCTRL1 closes one affine coefficient line with arbitrary own-source polynomial controls, and even rational controls if the WHOLE output map extends polynomially: only retained-signal effective profiles survive. UASELFLAUR1 supplies the exact nonlinear response and reciprocal-Riccati/pole proof. UASELFFORMAL1 provides all-order formal marked deformations and a genuine source denominator as the concrete next integration gate. UANATIVE2GEN1 replaces every finite native list by two unique effective source controls without changing the map. UAAFFINER1 closes all one-block affine-r controls and gives a fixed-size determinant equation for the nonlinear remainder. UASIGFIELD1 identifies stable signal-field normalizers as weighted compiler scalings plus vertical Keller maps. UAETALEGAUGE1 says the marked finite/formal examples are unique source coordinate changes, with necessarily unbounded source degrees in the explicit scalar family. UAQFSAT1 supplies polynomial descent for any dominant quasi-finite affine-space self-map. UANATIVEORBIT1 classifies the full native profile-coordinate orbit: affine Cout, generic affine-pair reducibility and signal-field-respecting stable profile equivalence all give the unique shear ideal (a^5*c^3). Its finite polynomial-r degree reduction closes the whole quadratic sector. UACUBICDESC1 tests an actual old cubic factor by reducing each output to its three fixed field-basis coefficients; no target-degree ansatz is needed. UAPROFFACT1 upgrades the native profile orbit to complete rational factor rigidity: recovery through ANY retained profile forces its unique target shear, by the already imported published HC4MYGL0 line theorem. UARPLANE1 converts the nonnegative-r generic leaf sector to an actual plane completion with Jacobian 1-SY. UAPLANEATOM1 makes every such completion plane-indecomposable and excludes signal-retaining whole factors whose intermediate coordinates also extend across its hyperbola. UARELPLANE1 cancels a plane Keller target whenever the final curve is a closed embedding, with no boundary-extension hypothesis. UASIGFACT1 closes EVERY native signal-retaining whole factorization, including negative Laurent-r sectors. UAINTERSURF1 replaces the former pole gate by the exact generic intermediate surface under arbitrary stabilization mixing: noninvertible target stages require a NON-PLANE fibre with the stated smooth complete-intersection, tangent, curve, unit, divisor and saturation constraints. UAPRIMUNIT1 closes the cofinite etale surface class with primitive source unit. UAUNITFACT1 uses published whole polynomial root closure to make every nonconstant geometric unit primitive and invert the source stage. A proper arbitrary stabilized native intermediate is therefore GEOMETRICALLY UNIT-FREE and non-plane, has arithmetic UFD ring and an all-irreducible-constant-fibre whole signal component. At every chain cut the unit lattice is either full Z or zero, dropping once at the first noninvertible prefix. UALOGVOL1 closes all nonnegative-logarithmic intermediates after a noninvertible source stage, by the actual r^2 whole-volume multiplier and log pullback on boundary resolutions. UAGEOPIC1 then forces NONZERO geometric Picard group for proper native factors, while its retained-field Galois invariant subgroup is ZERO by rational-point-normalized descent. UADANVOL1 excludes every ordinary smooth Danielewski exponent-one surface by a volume period; higher exponents have an explicit regular primitive. UAPLANECHART1 tests the ENTIRE carried line against EVERY open A2 chart: containment in any one inverts the whole target. Formal etaleness still makes all its finite/formal neighborhoods standard. UADANCHART1 exposes exact simultaneous Keller gluing on the classical Danielewski atlas, a JC(2)-level burden, nondividing ruling degrees and multi-root contact constraints. Its sharp beta-integral contact family fails geometric injectivity in every exponent. UAARITHRULING1 turns ANY actually descended affine-line ruling into a finite geometric plane atlas: arithmetic fibres are integral and geometric fibres reduced. A proper native factor would give JC(2) counterexamples and its whole curve must hit two components of one split fibre. UAPRODUCTTOPO1 uses source Euler characteristic1 and pi1=Z^N on actual product leaves to exclude finite proper stages and force a finite-index abelian intermediate subgroup with index dividing source degree. UAORBFIB1 excludes all multiple-fibre patterns over A1 except one fibre or two doubles, with even source degree in the latter case. UAMLFACTOR1 identifies the trivial-geometric-ML branch exactly with target invertibility in the native class. UAAFFDESC1 PROVES uniqueness and descent of every geometric AFFINE-type ruling: center at the rational point, take a nonzero weighted Galois trace in its stable coordinate line, and contract the actual volume to obtain a retained-field additive action.
lessons_before.avoid: Identifying different quotient source and target by affine stabilization, equating central-by-finite with virtually abelian, reading specified-group versality as full symmetric universality, or applying the full-degree universal-monodromy theorem to the trace filter. Do not search larger polynomial degrees in these closed rank-one cubic-return or retained-output coupling classes, or confuse a cyclic dependence graph with the removal of an intermediate field. Do not replace a non-descended Schur matrix by an ordinary time Jacobian without proving descent, or confuse generic covering degree with total coordinate degree. Do not deepen root-only polynomial profile degrees while retaining every first signal, equate ordinary nilpotence with vanishing of all principal minors, or read apparent coefficient-list cycles before effective cancellation. Do not freeze the scalar response at coefficient zero, infer polynomial integration from every finite Keller jet or a full formal series, or treat a rational source-open formula as an entire affine map. Do not add more native indices as independent control channels, infer map-degree bounds from the normal-form indices, treat finite/formal source-coordinate existence as a polynomial family, or confuse sigma composed F with a retained first output. Do not treat nonlinear-r B output or arbitrarily high marked contact as a new stable class: explicit whole polynomial target shears already have both. Do not infer atomicity from a nonzero cubic descent remainder, or replace native polynomial-module membership by the source jets alone. Do not reopen the conditional native degree-greater-than-one after-profile branch: it is now empty. Do not deepen searches for polynomial plane decompositions of the completed native map, apply the Keller line theorem directly to its nonconstant Jacobian, or infer stable full-map atomicity from plane indecomposability. Do not reopen the former intermediate boundary-pole route: it is now closed in the entire signal-retaining class. Do not identify a generic intermediate fibre with A2 without proof, assume abstractly isomorphic source surfaces imply trivial factor degrees, or treat a generic etale formula as a whole polynomial factor. Do not reopen the nonconstant-unit intermediate branch or allow a proper finite-index unit lattice in a whole Keller factor. Do not substitute a generic J_d surface cover for whole power descent, remove the retained node, infer geometric factoriality from arithmetic localization, or claim that a unit-free surface has been excluded. Do not reopen nonnegative-log surfaces, geometrically factorial proper native factors or invariant geometric divisor classes. Do not import the finite torus-domination classification into our nonfinite maps, use the obsolete two-surface log-zero list, or turn an exact primitive into an etale plane pair. Higher-power primitive formulas and lattice models do not construct either arrow. Do not identify the raw singular retained-base spread with an actual whole Keller intermediate. Do not turn standard formal curve neighborhoods into a global plane chart, glue plane automorphisms into a non-plane etale target, or call the classical chart-to-JC(2) reduction new. Do not substitute local contacts for the whole closed embedded curve, or search increasing degrees inside the excluded beta-integral family or low/divisibly reducible ruling sector. Do not replace geometric ruling existence after finite extension by descent to K0, transfer arithmetic UFD across that extension, or accept multiple geometric components with multiplicity>1 in a descended ruling. lessons_before.boundary: Finite normal-affine atomicity and nonfinite same-variety self-atomicity are different categories. lessons_before.title: Use the full-branch Orevkov quotient for every zero-excess ramification packet and retain explicit tangency costs
lessons_before.when: A plane Keller normalization has any number of ramified primes of any indices whose image maps are birational and immersive (zero excess); particularly the sole quartic packet left after PF2RULED45.
lessons_before.use: At each image value use the full finite local cover, whose cyclic factors lie on disjoint sheet clusters. Its local monodromy image is abelian, so the global representation factors through O(B) for the FULL branch union B. The transitive monodromy G must be nonabelian: abelian would be regular and Galois, but any branch defining polynomial pulls back to a source curve giving an unramified place over that branch. Hence any primary theorem making O(B) abelian excludes the full cover in every degree and index, without an S_d assumption. With a sole e2 prime the quotient is O(C)->S_d. Apply precise published abelianity criteria, not assumed positivity of polynomial infinity links. Use Nori directly in the nodal case; for quartic tangential double values include all m blowups of total multiplicity2, including final boundary separation, to obtain a_n<=1+2T. Independently classify unramified affine pieces by y=z^r,x=z^(1-r)t+h and pairwise translation poles; the common residue r*c_r is their complete exactness test.
lessons_before.avoid: Treating unramified omitted images as branch curves of the finite normalization; deleting an omitted prime before using finite monodromy; confusing the nonproperness union C union H with branch support C; applying a nodal positivity inequality to tangent double points without the finite blowup cost; inferring all polynomial links are positive braids, inferring nonabelianness from failure of a sufficient test, or using the withdrawn general Jacobian reduction; reopening high-index quartic rows already excluded by QPK4.
lessons_before.boundary: The all-index, multi-prime O(B)->G quotient requires residue-one immersive ramified image maps (zero excess), retains the full branch union and has nonabelian G without necessarily symmetric G. Positive braids for the whole branch union and the precise Neumann--Norbury class are excluded. Positive-excess/cusp local factors can be nonabelian and need new data. Only the distinct-image two-prime indices2,1 zero-excess quartic case remains; it is non-surjective and its ramified image has a double value. Every admissible unramified normal-form datum is actual smooth affine geometry, but exactness and the source LND do not supply a finite Keller target. 150 exact controls support primary-imported written proofs, not a topological formalization or independent review. Full two-prime quartic and higher-degree exclusions remain open.
lessons_before.reopen_when: Compare the two componentwise coordinate valuations in the same source ring and full finite target algebra. For the ramified image prioritize surviving nonpositive infinity types and their actual Orevkov quotient, canonical number and tangential contact budget. For several ramified primes use the simultaneous branch-union diagram and actual group G. For positive excess retain the noncommuting local inertia rather than assuming Orevkov factorization. Historical receipt limits remain sealed; audit their retained claims and canonical sources rather than forcing obsolete frontiers into the current next step.

lessons_before.title: Replace generic factoriality by abelian class-group monodromy and test affine height-one geometric integrality
lessons_before.when: A closed stable hypersurface embedding carries a plane Keller pair through ambient polynomial observables, but generic fibres are nonfactorial or some height-one associated graded fibres are reducible.
lessons_before.use: Use the elementary no-abelian-intermediate-field lemma for Keller maps. With a torsion-free generic Weil class group and abelian Galois action, an image-component class stabilizer must be the whole Galois group. The principal sum of conjugate components then makes each component principal. A common free filtration still supplies generic degree additivity, while geometric integrality of affine height-one fibres suffices for primitive saturation. This closes nonfactorial quadric surfaces, every r>=1 nondegenerate linear-quadratic pair, specified degenerate ranks and all cyclic Danielewski powers, in unrestricted embedding degree. HC4MYHX0/1 preserve arbitrary finite monodromy descending from a regular polynomial parameter; HC4MYHX2 closes all constant-coefficient Danielewski P(z) and every T*Y+xy-B(T,z) suspension in every degree, beyond the earlier abelian class-action gate. HC4MYHY0/1 now close normal finite monogenic root covers and every monic two-parameter Danielewski output by root transitivity; HC4MYHY2 imposes a global nonmonogenicity gate on every nontrivial finite Keller normalization. HC4MYHZ0/1/2 supply the finite leading-fibre gate and independent abelian-root gate for nonmonic outputs, with exact localized-unit defect. HC4MYIA0/1/2 upgrade the unconditional nonmonic gate to finite nilpotent root/class groups and arbitrary common-prime radical depth. HC4MYIB0/1/2 add arbitrary Galois-intermediate exclusion, the exact global normalization-boundary basis, and subnormal class-stabilizer closure beyond nilpotent actions. HC4MYIC0/1/2 add combined leading-order factor divisibility, rational-label critical-curve geometry and new unrestricted-parameter S3 cubic closures. HC4MYID0/1 refine critical units to factor-specific supports and all subset rank budgets, closing a new square-discriminant S3 family with arbitrary leading multiplicity. HC4MYID2 closes reduced singleton critical units with nonconstant separation, including the cubic two-simple-leading-level case. HC4MYID3 closes the fixed cubic by a polynomial second chart omitting a hyperbola and consequently the entire specified two-simple-level square-critical class. HC4MYIE0/1/2 supply the intermediate-pole necessity, cyclic derivative surface, normal monic rescaling and unrestricted square-free-leading cubic closure. HC4MYIF0/1/2 constrain every source factorization, close square-free-leading quartics and supply a field-degree and nonnormal-order obstruction for the remaining unequal pair. HC4MYIG0/1/2 add reduced-pencil rational monodromy, one-exception polynomial parameters and all-degree scaled and reciprocal-scaled one-variable output closures. The same mechanism now closes rational scalings and rational affine input with polynomial output translation, including all sparse two-positive-term outputs without a gcd condition. HC4MYIH0/1/2 add the strict projective multiplicity bound, exact affine-in-V exception certificate and all-degree mixed-critical-value expansion outputs. HC4MYII0/1/2/3/4 add plane intermediate-branch geometry, unrestricted rational affine parameters, actual-inertia quotient certificates, all nonadjacent pure-power binomials and every cubic output. HC4MYIJ0/1/2/3 add relative central-series descent, actual product-cover preservation with arbitrary parameter monodromy, and the all-degree finite-critical-pole binomial certificate. HC4MYIK0/1/2/3 add parameter-cover unit norms, integral algebraic monic models, a direct critical-value valuation lemma and unrestricted plane polynomial-output closure. HC4MYIL0/1/2 add generative factor transfer, exact fixed-multiplier class lattices and all-degree multivariable suspension closure with full global filtration. HC4MYIM0/1/2/3 add parameter-extension irreducibility, moving-row invariant vanishing, an exact content-fibre criterion and uniform adapted global frames. The IM3 determinant-one parameter matrix covers moving B, multivariable monic-leading b and arbitrary affine root terms, with a separate primitive-content check. The IM3 frame admits every strict joint degree-gap remainder; its univariate leading-divisibility corollary allows all lower P coefficients. HC4MYIN0/1 replace the former global-frame requirement by rank-two reflexive pencil descent and close every primitive disjoint moving suspension. HC4MYIO0/1/2 extend to arbitrary independent coefficient fields and overlapping polynomial directions; monic and polynomial-Bezout leading overlap outputs have uniform generic filtrations. HC4MYIP0/1/2 use moved relative additive actions instead of positive generic filtrations, and force every surviving overlap image into the multiplier-variable invariant subring. HC4MYIQ0/1/2 descend any univariate generic helper, close every one-helper admitted overlap including nonprimitive content, and reduce HC4 survivors to two-helper invariant plane curves. HC4MYIR0/1/2 close multiplier-zero images in all helper counts and every admitted two-helper overlap in every stable dimension; the complete admitted HC4 overlap family is now closed. lessons_before.title: Charge inverse-Fourier rank for cyclic branch extraction before constructing a model

lessons_before.use: Compute the rank N of the actual generic connection and its inverse-Fourier rank r. A Kummer self-twist of order e costs r>=N+irr_0-N_reg/e. With one finite puncture the same inequality excludes every finite cover. A degree-d pushforward of a rank-m branch costs at least (d-1)m, and boundary delta factors add rank. Use actual generic rank, not the formal classical rank.
lessons_before.avoid: Testing higher rank without a numerical rank budget, using raw cyclic order before minimal extension, treating arbitrary additional branched covers as cyclic, or identifying an algebraic projector with a full finite-left carrier.
lessons_before.boundary: The all-cover statement requires at most one finite singularity. General multiple-puncture statements concern cyclic power covers. The exact-R Long application uses QSO2 and scalar fiber reduction; it does not fix deformed first images or produce scalar projective frames. The explicit polynomial S=g(a)+2v family splits algebraically at inverse rank m+1 but the quadratic Long branch cannot have the required finite mate. QVL1 transports repeated roots to nonlinear ordinary infinity limits and closes all proper-power v-linear repairs when lower coefficients are bounded. Together with QVM1, every leading H of degree>=2 is excluded in that entire Laurent class, with arbitrary finite partner order and algebraic coefficient covers. Euler limits and finite Newton support certificates give further tests. A remaining exact-R scalar Long model in the v-linear rational Laurent class has H degree<=1 and inverse-Fourier rank at least four, by QSO2 and a positive infinity Newton contribution. The family 2v*(1+h*a)^k+4a-3ra^2 is excluded for every k>=2, even though k3 passes N6/r3 and branch extraction. Nonlinear-limit commuting Darboux algebras cannot supply a scalar generator, but other operators in larger idealizers remain outside that assertion. Other leading faces, fractional positive lower growth for nonprimitive H, H degree<=1 and nonpositional first images remain open. QZM1 gives a zero-mode cokernel test with finite-cover trace retraction and covariance under actual finite algebra automorphisms, provided the module is transported too. A new position localization can kill the vector and is not justified by trace. It excludes v*(lambda*a+mu)+G(a) for every nonconstant polynomial G and every finite scalar mate order or algebraic coefficient cover. The finite leading-divisor gate is stronger than the first PDO period test: if gcd(operator order, all leading-coefficient zero/pole orders)=1, the entire base low-order commutator image is zero by finite power subtraction. A passing leading condition remains necessary, and nonscalar matrix carriers are not classified.

lessons_before.title: Split a binary phase by its height-factor flag and resolve every A2 unfolding order
lessons_before.when: A nonisotropic vertex leaves a linear Gaussian direction and a squarefree binary cubic after exact completion, with a degenerate escaping A2 block.
lessons_before.use: Complete the Gaussian variable exactly and preserve the full binary rank4. For nonconstant height H=u, distinguish whether u divides the leading cubic before choosing normal coordinates. At a nonzero-action A2 escape construct C(r)+X^2+Y^3+A(r)Y by formal Morse splitting and division modulo Y^2. In an r^-4 exponent, ord A=1,2 gives two shrinking Gaussian charts, while ord A>=3 or A=0 gives a fixed cubic rank2 chart. Retain the entire full-rank frame and positive scalar seed valuations. Fixed critical parabolas reduce to quartic/Gaussian blocks with t^-1 seed prefactor.
lessons_before.avoid: Assuming every degenerate escape splits into Morse points with a valid local Gaussian scale, stopping at one generic unfolding coefficient, ignoring the height-factor flag, dropping the Schur Gaussian means, inferring an empty isotropic pure-null locus from GMC safety, or comparing expanded and factored expressions structurally. The squarefree resultant has factor d^2, though its nonzero locus for d!=0 is unchanged.

lessons_before.title: Bound finite monodromy by a selected normalization tube and meridian centralizer before resolving finite contacts
lessons_before.when: A chosen target branch-image component has immersive normalization and cyclic zero-excess finite factors; its normal bundle on the simultaneous target infinity model has positive degree. Other branch images may have cusps or nonabelian local monodromy.
lessons_before.use: Construct the compact normalization neighborhood from Nori, retaining q:V->X locally holomorphic invertible. Its normal degree is eta=Cbar^2-2delta; WLT(C) bounds the complement subgroup index by Cbar^2/eta. Decompose the whole tube into its punctured oriented normal bundle and local pieces. In the actual finite cover each selected cyclic sheet cluster is separate from the others, so their local images centralize the selected meridian even if those other local groups are nonabelian. lessons_before.title: Transport repeated momentum roots to infinity limits before accepting proper-power repairs
lessons_before.when: A proper-power leading polynomial is proposed to evade the primitive infinity criterion, a higher-order scalar mate is sought, or a rational Darboux/bispectral construction is proposed as a full carrier.
lessons_before.use: Apply an algebraic position change and momentum shift and compute the full operator coefficient limits. A nonlinear ordinary infinity limit has no finite scalar Weyl mate of any order or algebraic coefficient cover; an Euler infinity limit excludes every nonconstant limit. Repeated roots close all proper powers for v*H(a)+bounded-lower S0. Together with QVM1 this rejects every deg H>=2 in the natural v-linear Laurent class. A finite Newton support certificate can handle positive intermediate powers, with complete falling-factorial ordering at the Euler boundary. In the exact-R full scalar Long category a remaining H degree<=1 forces a growing Newton branch and inverse rank at least four. Rational commuting Darboux operators with nonlinear limits are excluded as generators as well.
lessons_before.avoid: Treating a repeated root as an automatic escape, omitting internal ordering at the Euler face, applying an ordinary infinity theorem when the new coordinate tends to a finite point, treating a rational momentum inverse as a finite operator, or inferring full carrier existence from bispectrality or commuting differential actions.
lessons_before.boundary: The complete v-linear conclusion requires every lower coefficient exponent<=0; QVM1 alone covers primitive H with fractional lower exponents<1. The tested generic root shift can have h poles and is not a regular formal comparison. Other infinity faces, H of degree<=1 and nonpositional first images remain open. The rank>=4 refinement uses exact-R scalar reduction and the rational Laurent class. The Darboux conclusion excludes one whole commuting algebra, not every member of a larger idealizer or every projective/matrix carrier. A formal mate of E+hE^2 exists with unbounded momentum, and an exact proper-power pair on another face is a positive control. QZM1 gives a zero-mode cokernel test with finite-cover trace retraction and covariance under actual finite algebra automorphisms, provided the module is transported too. A new position localization can kill the vector and is not justified by trace. It excludes v*(lambda*a+mu)+G(a) for every nonconstant polynomial G and every finite scalar mate order or algebraic coefficient cover. Combined with QVL1, the pure separable class v*H(a)+G(a) with both H and G nonconstant is closed; the leading-linear rank-four cubic and derivative-tuned cubic are excluded. QPC1 subsequently closes the H-constant nonlinear-G case by a universal p-power coefficient. The complete pure polynomial v*H(a)+G(a) Long form is therefore excluded, including every finite momentum degree and coefficient cover. Additional negative-v corrections, genuine mixed coefficients, other leading faces and deformed first images remain outside this classification. Conditional global pair transport clears c(R) and requires [R,T]=0; it neither admits every chart formula nor identifies QRF2 with this new class. QPC1 also gives linear trace descent for a fixed operator mate and the necessary matrix-fiber condition chi_S derivative zero. Scalar p-centrality requires central degree p and fails for general phase matrices; no arbitrary carrier exclusion follows. QAD1 supplies an arbitrary-scalar mixed-coefficient admission test: nonzero Adler periods exclude even bounded-above PDO mates, whereas finite differential existence is exactly constant-linear membership in the full almost-commuting defect span. It identifies a characteristic-zero residue proportional to QPC1 gamma_n. Vanishing periods construct only a PDO mate, as the harmonic control demonstrates; neither an h-pole dressing nor a finite defect prefix supplies a finite full carrier. This does not compare arbitrary Fourier completions, identify QRF2 or cover nonscalar matrix actions. The finite leading-divisor gate is stronger than the first PDO period test: if gcd(operator order, all leading-coefficient zero/pole orders)=1, the entire base low-order commutator image is zero by finite power subtraction. This excludes every nonconstant squarefree polynomial leading coefficient, with arbitrary mixed lower terms and all finite coefficient covers. Prime operator orders over K(v) require a scalar times an nth power leading coefficient. The separate rational leading PDO equation Qprime-(Hprime/(n*H))*Q=v tests algebraic primitive exactness; its squarefree degree>=3 exclusion strengthens to PDO mates. A passing leading condition remains necessary, and nonscalar matrix carriers are not classified. QST1 separates rational and spectral admission. Any nonzero Adler period excludes the entire rational operator division ring and makes the universal spectral class nontorsion; the G(a)+mu*v first period is explicit in all degrees. This blocks every rational conjugate and the corresponding actual rank-one projective pair orbit without a scalar free frame. Fixed rational mate equations descend through finite algebraic coefficient covers by monic-denominator Galois averaging. Constant-coefficient G has instead a critical-value torsion annihilator and a rational mate. Zero Adler periods are insufficient for rational admission: a torus residue excludes harmonic/Euler functional classes even with arbitrary operator denominators and identity spectators. Finite primitive-divisor and ordinary infinity exclusions must not be silently promoted to rational ones. No arbitrary moving spectral coefficient localization, nonlinear Galois descent or universal Long rational normalization is proved.

lessons_before.title: Transport the zero mode cokernel and use trace before enlarging coefficient covers
lessons_before.when: A candidate operator has an algebraic hyperexponential zero mode after an Ore shift, a missing Weyl action is sought, or an actual obstruction is being transported through canonical changes.
lessons_before.use: Compute the vector-space cokernel class [be] in V/LV with Le=0. A commutator [L,T]=b makes it exact. Normalized differential field trace retracts every finite algebraic coefficient extension, so a nonzero rational class survives all such covers. Carry the actual module under finite algebra automorphisms and identity stabilization. For S=v*(lambda*a+mu)+G(a), a root shift gives a zero mode and an all-degree rational pole/degree obstruction whenever G is nonconstant. QPC1 subsequently closes the H-constant case too, completing the pure separable polynomial Long exclusion. Clear c(R) denominators and retain [R,T]=0 for a conditional global pair certificate.
lessons_before.avoid: Holding the coefficient-function module fixed after Fourier transformation, discarding the supported zero mode by a new localization, treating the class as determined only by the classical symbol, identifying it with QRF2 without a comparison theorem, or applying linear trace descent to nonlinear correction equations or bounded support conditions.
lessons_before.boundary: The pure polynomial G theorem does not include arbitrary negative-v corrections. QPC1 closes the H-constant higher-degree polynomial family; genuinely mixed coefficients and deformed nonpositional first images remain open. Abstract covariance requires an actual algebra automorphism and an actual module; a classical Poisson change alone is insufficient. The global pair application assumes admission and a valid rational chart, and a root shift with h poles is not regular formal normalization. Self-Ext vanishing is necessary, not a complete finite-mate or full-carrier criterion. Matrix candidates need their own nonzero represented class. QPC1 also gives linear trace descent for a fixed operator mate and the necessary matrix-fiber condition chi_S derivative zero. Scalar p-centrality requires central degree p and fails for general phase matrices; no arbitrary carrier exclusion follows. QAD1 supplies an arbitrary-scalar mixed-coefficient admission test: nonzero Adler periods exclude even bounded-above PDO mates, whereas finite differential existence is exactly constant-linear membership in the full almost-commuting defect span. It identifies a characteristic-zero residue proportional to QPC1 gamma_n. Vanishing periods construct only a PDO mate, as the harmonic control demonstrates; neither an h-pole dressing nor a finite defect prefix supplies a finite full carrier. This does not compare arbitrary Fourier completions, identify QRF2 or cover nonscalar matrix actions. The finite leading-divisor gate is stronger than the first PDO period test: if gcd(operator order, all leading-coefficient zero/pole orders)=1, the entire base low-order commutator image is zero by finite power subtraction. This excludes every nonconstant squarefree polynomial leading coefficient, with arbitrary mixed lower terms and all finite coefficient covers. Prime operator orders over K(v) require a scalar times an nth power leading coefficient. The separate rational leading PDO equation Qprime-(Hprime/(n*H))*Q=v tests algebraic primitive exactness; its squarefree degree>=3 exclusion strengthens to PDO mates. A passing leading condition remains necessary, and nonscalar matrix carriers are not classified. QSC1 proves Cent_classical(R,S)=K[R,S] and commutativity of the full formal joint centralizer for every commuting Long deformation, including nonpositional first images. Faithful finite/corner and QMC1 full-carrier endomorphism algebras inherit commutativity. Global spectral Koszul classes exactly test the two individual conjugates; if they vanish, one algebraic curvature class exactly tests flat completion. All spectral fibers can pass while the global class fails, and a formally exact curvature can have nonzero rational double residue. If both matrix positions are scalar, normalized matrix trace scalarizes a full completion without degree growth. This does not scalarize genuinely matrix-valued positions or free a projective carrier, identify QRF2, or construct a finite Long lift. QST1 separates rational and spectral admission. Any nonzero Adler period excludes the entire rational operator division ring and makes the universal spectral class nontorsion; the G(a)+mu*v first period is explicit in all degrees. This blocks every rational conjugate and the corresponding actual rank-one projective pair orbit without a scalar free frame. Fixed rational mate equations descend through finite algebraic coefficient covers by monic-denominator Galois averaging. Constant-coefficient G has instead a critical-value torsion annihilator and a rational mate. Zero Adler periods are insufficient for rational admission: a torus residue excludes harmonic/Euler functional classes even with arbitrary operator denominators and identity spectators. Finite primitive-divisor and ordinary infinity exclusions must not be silently promoted to rational ones. No arbitrary moving spectral coefficient localization, nonlinear Galois descent or universal Long rational normalization is proved.
lessons_before.reopen_when: A surviving candidate has a new nonzero cokernel class on an actual module, a complete scalar or matrix action passes the current tests with a finite global lattice, or a comparison theorem identifies an existing strong residue with this canonical class without changing category.

lessons_before.title: Reduce equal-negative weighted completion searches before coefficient algebra
lessons_before.when: A3D counterexample is sought with weights(1,-1,-1), a fixed cubic first component, or a parabolic invariant zero curve.
lessons_before.use: Write the full map as(x*f(Y,Z),A(Y,Z)/x,B(Y,Z)/x),Y=xy,Z=xz, and verify the entire source determinant dictionary. Use equal-degree binary leading proportionality before a Groebner calculation. Prime-degree coprimality restricts the top forms; constant polynomial Wronskians on a graph or vertical root line bound the restrictions. Keep target-linear normalization charts separate from source changes that would alter the chosen f. Use explicit Rabinowitsch units and independently multiply all rational certificates. In the strict cubic-quotient branch, classify the negative cubic component and use the opposite-weight exceptional chart.
lessons_before.avoid: Repeating the original24-variable40-second fixed-cubic model; treating a timeout asUNSAT; setting the second-chart slope parameter tozero; using sourceZ-shears after a fixed parabola normalization without accounting for the changed f; extending a strict-profile proof to all weight111 degree7 maps; silently treating an unreplayed primary unit certificate as a theorem; confusing a degree9 cubic-component control with an improved global or equal-negative witness.

lessons_before.title: Turn a finite all-order zero-set description into a certified terminating least-prefix search
lessons_before.when: An all-order moment-null locus has a finite algebraic description over an effective field, possibly with constructible coefficient constraints.
lessons_before.use: Build a fixed finite target ideal, then test every target generator in each prefix radical using inverse-variable unit-ideal certificates. A proven equality of target and all-order zero sets plus finite support of ideal expressions supplies termination. Once a sufficient prefix is found, monotonicity gives the least one. Insufficient tests give algebraic points and eventual later nonzero moments. For ternary cubics, replace existential null directions by the8-by16 binary-quartic multiplication matrix and its degree8 maximal minors, retaining projective endpoints.
lessons_before.avoid: Stopping after consecutive prefix ideals agree; replacing radical membership by ordinary membership; inferring a numerical bound from abstract termination; treating a frame as pure-null; attributing an old source abstract to a changed latest revision; or transferring reduced-locus information to nilpotent scheme thickness.

lessons_before.reopen_when: A finite target description is unavailable or fails review, coefficient constraints are not effectively presented algebraically, positive characteristic is requested, or a numerical/complexity/scheme-theoretic bound is required.

lessons_before.title: Use normal quotients and the exact boundary class basis before reopening nonnilpotent output monodromy
lessons_before.when: A finite Keller intermediate field is Galois, a finite normalization is claimed factorial, or a nonnilpotent output class action has manageable class stabilizers.
lessons_before.use: Every target divisor has a visible source place of ramification index one. In a Galois intermediate normalization this reaches every prime over that divisor, including missing places; explicit purity and finite-cover rigidity force degree one. In the full plane normalization, source factoriality gives boundary generation and source constant units give independence, so the missing divisors are an exact free global class basis. A subnormal class stabilizer in the output action lies in a proper normal subgroup unless it is the whole group, yielding a forbidden Galois intermediate field. This closes some nonnilpotent class representations. HC4MYIC0/1/2 add combined leading-order factor divisibility, rational-label critical-curve geometry and new unrestricted-parameter S3 cubic closures. HC4MYID0/1 refine critical units to factor-specific supports and all subset rank budgets, closing a new square-discriminant S3 family with arbitrary leading multiplicity. HC4MYID2 closes reduced singleton critical units with nonconstant separation, including the cubic two-simple-leading-level case. HC4MYID3 closes the fixed cubic by a polynomial second chart omitting a hyperbola and consequently the entire specified two-simple-level square-critical class. HC4MYIE0/1/2 supply the intermediate-pole necessity, cyclic derivative surface, normal monic rescaling and unrestricted square-free-leading cubic closure. HC4MYIF0/1/2 constrain every source factorization, close square-free-leading quartics and supply a field-degree and nonnormal-order obstruction for the remaining unequal pair. HC4MYIG0/1/2 add reduced-pencil rational monodromy, one-exception polynomial parameters and all-degree scaled and reciprocal-scaled one-variable output closures. The same mechanism now closes rational scalings and rational affine input with polynomial output translation, including all sparse two-positive-term outputs without a gcd condition. HC4MYIH0/1/2 add the strict projective multiplicity bound, exact affine-in-V exception certificate and all-degree mixed-critical-value expansion outputs. HC4MYII0/1/2/3/4 add plane intermediate-branch geometry, unrestricted rational affine parameters, actual-inertia quotient certificates, all nonadjacent pure-power binomials and every cubic output. HC4MYIJ0/1/2/3 add relative central-series descent, actual product-cover preservation with arbitrary parameter monodromy, and the all-degree finite-critical-pole binomial certificate. HC4MYIK0/1/2/3 add parameter-cover unit norms, integral algebraic monic models, a direct critical-value valuation lemma and unrestricted plane polynomial-output closure. HC4MYIL0/1/2 add generative factor transfer, exact fixed-multiplier class lattices and all-degree multivariable suspension closure with full global filtration. HC4MYIM0/1/2/3 add parameter-extension irreducibility, moving-row invariant vanishing, an exact content-fibre criterion and uniform adapted global frames. The IM3 determinant-one parameter matrix covers moving B, multivariable monic-leading b and arbitrary affine root terms, with a separate primitive-content check. The IM3 frame admits every strict joint degree-gap remainder; its univariate leading-divisibility corollary allows all lower P coefficients. HC4MYIN0/1 replace the former global-frame requirement by rank-two reflexive pencil descent and close every primitive disjoint moving suspension. HC4MYIO0/1/2 extend to arbitrary independent coefficient fields and overlapping polynomial directions; monic and polynomial-Bezout leading overlap outputs have uniform generic filtrations. HC4MYIP0/1/2 use moved relative additive actions instead of positive generic filtrations, and force every surviving overlap image into the multiplier-variable invariant subring. HC4MYIQ0/1/2 descend any univariate generic helper, close every one-helper admitted overlap including nonprimitive content, and reduce HC4 survivors to two-helper invariant plane curves. HC4MYIR0/1/2 close multiplier-zero images in all helper counts and every admitted two-helper overlap in every stable dimension; the complete admitted HC4 overlap family is now closed. IT0/1/2 give intrinsic finite-energy and inverse-Hessian certificates and a mixed three-direction criterion before any ambient output construction. IU0/1/2 exploit actual free projections and the zero-section first jet, closing critical-value traces and testing the global immersion obligation in a universal noncritical construction. IV0/1/2 separate complete compensation identities from codimension-one source recovery and provide a canonical Legendre-hypersurface normality gate. IW0/1/2 close every constant trace through an infinite-order integral middle-cycle obstruction, with arbitrary helper degrees. IX0/1/2 separate arbitrary quadric plane classes from actual radical-curve recovery and close coordinate-composite or smooth/nonparametric descended nonconstant traces. lessons_before.avoid: Propagating one unramified place without Galois normality; inferring arbitrary full target-group preservation from the absence of Galois intermediate fields; confusing local factoriality with global class group zero; identifying normalization and ambient generic class groups; treating a nonabelian stabilizer as normal without evidence; claiming a Hurwitz-module ambient realization.
lessons_before.boundary: HC4MYIB0 now excludes every finite Galois intermediate target-field extension inside a complex Keller field, in every dimension and without a group restriction: a visible index-one place reaches all primes by Galois conjugacy, then explicit purity and finite-cover inputs force triviality. This does not assert arbitrary full splitting-group preservation. HC4MYIB1 identifies the finite plane normalization class group exactly as the free group on the omitted boundary divisors; a torsion or globally factorial normalization forces the inverse. Local factoriality alone is insufficient. HC4MYIB2 closes the filtered output criterion when divisor-class stabilizers are subnormal in an arbitrary finite class-action image; normal class stabilizers suffice even for nonnilpotent groups. The Hurwitz lattice gives an explicit nonnilpotent class-module certificate, without an asserted ambient realization. The S3 root-lattice order-two stabilizer is not subnormal and remains a genuine boundary. Within nonmonic xy-P(T,z), positive localized-unit defect and nonnilpotent monodromy remain necessary unless another retained gate closes the case. Both plane endpoints and unrestricted HC4/JC2 remain open. HC4MYIC0 now constrains every source root-factor degree by m/gcd(m,q_1,...,q_k) when leading-drop coefficient orders lie above the single-slope chords; coprime combined orders give irreducibility and close the carried output in arbitrary z degree without a special-fibre or monodromy hypothesis. HC4MYIC1 clears a rational root to a polynomial label with an exact vertical-Jacobian identity. The constructed polynomial map omits its normalized critical curve, so the explicit qualitative Jelonek-Lason nonproperness input forces each critical component to have affine normalization A1. Independently a square-free leading coefficient dividing the next coefficient excludes rational roots. HC4MYIC2 consequently closes nonmonic cubics if a is square-free and divides b, or if the critical discriminant D=b^2-3ac has square-free part of degree at least two. This includes new S3 families with unbounded T degree and no special-fibre hypothesis. The remaining cubic branch requires a rational label, positive localized-unit defect, S3 group, D of square-free degree at most one, and failure of the independent no-pole gate; D=0 was already cyclic and closed. Critical and root discriminants are distinct, and no-rational-root is not irreducibility in arbitrary higher degree. Both plane endpoints and unrestricted HC4/JC2 remain open. HC4MYIC1 also gives a quantitative critical-branch unit budget: if the normalized derivative Q_U has ell distinct rational roots over C(T), monicity puts them in C[T], and the corresponding polynomial labels u-beta_i(f) are localized source units with linearly independent classes modulo C(f)^*. Hence the exact localized-unit defect sum_(a(c)=0)(r_c-1) is at least ell. For a cubic with D=b^2-3ac a nonzero square, the two distinct rational critical roots force defect at least two. This counts rational critical roots, not every root after a parameter-field extension, and does not close the residual by itself. HC4MYID0 now gives precise allowed supports for all irreducible normalized critical factors over C(T), not only rational branches: H_i(f,u) can vanish only above leading levels with H_i(c,0)=0. Independence gives every subset rank inequality, so extra defect at an excluded level cannot help. An empty support, equivalently gcd(a,H_i(T,0))=1, excludes a rational root in every degree without a special-fibre hypothesis. No new external theorem is imported. The two-level coefficient control T*(T-1)*z^3+z^2-4*z/3 passes this necessary support test and is not closed by it. No higher-degree irreducibility is inferred from no rational roots. Both plane endpoints and unrestricted HC4/JC2 remain open. HC4MYID2 adds a global singleton-support pencil obstruction: two reduced rational critical units, each supported at one leading level, force their polynomial critical branches to differ by a nonzero constant. Mutual divisibility modulo the reduced units and ordinary polynomial degrees prove this in arbitrary degrees. In the cubic case a square-free leading coefficient with at most two zeros and gcd(a,b)=1 makes the two populated critical units reduced by the valuation-two Jacobian identity. Thus a nonconstant square critical gap H closes the output even when the support gcd test passes. The old coefficient control T*(T-1)*z^3+z^2-4*z/3 is now closed. A new residual has a=T*(T-1), b=1-2T, c=4/3, H^2=1 and constant critical gap; it is not closed by this argument. Repeated leading multiplicities require a separate reducedness audit. Both plane endpoints and unrestricted HC4/JC2 remain open. The proof writes the affine parameter change, polynomial z shift, constant rescaling, target shear and their inverses, transporting closed embedding data and Keller invertibility in both directions. lessons_before.title: Trace a fixed mate to the base field and test its p-power before constructing it
lessons_before.when: A fixed finite scalar operator is being tested for a Weyl mate, including partners on finite algebraic coefficient covers, or a relative finite matrix fiber is available.
lessons_before.use: For a fixed base operator S, normalized coefficient field trace retracts the linear commutator equation, eliminating finite algebraic covers. In a characteristic-p central algebra of degree p, a mate forces S^p central. Isolate a noncentral normal-order coefficient using word weights before computing the full power. For G(a)+mu*v on [a,v]=h/v, the two-v coefficient is universally (n^2-1)/(24n)*g_n^(p-2)*mu^2*h^(p+1) at v^-2p*a^((n-1)p-2n-1), for p>2n+1. Good reduction excludes every finite mate in characteristic zero. Combined with QVL1 and QZM1 this closes the entire pure polynomial v*H(a)+G(a) Long ansatz. For a general finite matrix fiber, use chi_S derivative zero as the necessary condition.
lessons_before.avoid: Bounding the unknown partner order, treating h-small leading coefficients as zero in the generic field, prescribing a Frobenius center map without proof, using normalized trace for idempotents or a nonlinear unknown tuple, or requiring scalar S^p in an arbitrary higher-dimensional matrix fiber.
lessons_before.boundary: The central-degree-p argument is relative rank one. Arbitrary m*p matrices require only chi_S(z)=f(z^p); QPH1 at p7 has nonscalar S^7 despite an exact Weyl mate. The complete classification concerns pure polynomial H,G and permits arbitrary partner poles and finite covers; it does not include arbitrary additional negative-v or genuinely mixed coefficients. The classification does not place every finite Long carrier in that form. New localization, nonpositional first images, global admission, a full right action and finite-left generation remain separate. QAD1 supplies an arbitrary-scalar mixed-coefficient admission test: nonzero Adler periods exclude even bounded-above PDO mates, whereas finite differential existence is exactly constant-linear membership in the full almost-commuting defect span. It identifies a characteristic-zero residue proportional to QPC1 gamma_n. Vanishing periods construct only a PDO mate, as the harmonic control demonstrates; neither an h-pole dressing nor a finite defect prefix supplies a finite full carrier. This does not compare arbitrary Fourier completions, identify QRF2 or cover nonscalar matrix actions. The finite leading-divisor gate is stronger than the first PDO period test: if gcd(operator order, all leading-coefficient zero/pole orders)=1, the entire base low-order commutator image is zero by finite power subtraction. This excludes every nonconstant squarefree polynomial leading coefficient, with arbitrary mixed lower terms and all finite coefficient covers. Prime operator orders over K(v) require a scalar times an nth power leading coefficient. The separate rational leading PDO equation Qprime-(Hprime/(n*H))*Q=v tests algebraic primitive exactness; its squarefree degree>=3 exclusion strengthens to PDO mates. A passing leading condition remains necessary, and nonscalar matrix carriers are not classified. QST1 separates rational and spectral admission. Any nonzero Adler period excludes the entire rational operator division ring and makes the universal spectral class nontorsion; the G(a)+mu*v first period is explicit in all degrees. This blocks every rational conjugate and the corresponding actual rank-one projective pair orbit without a scalar free frame. Fixed rational mate equations descend through finite algebraic coefficient covers by monic-denominator Galois averaging. Constant-coefficient G has instead a critical-value torsion annihilator and a rational mate. Zero Adler periods are insufficient for rational admission: a torus residue excludes harmonic/Euler functional classes even with arbitrary operator denominators and identity spectators. Finite primitive-divisor and ordinary infinity exclusions must not be silently promoted to rational ones. No arbitrary moving spectral coefficient localization, nonlinear Galois descent or universal Long rational normalization is proved.
lessons_before.reopen_when: An actual surviving operator has genuinely different mixed coefficients or a different leading face, a new coefficient can be proved nonzero for an entire carrier class, or a complete full matrix/projective model passes the characteristic-polynomial and global finite-lattice tests.

lessons_before.title: Use combined leading orders and omitted critical-curve geometry before reopening nonmonic factors

lessons_before.use: Single-slope leading drops constrain each factor degree by root valuations; combining all chosen levels can force transitivity without a monodromy hypothesis. A rational root clears to an integral polynomial label, whose exact Jacobian identity forces an auxiliary polynomial map to omit its normalized critical curve. The explicit qualitative nonproperness theorem makes that curve polynomially parametrizable. Cubic critical curves reduce to Y^2=b^2-3ac, giving a square-free-degree test; an independent square-free-leading no-pole criterion closes complementary cases. HC4MYID2 closes reduced singleton critical units with nonconstant separation, including the cubic two-simple-leading-level case. HC4MYID3 closes the fixed cubic by a polynomial second chart omitting a hyperbola and consequently the entire specified two-simple-level square-critical class. Therefore the fixed cubic stays irreducible under every plane Keller base change. The constant-gap fixed model is retired; the output normal form still does not imply fixed-potential Hessian invariance. HC4MYIE0 now proves in every z degree m>=3 that any rational source root must have an actual intermediate pole 0<r<ord_c(a) at a multiple leading zero. Absence of such poles forces R=D^(m-2), polynomial quotients and a generically finite polynomial map from the original A2 to an integral cyclic derivative surface; the root equation makes it omit a Cstar boundary curve except finitely many points, forbidden by the retained Jelonek-Lason theorem. lessons_before.title: Localize each critical-factor unit at its permitted leading levels and enforce every subset rank budget
lessons_before.when: A rational source label survives the geometric critical-curve and global unit-rank tests, especially a cubic with square critical discriminant.
lessons_before.use: Normalize the label, factor Q_U over C(T) into distinct monic H_i, and compute the supports S_i={a=0,H_i(T,0)=0}. The root equation and derivative have only zero as a possible common root at a leading level. Therefore each critical-factor unit has precisely this allowed support. Their independence modulo C(f)^* gives every subset rank inequality. Empty support excludes a rational root. For cubics the factors are linear when D=H^2, giving the coefficient gcd test and new arbitrary-leading-multiplicity S3 closures. HC4MYID2 closes reduced singleton critical units with nonconstant separation, including the cubic two-simple-leading-level case. HC4MYID3 closes the fixed cubic by a polynomial second chart omitting a hyperbola and consequently the entire specified two-simple-level square-critical class. HC4MYIE0/1/2 supply the intermediate-pole necessity, cyclic derivative surface, normal monic rescaling and unrestricted square-free-leading cubic closure. HC4MYIF0/1/2 constrain every source factorization, close square-free-leading quartics and supply a field-degree and nonnormal-order obstruction for the remaining unequal pair. HC4MYIG0/1/2 add reduced-pencil rational monodromy, one-exception polynomial parameters and all-degree scaled and reciprocal-scaled one-variable output closures. The same mechanism now closes rational scalings and rational affine input with polynomial output translation, including all sparse two-positive-term outputs without a gcd condition. HC4MYIH0/1/2 add the strict projective multiplicity bound, exact affine-in-V exception certificate and all-degree mixed-critical-value expansion outputs. HC4MYII0/1/2/3/4 add plane intermediate-branch geometry, unrestricted rational affine parameters, actual-inertia quotient certificates, all nonadjacent pure-power binomials and every cubic output. HC4MYIJ0/1/2/3 add relative central-series descent, actual product-cover preservation with arbitrary parameter monodromy, and the all-degree finite-critical-pole binomial certificate. HC4MYIK0/1/2/3 add parameter-cover unit norms, integral algebraic monic models, a direct critical-value valuation lemma and unrestricted plane polynomial-output closure. HC4MYIL0/1/2 add generative factor transfer, exact fixed-multiplier class lattices and all-degree multivariable suspension closure with full global filtration. HC4MYIM0/1/2/3 add parameter-extension irreducibility, moving-row invariant vanishing, an exact content-fibre criterion and uniform adapted global frames. The IM3 determinant-one parameter matrix covers moving B, multivariable monic-leading b and arbitrary affine root terms, with a separate primitive-content check. The IM3 frame admits every strict joint degree-gap remainder; its univariate leading-divisibility corollary allows all lower P coefficients. HC4MYIN0/1 replace the former global-frame requirement by rank-two reflexive pencil descent and close every primitive disjoint moving suspension. HC4MYIO0/1/2 extend to arbitrary independent coefficient fields and overlapping polynomial directions; monic and polynomial-Bezout leading overlap outputs have uniform generic filtrations. HC4MYIP0/1/2 use moved relative additive actions instead of positive generic filtrations, and force every surviving overlap image into the multiplier-variable invariant subring. HC4MYIQ0/1/2 descend any univariate generic helper, close every one-helper admitted overlap including nonprimitive content, and reduce HC4 survivors to two-helper invariant plane curves. HC4MYIR0/1/2 close multiplier-zero images in all helper counts and every admitted two-helper overlap in every stable dimension; the complete admitted HC4 overlap family is now closed. IS0/1/2 identify the full JC2 content of an unconditional residual-free extension, including an exact source-correlated class lattice and actual unit-Hessian embeddings with an always invertible constructed gradient. IT0/1/2 give intrinsic finite-energy and inverse-Hessian certificates and a mixed three-direction criterion before any ambient output construction. IU0/1/2 exploit actual free projections and the zero-section first jet, closing critical-value traces and testing the global immersion obligation in a universal noncritical construction. IV0/1/2 separate complete compensation identities from codimension-one source recovery and provide a canonical Legendre-hypersurface normality gate. IW0/1/2 close every constant trace through an infinite-order integral middle-cycle obstruction, with arbitrary helper degrees. IX0/1/2 separate arbitrary quadric plane classes from actual radical-curve recovery and close coordinate-composite or smooth/nonparametric descended nonconstant traces. IY0/1/2 close contractible full-preimage curves and descended cusps, and impose the exact generic-pencil boundary-defect certificate on the remaining multibranch cases. IZ0/1/2 match the intrinsic generic genus on all one-place zero curves and close every rank-one descended trace, including all internally multibranch cases and positive-power rational descent. JA0/1/2 force the actual disjoint extra-prime/unit/boundary configuration and bound its one-place part; scalar extra units close the selected one-place case.
lessons_before.avoid: Using defect at a level outside a subset support; asserting every permitted level is actually used; counting an irreducible critical factor as separate branches over a parameter extension; using no rational roots as higher-degree irreducibility; invoking an S-unit height bound or Hall theorem without need; declaring the two-supported coefficient residual a Keller realization.
lessons_before.boundary: HC4MYID0 now gives precise allowed supports for all irreducible normalized critical factors over C(T), not only rational branches: H_i(f,u) can vanish only above leading levels with H_i(c,0)=0. Independence gives every subset rank inequality, so extra defect at an excluded level cannot help. An empty support, equivalently gcd(a,H_i(T,0))=1, excludes a rational root in every degree without a special-fibre hypothesis. HC4MYID1 closes cubic square-critical-discriminant outputs whenever gcd(a,b-H)=1 or gcd(a,b+H)=1, including arbitrary pure-power leading multiplicities with b nonzero at the sole leading zero and the explicit S3 family T^q*z^3+z^2-(2R+T^q*R^2)*z/3+d. No new external theorem is imported. A surviving square-discriminant cubic needs nonempty support for both branches and the subset defect budgets; when gcd(a,b)=1, two separate reducible full f-fibres are required. The two-level coefficient control T*(T-1)*z^3+z^2-4*z/3 passes this necessary support test and is not closed by it. No higher-degree irreducibility is inferred from no rational roots. Both plane endpoints and unrestricted HC4/JC2 remain open. HC4MYID2 adds a global singleton-support pencil obstruction: two reduced rational critical units, each supported at one leading level, force their polynomial critical branches to differ by a nonzero constant. Mutual divisibility modulo the reduced units and ordinary polynomial degrees prove this in arbitrary degrees. In the cubic case a square-free leading coefficient with at most two zeros and gcd(a,b)=1 makes the two populated critical units reduced by the valuation-two Jacobian identity. Thus a nonconstant square critical gap H closes the output even when the support gcd test passes. The old coefficient control T*(T-1)*z^3+z^2-4*z/3 is now closed. A new residual has a=T*(T-1), b=1-2T, c=4/3, H^2=1 and constant critical gap; it is not closed by this argument. Repeated leading multiplicities require a separate reducedness audit. Both plane endpoints and unrestricted HC4/JC2 remain open. HC4MYID2 further reduces the remaining two-simple-leading-level constant-critical-gap subclass, in all coefficient degrees, to the one fixed output model (T,xy-[T*(T-1)*z^3+(1-2T)*z^2+4*z/3]). The proof writes the affine parameter change, polynomial z shift, constant rescaling, target shear and their inverses, transporting closed embedding data and Keller invertibility in both directions. This is an output-data normal form; the fixed-model endpoint is closed by HC4MYID3, and any fixed quadratic potential must be transported literally rather than assuming Hessian invariance. Increasing coefficient degrees in this output subclass adds no new output-base geometry. HC4MYID3 closes the fixed constant-gap cubic output model. A rational root label gives reduced critical units and polynomial quotients p,q; their difference and the label give a dominant polynomial second chart (A,t). The cleared root equation forces that chart to omit the hyperbola A*(t+1)=3 except possibly one point. The explicit retained Jelonek-Lason nonproperness theorem forbids this, since a hyperbola has no nonconstant polynomial A1 parametrization. Therefore the fixed cubic stays irreducible under every plane Keller base change. Together with HC4MYID2 this closes all cubic outputs with square-free leading a having at most two zeros, gcd(a,b)=1 and nonzero square critical discriminant, in every coefficient and embedding degree. The constant-gap fixed model is retired; the output normal form still does not imply fixed-potential Hessian invariance. Nonsquare linear critical part, more leading levels, repeated-level reducedness and higher-degree factorization branches remain open, as do both plane endpoints and unrestricted HC4/JC2. HC4MYIE0 now proves in every z degree m>=3 that any rational source root must have an actual intermediate pole 0<r<ord_c(a) at a multiple leading zero. Absence of such poles forces R=D^(m-2), polynomial quotients and a generically finite polynomial map from the original A2 to an integral cyclic derivative surface; the root equation makes it omit a Cstar boundary curve except finitely many points, forbidden by the retained Jelonek-Lason theorem. The integer coefficient pole spectrum excludes roots whenever only full poles are permitted; gcd(a,a_prime,b_(m-1))=1 suffices. HC4MYIE1 separately proves full arbitrary-degree irreducibility for balanced monic rescaling P=A^(m-1)z^m+sum A^(i-1)c_i z^i+d when its explicit finite monic surface is normal; every square-free A is allowed, and the triple gcd F,F_U,F_T at each repeated A zero gives the more general normality test. It explicitly imports Stacks 00SB,031S,07PF. HC4MYIE2 closes every cubic with square-free leading a of arbitrary degree, every cubic with gcd(a,b)=1, and every cubic with leading parameter degree at most two, without a critical-discriminant restriction or special-fibre assumption. This supersedes earlier residual wording concerning square-free-leading nonsquare-linear critical parts and additional square-free leading levels. Remaining cubic rational roots require actual intermediate poles at joint zeros of a,a_prime,b and failure of this normal monic rescaling and the other retained gates. No-rational-root is not full irreducibility in higher degree. Both plane endpoints and unrestricted HC4/JC2 remain open. HC4MYIF0 extends the obstruction to all factor patterns: for any Keller map in n>=2 dimensions, primitive source factors with pairwise coprime leading coefficients have constant cross-resultants. The target gcd(a,a_prime,b_(m-1))=1 guarantees that coprimality. At V=infinity all normalized-root differences have valuation -1/m, so every pair gives ell_i/d_i+ell_j/d_j=1/m with sum ell_i=0. This excludes three or more factors and two equal factors in arbitrary degree and dimension. HC4MYIF1 combines the plane rational-root gate to leave exactly two unequal factors 2<=d<e under that gcd. In particular all square-free-leading quartics of arbitrary parameter degree and all quartics with gcd(a,b_3)=1 close, without a critical-discriminant, root-group or special-fibre hypothesis. The full quartic conclusion uses the plane-only root gate. HC4MYIF2 proves for the surviving unequal pair R=lambda*a^(e(d-1))*D^(e-d), the exact degree divisor m(e-d)/gcd(de,m(e-d)) for [L:F], and an explicit integral zeta=a^ceil(e(d-1)/(e-d))*D generating a necessarily nonnormal finite monogenic order. Unequal-factor valuations remain consistent; generic primitive orders cannot be treated as normal. The remaining gcd-admitted high-degree cases have precisely two unequal factors of degrees at least two, subject to that field-degree and order obstruction; joint repeated-leading cases remain separate. Both plane endpoints and unrestricted HC4/JC2 remain open. HC4MYIG0 supplies an all-degree rational-parameter regularity test: every finite reduced pencil member must be nonconstant and square-free. At most one projective parameter point can have constant point form; Riemann-Hurwitz forces any nontrivial composition to give a forbidden constant finite member. A polynomial parameter also passes when all but one finite fibre are reduced and the exceptional multiplicity gcd is one. The proof explicitly imports Petravchuk-Iena Lemma 2(1) closedness/noncomposition equivalence and reuses projective Riemann-Hurwitz. HC4MYIG1 shows Keller pullback preserves these tests and the full group of every finite Galois cover of the resulting one-variable rational parameter field. It extends the filtered class-action criterion without deleting any affine pole fibres. Parameters include (V+B(U))/A(U) and Q(U)(V+B(U)) with arbitrary polynomial A,Q and arbitrary repeated zeros; critical points and critical lines are allowed. HC4MYIG2 closes every P=A(T)R(c(T)z+beta(T))+B(T) for arbitrary nonconstant constant-coefficient R and nonzero polynomial A,c, with beta,B polynomial, and every polynomial P=R(c(T)z+beta(T))/Q(T)+B(T) with nonzero polynomial Q,c. All parameter, source, z and embedding degrees and leading multiplicities are unrestricted, with no root-group restriction. This closes the S3 family T^(3k)(z^3+z)+B(T) despite its intermediate pole, and the full sparse family T^k z^m+z^(m-1)+B(T) despite previously allowed unequal higher factors. General coefficient variation, rational affine representations not meeting the stated polynomial or parameter tests, two unequal factors outside these new closures, other joint repeated-leading cases and other outputs remain open. lessons_before.avoid: Confusing irreducible integers with principal prime ideals; replacing a full cyclotomic base by a smaller field lacking its automorphism; using fieldwise point existence as a natural point choice or scheme universality; or interpreting the universal primitive-idempotent scheme as a chosen idempotent. Do not search larger polynomial degrees in these closed rank-one cubic-return or retained-output coupling classes, or confuse a cyclic dependence graph with the removal of an intermediate field. Do not replace a non-descended Schur matrix by an ordinary time Jacobian without proving descent, or confuse generic covering degree with total coordinate degree. Do not deepen root-only polynomial profile degrees while retaining every first signal, equate ordinary nilpotence with vanishing of all principal minors, or read apparent coefficient-list cycles before effective cancellation. Do not freeze the scalar response at coefficient zero, infer polynomial integration from every finite Keller jet or a full formal series, or treat a rational source-open formula as an entire affine map. Do not add more native indices as independent control channels, infer map-degree bounds from the normal-form indices, treat finite/formal source-coordinate existence as a polynomial family, or confuse sigma composed F with a retained first output. Do not deepen searches for polynomial plane decompositions of the completed native map, apply the Keller line theorem directly to its nonconstant Jacobian, or infer stable full-map atomicity from plane indecomposability. Do not reopen the former intermediate boundary-pole route: it is now closed in the entire signal-retaining class. Do not identify a generic intermediate fibre with A2 without proof, assume abstractly isomorphic source surfaces imply trivial factor degrees, or treat a generic etale formula as a whole polynomial factor. Do not reopen the nonconstant-unit intermediate branch or allow a proper finite-index unit lattice in a whole Keller factor. Do not substitute a generic J_d surface cover for whole power descent, remove the retained node, infer geometric factoriality from arithmetic localization, or claim that a unit-free surface has been excluded. Do not reopen nonnegative-log surfaces, geometrically factorial proper native factors or invariant geometric divisor classes. Do not import the finite torus-domination classification into our nonfinite maps, use the obsolete two-surface log-zero list, or turn an exact primitive into an etale plane pair. Higher-power primitive formulas and lattice models do not construct either arrow. Do not identify the raw singular retained-base spread with an actual whole Keller intermediate. Do not turn standard formal curve neighborhoods into a global plane chart, glue plane automorphisms into a non-plane etale target, or call the classical chart-to-JC(2) reduction new. Do not substitute local contacts for the whole closed embedded curve, or search increasing degrees inside the excluded beta-integral family or low/divisibly reducible ruling sector. Do not replace geometric ruling existence after finite extension by descent to K0, transfer arithmetic UFD across that extension, or accept multiple geometric components with multiplicity>1 in a descended ruling. Do not fill a nonfinite surface completion with finitely many points, infer positive Euler integral from nonnegative sheet loss, or apply product-leaf topology to a changed-signal receiver without proving its actual generic fibre.
