lessons_before.boundary: Field-versal specified-group isogenies, fixed all-scheme universality, canonical stack-valued map descent and atomicity have distinct conditions. The canonical trace receiver retains inertia and varies its bundle, so it respects the fixed-scheme no-go. Its two nontrivial factors are canonical; an atomic replacement is still required. These classifications use characteristic-zero polynomial retained-signal profiles and the named compiler. Any number of controls with rank-one cubic return is closed; non-descended higher-rank return and other compilers are separate. For another auxiliary block rank-one output recovery is equivalent to geometric generic-line connectedness; no general closedness conjecture is silently assumed. Arithmetic atomicity of connected input algebras is not absolute atomicity. Common kernels are proved for all constant ranks; the full selector classification is only one-directional. Higher-rank membership in C[Z,t] is an explicit hypothesis, not a determinant consequence. The full C is not assumed finitely generated or polynomial. Marked divisor identities hold universally; effective degree and absolute atomicity use the stated characteristic-zero field hypotheses. Fixed-signal rank-two source leaves need not be affine planes. A slice does not imply local nilpotence, and stable polynomiality is not an atomicity converse. The root-feedback theorem requires characteristic-zero fields, unchanged first signals and corrections in k[u,sigma,X]. Independent r_i diagonal variables force every principal minor to vanish. Frobenius dependencies and nilpotent coefficient cycles show why positive characteristic and nonreduced bases are excluded. Transitive product-fibre conclusions require transitivity on ALL nonidentity blocks; the trace filter has an extra auxiliary orbit and changes its first signal. Scalar self-feedback rigidity is a one-block affine coefficient-line theorem with a nonzero effective direction in characteristic zero. It permits all own-source channels and rational controls with whole polynomial landing, but says only that EFFECTIVE profiles are retained-signal polynomials; common direction factors may cancel a rational signal control. Curved coefficient families and mutually changing blocks remain outside. Finite-order parameter bases are nonreduced; the formal ring k[P][[lambda]] permits unbounded source degrees and differs from k[[lambda]][P]. The two-control module identity is universal over bases with2 invertible and preserves arbitrary source dependence. Affine-r rigidity and the stable signal-field normalizer use characteristic-zero fields. Affine-r rigidity is a one-block theorem with actual identity parameters and native source jets, not a theorem about mutually changing blocks. Formal-etale source gauges are classical and work over arbitrary nilpotent base ideals; their compatible formal limit can have unbounded source degree. The source-field normalizer leaves a vertical JC(m) problem and does not classify merely retained-output maps or arbitrary coordinate changes moving that field. Formal marked source equivalence permits actual polynomial families with arbitrary generic-degree jumps; it is not a global degree or stable-class invariant. Native orbit rigidity requires characteristic zero, one retained block, polynomial module membership and coordinate operations fixing identity parameters. Its stable equivalence is restricted to source maps normalizing k(u,sigma); unrestricted source changes are outside. A polynomial-r reduction survivor has non-dividing degrees >=2; negative Laurent sectors and genuine cross-block interaction remain open. The fixed dimension-three descent certificate excludes only the old cubic factor when its remainder is nonzero. Quasi-finite saturation is a classical elementary divisor consequence, not a novelty claim. The profile-factor theorem is one block with retained identities and a literal profile first factor; arbitrary source changes remain outside. Plane completion is generic in the signal and covers only nonnegative r powers. Plane indecomposability requires an irreducible Jacobian and an embedded line; its extension to all fields requires GEOMETRIC irreducibility. It does not imply stable whole-map atomicity. A nontrivial signal-retaining factor must have a genuine intermediate boundary pole. Whole-source special-signal landing and signal-moving factors remain open. The saturation overlap has explicit prior public attribution to Trushin Proposition3.1.1. The relative cancellation theorem leaves exactly TWO generic coordinates and requires a whole embedded A1 image; three-dimensional Keller counterexamples show that one curve alone does not invert a higher-dimensional target. It uses only the curve restriction, allowing poles elsewhere. Arbitrary identity stabilization and intermediate mixing are covered by the NON-PLANE generic intermediate-fibre obstruction. This is still a necessary all-factor condition, not full absolute stable atomicity. Intermediate surfaces satisfy BOTH saturation identities, geometrically have unit rank at most1 and their etale arrows miss at most finitely many points. Their abstract shape, smoothness and tangent triviality do not construct a proper factor. Primitive-unit surface rigidity requires characteristic zero, an AFFINE smooth target, cofinite etale image and the actual node. Its whole-factor unit theorem covers arbitrary last outputs with the fixed retained signal, without native jets or Laurent-degree bounds. Proper intermediates have CONSTANT geometric units; the earlier unit-rank-at-most-one route is now CLOSED on the nonconstant side. Whole constant-level irreducibility is not a statement about all further fibres after fixing E_u. Arithmetic UFD over k(u,a) does not prove geometric factoriality. The native NON-PLANE conclusion still requires the UARELPLANE1 embedded-curve witness. The one-way unit drop bounds no later unit-free chain length. CURRENT: a PROPER native intermediate is GEOMETRICALLY UNIT-FREE, has log kappa=-infinity, and has NONZERO geometric Picard group with ZERO retained-field Galois invariants, despite arithmetic UFD. The Picard factor criterion uses the native curve witness and explicitly imported Miyanishi negative-log affine-plane criterion. The log dichotomy and invariant-class vanishing cover every actual whole retained-signal Keller map. Higher-power Danielewski surfaces m>=2 pass exact volume; u has no Keller mate for all m>=1. Required arrows, free tangent frame, global polynomial lift and canonical marks/gluing remain unconstructed. The raw spread a=z^d-u^m*v is excluded globally by its critical zero fibre; only another smooth whole model could realize the same generic surface. CURRENT CHART GATE: the WHOLE carried A1 crosses the boundary of EVERY plane chart in a proper native factor, despite all finite/formal neighborhoods being standard. Any non-plane etale target containing an open A2 yields JC(2) counterexamples on all charts; this remains CONDITIONAL and has Dubouloz2009 precedent. Higher-power Danielewski targets need compatible nonautomorphic pairs surviving at nondividing ruling degrees>=2 and a carried closed embedding meeting two root components with deg Z>=m*N-r+1. Sharp beta-integral contact maps fail geometric injectivity for EVERY m>=2; other multi-root embedded curves remain open. These deductions retain the actual native/witness two-dimensional fibre and entire-curve hypotheses. CURRENT RULING/TOPOLOGY GATE: a retained-field ruling has base A1, integral arithmetic fibres and reduced geometric fibres, hence a finite geometric A2 atlas and a JC(2) burden for proper native targets. Geometric ruling existence does NOT prove descent. The whole carried curve hits two components of some split fibre. On an ACTUAL U^N times A^h leaf both proper arrows are NONFINITE and intermediate pi1 has an abelian subgroup with index DIVIDING source degree. This is virtually cyclic for one block. Multiple fibres of any surjective connected-generic geometric map to A1 are limited to one or two doubles; the two-double case requires EVEN source degree. No silent product hypothesis for the trace receiver or Euler-integral positivity is permitted. Published Galois-invariant/unique-ruling descent already closes that special descent uncertainty: a proper native factor with such a ruling would disprove JC(2). Conditional on JC(2), every geometric ruling must have a NONTRIVIAL Galois orbit of inequivalent rulings. CURRENT DESCENT RESULT: every geometric affine-type ruling of a proper native intermediate is unique and actually descends; its additive action descends too. Conditional on JC(2), only ADDITIVELY RIGID intermediates with COMPLETE-type Galois-permuted P1 rulings remain. Their descent is OPEN. A zero Picard orbit norm does not identify the individual fibrations.
lessons_before.reopen_when: A prescribed primitive group or smaller geometric cost is proved, or a canonical atomic coupling replaces the trace filter while retaining its exact cover and base-change-compatible polynomial descent. An actual candidate leaves the rank-one cubic architecture, for example through non-descended higher-rank return geometry, another compiler or a non-locally-nilpotent auxiliary with constants outside the stable-polynomial criterion, satisfies its whole-source determinant identity, retains the exact complete fibre and gluing, and proves absolute atomicity. In one constant direction, an auxiliary-only canonical escape must be all-inactive and demonstrate a full constant ring outside the stable-polynomial criterion, retaining exact marked fibre and descent. For root feedback, an atomic candidate must leave the all-signal-retaining polynomial root subring class, for example using additional source channels or a changed first output, and still prove the complete marked fibre and atomicity. A proved broader curved/multi-direction or genuine cross-block construction removes the explicit formal scalar denominator on the WHOLE source, retains complete marks and gluing, and proves full-map absolute atomicity. Scalar-line degree sweeps are closed. A two-effective-control native family leaves the scalar-line and affine-r sectors through nonlinear Laurent-r dependence, or another first-output/compiler/cross-block architecture, and proves whole-source polynomial landing, exact canonical marks, gluing and full-map atomicity. A native candidate has Cout genuinely nonlinear, escapes generic profile-coordinate reduction at a non-dividing polynomial-r degree pair or in a negative Laurent sector, and proves the full marked scheme, effective gluing and absence of ALL actual polynomial factors; another compiler or changed first-output architecture remains permitted. A whole-source native construction has genuinely nonlinear Cout and exact canonical marks/gluing; any claimed factor must escape literal profile recovery and, in the polynomial-r sector, polynomial intermediate extension. A genuinely non-plane generic intermediate surface with the exact saturated field model and whole-source realization, a new curve-witness failure or another compiler must be analyzed without assuming JC(2). A proper factor realizes a NON-PLANE geometric generic retained fibre, both field degrees exceed one, and all curve, unit, saturation, divisor and whole-polynomial requirements are certified; or an actual native integration preserves complete canonical marks/gluing and excludes every such factor. A proper generic surface is geometrically unit-free with the exact arithmetic factorial ring, saturated embedded field, whole carried curve and an all-irreducible-constant-fibre intermediate signal; both whole degrees exceed one and the entire map/global marked gluing is certified. Nonconstant-unit and finite-index unit candidates are closed. Produce an actual negative-log unit-free geometrically nonfactorial intermediate with nonzero Picard group and no invariant class, the exact canonical volume and both etale arrows. The u^m*v=z^d-a families with m>=2 are explicit necessary-condition models, not permission for a bounded coefficient sweep or proof of a whole factor. Supply an actual compatible nonautomorphic Keller atlas and a WHOLE multi-root embedded line satisfying all contacts, both cofinite arrows and a different smooth whole spread, or move to a proved intermediate geometry without such a plane chart. Finite/formal neighborhoods and exact primitives alone are insufficient; JC(2) and canonical atomicity are not declared solved. Prove a compatible JC(2)-counterexample atlas in the descended-ruling class, or prove an actual failure of ruling descent retaining all field, curve, volume and whole-source constraints. Respect the nonfinite source-divisor and sheet-loss budget, the dividing-index group constraint and the orbifold multiplicity/parity gates. Full canonical marks, gluing and absolute stable atomicity remain necessary. Prove descent or exclude actual realization of the remaining COMPLETE-type Galois orbit. The affine-type descent subproblem is closed; extend by a new identification argument, not more necessary conditions.

lessons_before.title: Test global spectral translations and algebraic curvature before matrix padding
lessons_before.when: A commuting Long quantum pair in a finite operator algebra or a faithful projective carrier is to be completed, or a matrix repair keeps both position images scalar.
lessons_before.use: Use the all-deformation commutative joint centralizer proved from Cent(R,S)=K[R,S]. Work in the actual algebra E. The two global spectral Koszul classes (h,0),(0,h) test individual conjugates; if they vanish, the choice-independent curvature class lies in B/(delta1 B+delta2 B) and exactly tests the remaining mixed relation. Seek a nonzero global class or a finite primitive in that actual centralizer. For scalar matrix positions, normalized trace of a flat matrix pair is already a flat scalar pair, with no degree increase. For a projective carrier this scalarization is in its endomorphism algebra and does not supply a Weyl free frame.
lessons_before.avoid: Using pointwise or generic spectral vanishing to infer the global translation class, replacing the actual centralizer by its completed polynomial algebra, treating a completed curvature primitive as algebraic, tracing arbitrary nonlinear matrix tuples when the positions are nonscalar or the joint centralizer is noncommutative, or assuming a partial module has a faithful formal frame without separatedness/rank evidence.
lessons_before.boundary: The classical joint-centralizer theorem and formal induction cover every commuting Long deformation, including nonpositional first images. The finite carrier extension requires a faithful embedding, supplied by QMC1 rank-one torsion-freeness for full carriers or directly by finite projective corners. No finite Long pair with both individual conjugates is constructed. A twisted Ore boundary with double residue one proves completed curvature exactness is insufficient but is not a finite Weyl example. Actual algebra isomorphisms transport the classes; a classical Poisson change alone does not. The old QRF2 residue and the related Hochschild classes are not identified with these classes. QST1 separates rational and spectral admission. Any nonzero Adler period excludes the entire rational operator division ring and makes the universal spectral class nontorsion; the G(a)+mu*v first period is explicit in all degrees. This blocks every rational conjugate and the corresponding actual rank-one projective pair orbit without a scalar free frame. Fixed rational mate equations descend through finite algebraic coefficient covers by monic-denominator Galois averaging. Constant-coefficient G has instead a critical-value torsion annihilator and a rational mate. Zero Adler periods are insufficient for rational admission: a torus residue excludes harmonic/Euler functional classes even with arbitrary operator denominators and identity spectators. Finite primitive-divisor and ordinary infinity exclusions must not be silently promoted to rational ones. No arbitrary moving spectral coefficient localization, nonlinear Galois descent or universal Long rational normalization is proved. QFC1 closes algebraic curvature exactness under actual centralizer module finiteness, even if only the generic centralizer is module-finite. Integral individual mates and the polynomial classical centralizer yield an integral polynomial primitive in every rank, h-small for a flat classical tuple. Independent Bernstein leading symbols with a full module-finite Poisson centralizer supply a scalar filtered certificate. The required Long input has not been constructed. QET1 can decide the translation/completion route from the actual centralizer field. With finite generation, actual individual mates make it etale. Scalar Weyl units and a birational field force finite flat completion; a nontrivial Galois field makes simultaneous individual mates impossible. Non-Galois degree at least three and fixed sheets for all generic inertia generators remain possible. This does not compute a Long centralizer or its global translation classes. QET1 also removes actual parameter poles under the polynomial classical centralizer hypothesis, with no finite-generation or field-degree assumption: individual mates have unique finite polynomial polar parts. Subtraction preserves any integral curvature exactly, so an actual generic flat tuple with regular positions descends to a finite integral flat tuple and can match a prescribed classical flat frame. Only h is inverted; rational spatial/operator denominators and arbitrary completed series remain outside this descent. QTB1 provides all-partner tests without finite generation of the actual centralizer. A nontrivial finite Galois factor or actual new radical in its fraction field forbids simultaneous individual mates; birationality makes the centralizer polynomial and permits finite completion. The radical certificate uses two actual commutants, a cleared polynomial identity and a certified nonpower. No actual Long certificate is produced. QPD1 proves nonzero annihilator of each global translation class iff a rational individual mate exists, by clearing a finite adjoint orbit with a spectral polynomial. It applies to rank-one finite projective Weyl orders. Zero classes remain the actual-mate criterion; nonzero torsion can coexist with no actual mate. Full rational and actual curvature tests remain separate. QCI1 shows that even a polynomial actual joint centralizer and a flat completion retain a nontrivial residual division cover for Long. After adjoining the full rational position centralizer the residual indices are at least3. No ambient rational target automorphism, even with h poles, can make the fixed positions ordinary rational coordinate functions. Mixed source polarizations remain outside this statement. QCI1 adds a finite-carrier test before the actual spectral complex is available: a rational matrix Weyl generator with uniformly bounded Bernstein powers cannot preserve a finite full left lattice of any rank. Its exact rational degree-m Weyl pairs demonstrate why rational full relations alone do not supply an actual finite algebra in which the zero-class criterion can be applied.
lessons_before.reopen_when: An actual candidate lattice and commuting position pair admit computable global translation classes, a structural theorem proves algebraic curvature exactness for its centralizer, or a genuinely matrix-valued/projective model passes all classes and global admission with a finite frame where required.

lessons_before.title: Keep the original source plane while dividing out a derivative power and testing the modified boundary
lessons_before.when: A nonmonic output equation might acquire a rational source root, or its leading orders permit an intermediate pole.
lessons_before.use: First compute the coefficient integer pole spectrum. A root with only regular branches and full leading poles forces R=D^(m-2), p=a(f)/D and w=u/D polynomial. Their cyclic derivative surface is integral by an infinity valuation, while its Cstar boundary is omitted except finitely many points by the full root equation. Apply the retained nonproperness theorem to the polynomial map from the original A2. Independently, try a balanced rescaling U=A z and certify the resulting finite monic surface normal by the explicit partial-zero and triple gcd test. The latter gives full arbitrary-degree irreducibility; the former gives no rational roots and hence full cubic irreducibility. HC4MYIF0/1/2 constrain every source factorization, close square-free-leading quartics and supply a field-degree and nonnormal-order obstruction for the remaining unequal pair. HC4MYIG0/1/2 add reduced-pencil rational monodromy, one-exception polynomial parameters and all-degree scaled and reciprocal-scaled one-variable output closures. The same mechanism now closes rational scalings and rational affine input with polynomial output translation, including all sparse two-positive-term outputs without a gcd condition. HC4MYIH0/1/2 add the strict projective multiplicity bound, exact affine-in-V exception certificate and all-degree mixed-critical-value expansion outputs. HC4MYII0/1/2/3/4 add plane intermediate-branch geometry, unrestricted rational affine parameters, actual-inertia quotient certificates, all nonadjacent pure-power binomials and every cubic output. HC4MYIJ0/1/2/3 add relative central-series descent, actual product-cover preservation with arbitrary parameter monodromy, and the all-degree finite-critical-pole binomial certificate. HC4MYIK0/1/2/3 add parameter-cover unit norms, integral algebraic monic models, a direct critical-value valuation lemma and unrestricted plane polynomial-output closure. HC4MYIL0/1/2 add generative factor transfer, exact fixed-multiplier class lattices and all-degree multivariable suspension closure with full global filtration. HC4MYIM0/1/2/3 add parameter-extension irreducibility, moving-row invariant vanishing, an exact content-fibre criterion and uniform adapted global frames. The IM3 determinant-one parameter matrix covers moving B, multivariable monic-leading b and arbitrary affine root terms, with a separate primitive-content check. The IM3 frame admits every strict joint degree-gap remainder; its univariate leading-divisibility corollary allows all lower P coefficients. HC4MYIN0/1 replace the former global-frame requirement by rank-two reflexive pencil descent and close every primitive disjoint moving suspension. HC4MYIO0/1/2 extend to arbitrary independent coefficient fields and overlapping polynomial directions; monic and polynomial-Bezout leading overlap outputs have uniform generic filtrations. HC4MYIP0/1/2 use moved relative additive actions instead of positive generic filtrations, and force every surviving overlap image into the multiplier-variable invariant subring. HC4MYIQ0/1/2 descend any univariate generic helper, close every one-helper admitted overlap including nonprimitive content, and reduce HC4 survivors to two-helper invariant plane curves. HC4MYIR0/1/2 close multiplier-zero images in all helper counts and every admitted two-helper overlap in every stable dimension; the complete admitted HC4 overlap family is now closed. lessons_before.title: Use all pairwise resultants at infinity before treating higher-degree source factors as unconstrained
lessons_before.when: A nonmonic source polynomial can factor without a rational root, especially after the leading triple gcd has excluded intermediate poles.
lessons_before.use: Factor primitively over the source polynomial UFD. Smoothness of P(f_1,z)+f_2 and pairwise coprime leading factors make every pairwise resultant a complex constant. Monic normalization and the uniform root-difference valuation at V=infinity give ell_i/d_i+ell_j/d_j=1/m while sum ell_i=0. Three factors or two equal factors are impossible in all dimensions. In the plane the prior no-root gate leaves two unequal degrees at least two and closes quartics. For that unequal pair compute the exact resultant power, Keller-degree divisor and explicit integral source element whose monogenic order must be nonnormal. HC4MYIG0/1/2 add reduced-pencil rational monodromy, one-exception polynomial parameters and all-degree scaled and reciprocal-scaled one-variable output closures. The same mechanism now closes rational scalings and rational affine input with polynomial output translation, including all sparse two-positive-term outputs without a gcd condition. HC4MYIH0/1/2 add the strict projective multiplicity bound, exact affine-in-V exception certificate and all-degree mixed-critical-value expansion outputs. HC4MYII0/1/2/3/4 add plane intermediate-branch geometry, unrestricted rational affine parameters, actual-inertia quotient certificates, all nonadjacent pure-power binomials and every cubic output. HC4MYIJ0/1/2/3 add relative central-series descent, actual product-cover preservation with arbitrary parameter monodromy, and the all-degree finite-critical-pole binomial certificate. HC4MYIK0/1/2/3 add parameter-cover unit norms, integral algebraic monic models, a direct critical-value valuation lemma and unrestricted plane polynomial-output closure. HC4MYIL0/1/2 add generative factor transfer, exact fixed-multiplier class lattices and all-degree multivariable suspension closure with full global filtration. HC4MYIM0/1/2/3 add parameter-extension irreducibility, moving-row invariant vanishing, an exact content-fibre criterion and uniform adapted global frames. The IM3 determinant-one parameter matrix covers moving B, multivariable monic-leading b and arbitrary affine root terms, with a separate primitive-content check. The IM3 frame admits every strict joint degree-gap remainder; its univariate leading-divisibility corollary allows all lower P coefficients. HC4MYIN0/1 replace the former global-frame requirement by rank-two reflexive pencil descent and close every primitive disjoint moving suspension. HC4MYIO0/1/2 extend to arbitrary independent coefficient fields and overlapping polynomial directions; monic and polynomial-Bezout leading overlap outputs have uniform generic filtrations. HC4MYIP0/1/2 use moved relative additive actions instead of positive generic filtrations, and force every surviving overlap image into the multiplier-variable invariant subring. HC4MYIQ0/1/2 descend any univariate generic helper, close every one-helper admitted overlap including nonprimitive content, and reduce HC4 survivors to two-helper invariant plane curves. HC4MYIR0/1/2 close multiplier-zero images in all helper counts and every admitted two-helper overlap in every stable dimension; the complete admitted HC4 overlap family is now closed. IS0/1/2 identify the full JC2 content of an unconditional residual-free extension, including an exact source-correlated class lattice and actual unit-Hessian embeddings with an always invertible constructed gradient. IT0/1/2 give intrinsic finite-energy and inverse-Hessian certificates and a mixed three-direction criterion before any ambient output construction. IU0/1/2 exploit actual free projections and the zero-section first jet, closing critical-value traces and testing the global immersion obligation in a universal noncritical construction. IV0/1/2 separate complete compensation identities from codimension-one source recovery and provide a canonical Legendre-hypersurface normality gate. IW0/1/2 close every constant trace through an infinite-order integral middle-cycle obstruction, with arbitrary helper degrees. IX0/1/2 separate arbitrary quadric plane classes from actual radical-curve recovery and close coordinate-composite or smooth/nonparametric descended nonconstant traces. IY0/1/2 close contractible full-preimage curves and descended cusps, and impose the exact generic-pencil boundary-defect certificate on the remaining multibranch cases. IZ0/1/2 match the intrinsic generic genus on all one-place zero curves and close every rank-one descended trace, including all internally multibranch cases and positive-power rational descent. JA0/1/2 force the actual disjoint extra-prime/unit/boundary configuration and bound its one-place part; scalar extra units close the selected one-place case.
lessons_before.avoid: Inferring constant resultants from disjoint finite factors when their leading coefficients share a divisor; assuming every unequal pair contradicts the valuation equations; extending the plane rational-root theorem to arbitrary dimensions; calling a primitive integral order normal; applying ruled-surface classification without Q-factoriality or almost surjectivity; inferring actual Keller realizations from a surviving degree pattern.
lessons_before.boundary: HC4MYIF0 extends the obstruction to all factor patterns: for any Keller map in n>=2 dimensions, primitive source factors with pairwise coprime leading coefficients have constant cross-resultants. The target gcd(a,a_prime,b_(m-1))=1 guarantees that coprimality. At V=infinity all normalized-root differences have valuation -1/m, so every pair gives ell_i/d_i+ell_j/d_j=1/m with sum ell_i=0. This excludes three or more factors and two equal factors in arbitrary degree and dimension. HC4MYIF1 combines the plane rational-root gate to leave exactly two unequal factors 2<=d<e under that gcd. In particular all square-free-leading quartics of arbitrary parameter degree and all quartics with gcd(a,b_3)=1 close, without a critical-discriminant, root-group or special-fibre hypothesis. The full quartic conclusion uses the plane-only root gate. HC4MYIF2 proves for the surviving unequal pair R=lambda*a^(e(d-1))*D^(e-d), the exact degree divisor m(e-d)/gcd(de,m(e-d)) for [L:F], and an explicit integral zeta=a^ceil(e(d-1)/(e-d))*D generating a necessarily nonnormal finite monogenic order. Unequal-factor valuations remain consistent; generic primitive orders cannot be treated as normal. The remaining gcd-admitted high-degree cases have precisely two unequal factors of degrees at least two, subject to that field-degree and order obstruction; joint repeated-leading cases remain separate. Both plane endpoints and unrestricted HC4/JC2 remain open. HC4MYIG0 supplies an all-degree rational-parameter regularity test: every finite reduced pencil member must be nonconstant and square-free. At most one projective parameter point can have constant point form; Riemann-Hurwitz forces any nontrivial composition to give a forbidden constant finite member. A polynomial parameter also passes when all but one finite fibre are reduced and the exceptional multiplicity gcd is one. The proof explicitly imports Petravchuk-Iena Lemma 2(1) closedness/noncomposition equivalence and reuses projective Riemann-Hurwitz. HC4MYIG1 shows Keller pullback preserves these tests and the full group of every finite Galois cover of the resulting one-variable rational parameter field. It extends the filtered class-action criterion without deleting any affine pole fibres. Parameters include (V+B(U))/A(U) and Q(U)(V+B(U)) with arbitrary polynomial A,Q and arbitrary repeated zeros; critical points and critical lines are allowed. HC4MYIG2 closes every P=A(T)R(c(T)z+beta(T))+B(T) for arbitrary nonconstant constant-coefficient R and nonzero polynomial A,c, with beta,B polynomial, and every polynomial P=R(c(T)z+beta(T))/Q(T)+B(T) with nonzero polynomial Q,c. All parameter, source, z and embedding degrees and leading multiplicities are unrestricted, with no root-group restriction. This closes the S3 family T^(3k)(z^3+z)+B(T) despite its intermediate pole, and the full sparse family T^k z^m+z^(m-1)+B(T) despite previously allowed unequal higher factors. lessons_before.title: Separate spectral torsion, rational denominators and projective frame changes
lessons_before.when: A rational partner, spectral localization, coefficient cover or fractional/projective frame is proposed after a finite differential obstruction, or all Adler periods vanish.
lessons_before.use: A nonzero Adler moment excludes mates in the entire rational division ring, not only finite operators. Its first nonzero moment gives triangular strong duals for every q(S), proving nontorsion of the universal spectral class. For G(a)+mu*v the all-degree first period is explicit and survives every rational conjugate. Use rational Galois Reynolds descent for fixed linear mate equations on finite coefficient covers. If Adler periods vanish, test rational torus residues: rational functions of Euler operators and harmonic oscillator Hamiltonians still have no rational mate. In an actual rank-one projective realization, reduce the centralizer of exact r to the relative division ring before testing a rational pair orbit.
lessons_before.avoid: Inferring rational nonexistence from a finite primitive-divisor or ordinary infinity obstruction, identifying arbitrary PDO series with rational operators, equating scalar spectral localization with moving v,u coefficient poles, using Galois averaging for nonlinear simultaneous tuples, or assuming every Long deformation admits the obstructed rational normal form.
lessons_before.boundary: G(a) has a torsion spectral class with critical-value annihilator and a rational mate. A mixed squarefree-leading operator can also have a rational mate. The harmonic oscillator passes all Adler periods but fails rational torus admission. The all-cover rational descent uses the one-derivation Euclidean ring. Torus obstruction is stable in every rank, while coefficient-cover descent is asserted in that one-variable setting. Projective obstruction requires an actual rational pair equivalence; arbitrary formal gauges may be nonrational. General nonscalar matrices and new Long rational pair orbits remain open. QET1 uses Galois structure of the actual commutative centralizer field, not Galois averaging of coefficient covers. With finite generation and scalar Weyl units, a nontrivial Galois centralizer field forbids simultaneous individual mates. Its quadratic scalar control has an exact rational mate, preserving the rational/finite distinction. This is independent of QST1's fixed linear rational descent. QET1 also removes actual parameter poles under the polynomial classical centralizer hypothesis, with no finite-generation or field-degree assumption: individual mates have unique finite polynomial polar parts. Subtraction preserves any integral curvature exactly, so an actual generic flat tuple with regular positions descends to a finite integral flat tuple and can match a prescribed classical flat frame. Only h is inverted; rational spatial/operator denominators and arbitrary completed series remain outside this descent. QTB1's radical/Galois-factor obstruction requires membership in the fraction field of the actual centralizer, not merely commutation in the full operator division ring. An actual ratio b/c and a certified identity q(F)b^k=p(F)c^k suffice, without centralizer finite generation. This does not replace QST1 rational denominator or coefficient-cover tests. QPD1 supplies the spectral-denominator converse unused in QST1: rational mate existence on the coefficient curve is equivalent to torsion of the finite universal spectral class. The source admission boundary is corrected; Adler, torus and rational Galois proofs are unchanged. Spectral clearing also applies to rank-one projective Weyl orders, where rational commutants automatically belong to Frac B. This is not an identification with arbitrary moving-coefficient localization.
lessons_before.reopen_when: An actual finite carrier has a different rational orbit, a new mixed operator passes both period and torus tests with a finite Darboux certificate, or a structural theorem controls the rational pair orbit for every bounded Long carrier.

lessons_before.title: Use the full trace-dual pencil and radical rank to test the actual non-equivariant finite algebra
lessons_before.when: A Keller normalization has sole index-two R and a source coordinate with nonvanishing simple pole along the entire R, regular on every other unramified omitted prime; in particular the full complementary r2q1 row.
lessons_before.use: The inverse different is O(R), generated everywhere by 1,x, so B^vee=B+xB. Use both symmetric trace pairings G0 and G1 and require their block columns to generate the entire dual at every target point. Their determinant pencil is the full source-coordinate inverse, with leading G_R and exact degree drop2 there. At a closed value compute G1 on kerG0: its rank is exactly the local ramification excess, by maximal-ideal/socle Frobenius duality. Sum these ranks in d=n+3+E. Couple this to the exact line-image member factorizations and the already retained conductor derivative pole d-3.
lessons_before.avoid: Treating Tr(xB) subset A as the full dual description without checking global nonvanishing of the pole coefficient; deleting unramified primes; mistaking the finite-x normalization N minus R for U; using generic block rank instead of a sheaf surjection; confusing several folds with a nonimmersive factor; claiming matrix sufficiency or global Keller realization from finite local controls; repackaging sealed PF2OMIT4 formulas as new results; using the unregistered central inverse draft as evidence.
lessons_before.boundary: PF2RULED53 is uniform in finite degree, D orders, poles, boundary values and coefficients throughout the sole-ramified r2q1 row. It needs no symmetry and no zero-excess assumption. The local finite controls pass these necessary conditions but have no marked source A2. 136 controls support universal written proofs with imported duality facts; remaining finite maps and independent proof review stay open.
lessons_before.reopen_when: Construct or exclude an actual finite algebra satisfying the trace-dual equality, global block surjection, radical-isotropy/excess equation, coefficient-unit inverse, line-image factors and conductor pole simultaneously. Preserve every prime and the actual source embedding. Other R orders and common rulings require their full pole/different modules rather than substituting this two-generator special case.

lessons_before.title: Certify rational-parameter regularity from reduced pencil members before analyzing nonnormal factor orders
lessons_before.when: Root or divisor-class monodromy may descend from a rational target parameter, especially a scaled one-variable output with repeated leading coefficients.
lessons_before.use: Require coprime numerator and denominator and all finite pencil members nonconstant and square-free. A rational composition would force every finite ramified point into the one possible constant point form, and Riemann-Hurwitz would then force a forbidden constant member. For polynomial parameters permit one exceptional fibre if its multiplicity gcd is one. Keller pullback preserves both certificates and hence every finite parameter-cover group. Apply this to (V+B)/A and Q(V+B), with arbitrary repeated zeros, to close polynomial and polynomial reciprocal scalings of a fixed one-variable R, including all admitted affine input changes and every degree. The same mechanism now closes rational scalings and rational affine input with polynomial output translation, including all sparse two-positive-term outputs without a gcd condition. HC4MYIH0/1/2 add the strict projective multiplicity bound, exact affine-in-V exception certificate and all-degree mixed-critical-value expansion outputs. HC4MYII0/1/2/3/4 add plane intermediate-branch geometry, unrestricted rational affine parameters, actual-inertia quotient certificates, all nonadjacent pure-power binomials and every cubic output. HC4MYIJ0/1/2/3 add relative central-series descent, actual product-cover preservation with arbitrary parameter monodromy, and the all-degree finite-critical-pole binomial certificate. HC4MYIK0/1/2/3 add parameter-cover unit norms, integral algebraic monic models, a direct critical-value valuation lemma and unrestricted plane polynomial-output closure. HC4MYIL0/1/2 add generative factor transfer, exact fixed-multiplier class lattices and all-degree multivariable suspension closure with full global filtration. HC4MYIM0/1/2/3 add parameter-extension irreducibility, moving-row invariant vanishing, an exact content-fibre criterion and uniform adapted global frames. The IM3 determinant-one parameter matrix covers moving B, multivariable monic-leading b and arbitrary affine root terms, with a separate primitive-content check. The IM3 frame admits every strict joint degree-gap remainder; its univariate leading-divisibility corollary allows all lower P coefficients. HC4MYIN0/1 replace the former global-frame requirement by rank-two reflexive pencil descent and close every primitive disjoint moving suspension. HC4MYIO0/1/2 extend to arbitrary independent coefficient fields and overlapping polynomial directions; monic and polynomial-Bezout leading overlap outputs have uniform generic filtrations. HC4MYIP0/1/2 use moved relative additive actions instead of positive generic filtrations, and force every surviving overlap image into the multiplier-variable invariant subring. HC4MYIQ0/1/2 descend any univariate generic helper, close every one-helper admitted overlap including nonprimitive content, and reduce HC4 survivors to two-helper invariant plane curves. HC4MYIR0/1/2 close multiplier-zero images in all helper counts and every admitted two-helper overlap in every stable dimension; the complete admitted HC4 overlap family is now closed. IS0/1/2 identify the full JC2 content of an unconditional residual-free extension, including an exact source-correlated class lattice and actual unit-Hessian embeddings with an always invertible constructed gradient. IT0/1/2 give intrinsic finite-energy and inverse-Hessian certificates and a mixed three-direction criterion before any ambient output construction. IU0/1/2 exploit actual free projections and the zero-section first jet, closing critical-value traces and testing the global immersion obligation in a universal noncritical construction. IV0/1/2 separate complete compensation identities from codimension-one source recovery and provide a canonical Legendre-hypersurface normality gate. IW0/1/2 close every constant trace through an infinite-order integral middle-cycle obstruction, with arbitrary helper degrees. IX0/1/2 separate arbitrary quadric plane classes from actual radical-curve recovery and close coordinate-composite or smooth/nonparametric descended nonconstant traces. IY0/1/2 close contractible full-preimage curves and descended cusps, and impose the exact generic-pencil boundary-defect certificate on the remaining multibranch cases. IZ0/1/2 match the intrinsic generic genus on all one-place zero curves and close every rank-one descended trace, including all internally multibranch cases and positive-power rational descent. JA0/1/2 force the actual disjoint extra-prime/unit/boundary configuration and bound its one-place part; scalar extra units close the selected one-place case.
lessons_before.avoid: Allowing the constant finite member of 1/x^d; ignoring multiple finite members; assuming all fixed fibres irreducible; replacing field regularity with affine-etale finiteness; dropping pole fibres from global filtration hypotheses; assuming a polynomial slice is locally nilpotent; treating every rational affine-isotrivial representation as admitted without polynomiality and a parameter certificate; inferring nonlinear Hessian invariance.
lessons_before.boundary: HC4MYIG0 supplies an all-degree rational-parameter regularity test: every finite reduced pencil member must be nonconstant and square-free. At most one projective parameter point can have constant point form; Riemann-Hurwitz forces any nontrivial composition to give a forbidden constant finite member. A polynomial parameter also passes when all but one finite fibre are reduced and the exceptional multiplicity gcd is one. The proof explicitly imports Petravchuk-Iena Lemma 2(1) closedness/noncomposition equivalence and reuses projective Riemann-Hurwitz. HC4MYIG1 shows Keller pullback preserves these tests and the full group of every finite Galois cover of the resulting one-variable rational parameter field. It extends the filtered class-action criterion without deleting any affine pole fibres. Parameters include (V+B(U))/A(U) and Q(U)(V+B(U)) with arbitrary polynomial A,Q and arbitrary repeated zeros; critical points and critical lines are allowed. HC4MYIG2 closes every P=A(T)R(c(T)z+beta(T))+B(T) for arbitrary nonconstant constant-coefficient R and nonzero polynomial A,c, with beta,B polynomial, and every polynomial P=R(c(T)z+beta(T))/Q(T)+B(T) with nonzero polynomial Q,c. All parameter, source, z and embedding degrees and leading multiplicities are unrestricted, with no root-group restriction. This closes the S3 family T^(3k)(z^3+z)+B(T) despite its intermediate pole, and the full sparse family T^k z^m+z^(m-1)+B(T) despite previously allowed unequal higher factors. General coefficient variation, rational affine representations not meeting the stated polynomial or parameter tests, two unequal factors outside these new closures, other joint repeated-leading cases and other outputs remain open. Both plane endpoints and unrestricted HC4/JC2 remain open. HC4MYIG0 further admits a one-exception rational pencil with algebraically independent numerator and denominator and exceptional multiplicity gcd one; independence rules out every omitted point form. HC4MYIG1 therefore certifies q=Q(U)(V+B(U))/D(U) for arbitrary coprime nonzero polynomial Q,D and polynomial B. HC4MYIG2 upgrades the output closure to P=A(T)R(c(T)z+beta(T))+B(T) polynomial, with arbitrary nonzero rational A,c, rational beta and polynomial B. In particular every sparse a(T)z^m+b(T)z^(m-1)+d(T), a nonzero, closes fully in all degrees without any gcd or leading multiplicity restriction. This removes both unequal-factor and common-repeated-leading residuals for that sparse family. General coefficient variation and rational output translations lacking a parameter certificate remain open; both plane endpoints and unrestricted HC4/JC2 remain open. HC4MYIH0 now permits several exceptional projective pencil values: for independent coprime numerator and denominator, require a multiplicity-one factor in each exceptional member and a bound M_lambda for its largest multiplicity. If sigma=sum(1-1/M_lambda)<2, every composition degree is excluded by the per-fibre bound (d-1)(1-1/M_lambda) and Riemann-Hurwitz. Keller pullback preserves the exact multiplicities and hence full finite parameter-cover monodromy. Equality is not closed: an explicit independent-numerator cubic rational example has four double-plus-simple members and sigma=2. The four numerical equality lists and d=1 modulo each M are necessary only. HC4MYIH1 computes all exceptional values of (Q(T)V+C(T))/D(T) from content gcds when D is nonconstant square-free. Its finite members always have a primitive horizontal factor of multiplicity one. HC4MYIH2 closes P=D[R(beta+Hz)-R(beta)]/H^2+B whenever H,D are nonconstant square-free coprime, H divides R_prime(beta), and the zeros of H select at most three critical values of constant-coefficient R. All source, coefficient, embedding and z degrees are unrestricted, with leading D H^(m-2) and repeated H levels in m>=4. This includes an explicit family for every m>=3 and a mixed-three-critical-value quartic failing the older leading gcd. The proof adds no new external theorem or orbifold classification. Coefficient profiles at or above the bound, missing simple factors, uncertified denominator members and other output geometries remain open. Both plane endpoints and unrestricted HC4/JC2 remain open. HC4MYII0 now identifies every ramified divisorial curve of any plane Keller intermediate field as a polynomially parametrizable nonproperness component; other unramified sheets may remain visible. HC4MYII1 consequently makes every rational affine-in-V parameter (Q V+C)/D regular under plane Keller pullback, with only Q,D nonzero and triple gcd one: primitive horizontal branch curves leave at most one finite composition branch value, and Riemann-Hurwitz plus valuation one exclude the remaining power map. No multiplicity or denominator restriction remains in this plane parameter class. HC4MYII2 closes every final-polynomial rational affine fixed-polynomial output A R(cz+beta)+B0, now with rational B0. HC4MYII3 places the normal subgroup of actual nonparametrizable-curve inertia inside every source group; transitivity gives irreducibility, while a separately preserved quotient, including any nilpotent quotient, gives the full group. This closes (T-c0)^r z^m+z^q+d(T) for every r>=1 and 1<=q<m, since its non-axis critical curves lie in a torus and the residual quotient is abelian. HC4MYII4 completes every cubic output with all coefficient and leading degrees unrestricted: square and zero critical discriminants use II2, while a linear critical double cover forces integral critical values, polynomial cube scaling and a monic Jacobian contradiction. Full splitting-group preservation is not asserted for all cubics. These are plane-only strengthenings; earlier all-dimensional strict multiplicity tests and their equality counterexample remain valid. General higher-degree coefficient variation outside the field/inertia certificates and other output geometries remain open. Both plane endpoints and unrestricted HC4/JC2 remain open. HC4MYIJ0 extends the full-group gate to a relative central series over any separately preserved quotient, using the absence of Galois intermediate fields to descend the series. HC4MYIJ1 preserves every finite cover etale on an actual product U times Y when the finite geometric fibre image is nilpotent: commuting product monodromy makes it relatively central, and an algebraic section plus newly used full faithfulness of Milne Theorem 3.4 identifies the residual field with a genuine parameter cover. Both statements work in all Keller dimensions; the parameter quotient may be nonnilpotent. Essential surjectivity is not used and old forward-only imports remain unchanged. HC4MYIJ2 combines this with plane bad inertia, replacing the former nilpotent residual-group restriction by a punctured-cylinder or certified product-cover quotient. HC4MYIJ3 closes a(T)z^m+b(T)z^q+d(T) whenever a,b are nonzero, 1<=q<m and b^m/a^q has a finite pole, equivalently a^q does not divide b^m. The reduced critical-value curve U V^(m-q)=W has a nonconstant unit U(T), so no component admits polynomial A1 parametrization; the residual branch support is vertical coefficient levels plus V=0. This proves full group preservation, irreducibility and every carried stable plane inverse, without any coefficient, leading-multiplicity or degree bound. In particular every a(T)z^m+z^q+d(T) closes for arbitrary nonzero a, and varying shared-zero coefficients a=T^(m+1),b=T close for every m>=2 and 1<=q<m. The binomial bad-inertia application is plane-only. No-finite-pole binomials require another certificate; their failure of this test is not a nonclosure or Keller-realization claim. Nonproduct residual arrangements and nonnilpotent geometric fibre images remain distinct. Both plane endpoints and unrestricted HC4/JC2 remain open. HC4MYIK0/1/2/3 now close the entire plane polynomial output coefficient class. HC4MYIK0 extends normal monogenic irreducibility preservation over a finite algebraic parameter curve: the actual source is smooth and finite free over the original polynomial source, and its cross-resultant units have nonzero constant norms. Integrality of every conjugate monic model makes both the target resultant and its inverse integral; inertia, purity and algebraic section descent finish the proof without assuming constant units or an affine-plane parameter source. HC4MYIK1 admits every integral algebraic affine monic model in all dimensions, and combines the no-pole binomial side with IJ3 to complete all plane binomials. HC4MYIK2 directly proves that integral critical values force integral centered monic coefficients in every degree and every residue-characteristic-zero valuation; no dynamical reduction theorem is imported. HC4MYIK3 uses contained plane bad inertia and its normal-orbit block system. Ordinary one-variable Luroth plus a unique-pole argument gives a polynomial outer block quotient. Its surviving critical curves are polynomially parametrizable, so every outer critical value is integral. IK2/1 make the source outer action transitive, and the contained bad inertia then makes the whole root action transitive. Therefore P(f,Z)+g is irreducible for every nonconstant P in C(T)[z], and every carried closed stable embedding through (T,xy-P(T,z)) with P polynomial of positive z degree and r>=1 forces the plane Keller inverse. Every coefficient, source, embedding, leading multiplicity and z degree is unrestricted. This retires all remaining plane coefficient-profile, unequal-factor, no-finite-pole-binomial and critical-curve refinements for this output class. Full splitting-group preservation is not inferred; earlier stronger group and all-dimensional subclass statements remain valid. The unrestricted final theorem is plane-only. Other output geometries and finding compatible ambient observables for arbitrary graph embeddings remain separate. Both plane endpoints and unrestricted HC4/JC2 remain open. HC4MYIL0/1/2 extend the entire polynomial-output closure to arbitrarily many Z variables and arbitrary fixed polynomial multipliers in disjoint X variables. Minimal inner degree gives P=R(S) over C(T) with S noncomposite. lessons_before.title: Turn actual centralizer module finiteness into finite flat completion
lessons_before.when: A finite commuting quantum tuple has actual individual conjugates and a polynomial classical joint Poisson centralizer, especially for a Long candidate.
lessons_before.use: Prove actual centralizer module finiteness over the commuting images; generic module finiteness suffices. Translation connections force the centralizer to be the polynomial ring, and a finite polynomial de Rham primitive removes the remaining curvature with no parameter poles. Preserve a flat classical tuple by choosing h-small corrections. In a scalar Weyl algebra, independent leading symbols and a complete module-finite Poisson centralizer give an all-degree filtered certificate and an explicit rank-two primitive bound. For a finite corner verify the algebra hypotheses before applying the separate matrix-carrier criterion.
lessons_before.avoid: Substituting algebra finite generation, finite fraction-field degree, polynomial h-adic completion, finitely many symbol tests or a finite curvature jet for the actual module-finiteness hypothesis. Do not use rational or completed mates outside the actual generic algebra to assert integral classical-limit preservation or assume every projective idealizer has the scalar Bernstein filtration. Failure of this sufficient finiteness gate is not an all-representative nonlifting certificate; actual flat tuples can have nonfinite centralizers.
lessons_before.boundary: The criterion assumes actual individual mates and does not produce them. Its generic proof uses the external constant-cover theorem in characteristic zero; horizontal constants eliminate nontrivial base-field extensions. A universal finiteness claim even for planar rescaled cotangent tuples with identity reduction would imply JC2. The positive nonpositional PBW control is an identity graph. The escaping-boundary Ore algebra has individual mates and a completed polynomial centralizer but fails module finiteness. No Long candidate passes the new gate yet, and QST1's excluded rational pair orbit remains excluded. QET1 supplies another positive gate: a finitely generated actual scalar centralizer with birational fraction field is polynomial once individual mates exist. A Galois field also collapses to degree one by divisor retention and branch purity; a nontrivial Galois field therefore forbids those mates. A nonpolynomial survivor has non-Galois degree at least three. Actual field data, finite generation and the unit condition are essential; leading field degree does not substitute. QET1 also removes actual parameter poles under the polynomial classical centralizer hypothesis, with no finite-generation or field-degree assumption: individual mates have unique finite polynomial polar parts. Subtraction preserves any integral curvature exactly, so an actual generic flat tuple with regular positions descends to a finite integral flat tuple and can match a prescribed classical flat frame. Only h is inverted; rational spatial/operator denominators and arbitrary completed series remain outside this descent. QTB1 gives birational polynomiality without first proving module finiteness or algebra finite generation. Coordinate-differential overrings of the rational position field are localizations; scalar units remove all denominators. Actual generic mates then descend integrally by QET1 and curvature is finitely corrected by QFC1. This still needs an actual birational field certificate. QPD1 allows rational centralizer field tests in a rank-one projective order without first exhibiting actual ratios or checking its scalar units separately. Spectral denominators clear all rational commutants and rational individual mates, but torsion alone does not supply the actual mates required by QFC1. No generic scalar free frame or new Long input is constructed. QGC1 also applies the multiplier/Fitting criterion to a finite full valuation-level lattice obtained from the identified classical graph, removing original saturation at ordinary quantum parameter. Split-abelian equivariance of the correct torsion-free special rank gives another finite repair for arbitrary parameter order. Neither argument proves finite generation of a new quantum position centralizer. The etale multiplier belongs above the physical target field in the larger closure; it does not make Long degree-three image map etale-finite or rule out its original graph.
lessons_before.reopen_when: An actual finite Long pair with integral individual conjugates has a complete module-finite leading-symbol centralizer certificate, another direct finiteness proof, or a structural obstruction shows the finiteness gate cannot hold for every admissible candidate.

lessons_before.title: Use actual centralizer field and boundary inertia before proving module finiteness
lessons_before.when: A fixed commuting quantum pair or tuple has a finitely generated commutative actual centralizer and one wants individual conjugates or a finite flat completion.
lessons_before.use: Determine the actual fraction field H over L(F_i). Under actual generic individual mates and QFC1's classical hypothesis, differential simplicity makes the finitely generated centralizer etale. Scalar Weyl units retain every base divisor; birational or Galois field data then force the polynomial centralizer and finite completion. A nontrivial Galois field instead obstructs simultaneous individual mates in all orders. Every generic inertia generator of a nonpolynomial survivor must have a fixed sheet, and its field is non-Galois of degree at least three. For another actual algebra verify the finite field extension and base-unit condition explicitly. Normalize their finite polynomial parameter-pole parts first; a full generic flat tuple already descends integrally without centralizer finite generation.
lessons_before.avoid: Confusing finite algebra generation with module finiteness, leading-symbol field degree with actual centralizer field degree, the latter with whole quantum division indices, a local fixed sheet with one global branch, or scalar Weyl units with units of a projective idealizer. Do not assert finite generation for all Long centralizers or use the Galois theorem without actual centralizer and individual-mate hypotheses.
lessons_before.boundary: A unit-bearing quadratic Galois Ore model has full flat relations and identity classical reduction but is outside the scalar Weyl algebra. The retained rank-three cotangent countercontrol has non-Galois cubic centralizer field with S3 normal closure, so the degree-three lower bound is sharp there and no universal finiteness follows. The scalar quadratic deformation has rational mates but no finite mate. Birationality is an actual field certificate, not a leading or completed one. The general etale/normalization theorem assumes finite generation; that hypothesis remains unknown for a new Long candidate. QET1 also removes actual parameter poles under the polynomial classical centralizer hypothesis, with no finite-generation or field-degree assumption: individual mates have unique finite polynomial polar parts. Subtraction preserves any integral curvature exactly, so an actual generic flat tuple with regular positions descends to a finite integral flat tuple and can match a prescribed classical flat frame. Only h is inverted; rational spatial/operator denominators and arbitrary completed series remain outside this descent. QTB1 removes finite generation from the birational/Galois conclusions, not from the finite-type etale description. Taylor flatness gives unramified valuations in every specified finite intermediate, so no nontrivial finite Galois factor survives. A birational differential overring is a localization, and scalar units force it polynomial. An actual radical ratio supplies a finite obstruction certificate without computing all B. QPD1 supplies scalar units and the field hypotheses for rank-one finite projective Weyl orders and identifies their rational centralizer with Frac B, without a scalar free frame. Its spectral clearing theorem equates rational individual admission with torsion; actual zero classes and full curvature still remain separate. The commutativity hypothesis must hold, as QSC1 ensures for Long.

lessons_before.when: An actual normal affine double sign surface has irreducible branch, finite rational-tree resolution singularities and knot outer boundary; in particular the entire surviving quartic Keller packet has the PF54 everywhere-etale cyclic triple.
lessons_before.use: Close the units quotient with the prime cyclic-cover theorem or quadratic UFD degree descent. Kummer then requires nonzero Pic[3] for the quartic triple. Apply the singular Stein CW theorem to S, then the relative exceptional-tree sequence to prove H1 unchanged and H2 of its resolution free. For the compact truncation, compute the exact boundary sequence and the torsion correction: detK=abs(det Q)*abs(H1(S))^2. Thus9 divides detK in the quartic, and the entire Picard torsion order squared divides detK. Retain the isotropic torsion image in the boundary linking form, which can fail even at order9. Propagate the3-adic cable recurrence through every stage with actual winding convention.
lessons_before.avoid: Using a smooth-only Stein theorem on a singular sign surface; assuming a resolution is affine; discarding torsion in H2 before deriving the square formula; replacing the whole torsion correction by H1 without proving freeness; substituting Cl[3] for Cartier Pic[3] or quasi-etale for everywhere etale; assuming nine divisibility suffices for global monodromy; assuming a rational compactification or negative definiteness; exporting S4/V4=S3 to higher symmetric groups.
lessons_before.boundary: PF2RULED55 excludes all infinity knots with v3(detK)<=1 for the entire quartic packet at unbounded source orders, target degrees and rulings. The sign-surface square theorem is independent of branch degree, conditional on the stated topology and actual cover data. Oka Pic=Z3 is a Cstar-branch control; the A2 cone has Cl=Z3 but Pic0. 55 finite controls support written proofs with primary imports, not formal or independent full verification. Nine-divisible candidates and the general Keller objective remain open.
lessons_before.reopen_when: Use actual infinity discriminant/linking forms and the actual global Picard group, not deeper source coefficients. For nine-divisible survivors, test isotropic3 subgroups and combine the sign cover with the marked source and full trace-dual algebra. Higher Keller degrees need a separately justified global cover or a different general geometric argument.

lessons_before.title: Cover every carrier relation subspace and certify degree and support by coefficient units
lessons_before.when: A triangular carrier map is simplified by imposing simultaneous linear relations among its carrier outputs, or raw nonlinear occurrence counts are minimized in such graph restrictions.
lessons_before.use: Use reverse row reduction to cover every relation subspace by its highest-pivot chart. For each deleted outputj, include every free carrierk<j with an independent scalar, without a weight restriction. Build every full source-coefficient polynomial. A rational constant combination of the degree-defect coefficients equal to1 excludes the entire chart, including all parameter specializations. For sparsity, count parameter-independent nonzero coefficient slots; a unit identity among additional varying slots forces another occurrence. Classify surviving minimal-degree charts by exact generator identities, product-domain branches and coefficientwise normal forms. Independently replay live graph substitutions, rather than importing the producer embedding.
lessons_before.avoid: Treating512 charts as512 sampled points; dropping cross-weight coefficients or pivot boundaries; assuming raw occurrence counts invariant under arbitrary affine output changes; asserting an entire Pareto frontier from fixed-dimension degree minima; using a generic Groebner answer or parameter probing as an exclusion; repeating the now-closed linear graph class.
lessons_before.boundary: KCUB29 covers all512 full relation charts of KCUB3 in its fixed highest-pivot graph parametrization and raw retained output frame.508 constant-combination obstructions give exact minimum degrees7,6,5,5,4,4,4,4,4,3 across dimensions3..12.511 charts have13 fixed nonlinear slots; one has12 plus a two-coefficient unit, so13 occurrences are sharp in the entire class regardless of degree. Minimal degree6/5/4 normal forms at4/5/7 variables have sharp15/17/23 counts; both quartic branches give the same saved map. Written echelon, block-Jacobian and polynomial-domain arguments combine with independent exact arithmetic, not formal or external review. Global support, affine-orbit and special-form dimension minima remain open. KCUB30 gives31 nonlinear/17 linear occurrences with a nonidentity unipotent linear part, still48 total. lessons_before.title: Rule out basepoint-free power differences and retain the unavoidable cubic order index
lessons_before.when: A polynomially A1-normalized irreducible branch curve is represented as A^p-B^q for coprime p,q>=2, or a genuine everywhere-etale sign triple supplies a normal cubic resolvent with only2+1 branch fibres.
lessons_before.use: Treat dependent and dominant coefficient maps separately. Constant units on A1 force coefficient constancy along the branch if there is no basepoint. Use polynomial abc for the dependent image and an explicit logarithmic pq-canonical form for the dominant map lifted to the smooth-point blowup retaining its exceptional curve. The piecewise toric order identities prove the obstruction in all degrees and exponents. For the actual quartic cubic quotient, derive the local product R x R[z]/(z^2-G) also at sign singularities; a global generator would produce a basepoint-free square-cube branch equation, contradiction. Keep the nonconstant determinant index of every primitive integral cubic element and the full normal algebra.
lessons_before.avoid: Assuming coefficient-map dominance; applying polynomial abc directly to two-variable polynomials; dropping the exceptional curve after blowing up a smooth branch point; checking a finite fan census instead of all-ray identities; treating any monogenic S3 cover of an immersive A1 curve as having an everywhere-etale sign triple; confusing free modules or primitive field elements with monogenic integral algebras; discarding the discriminant index square or assuming its support is distinct from the true branch; putting the cubic resolvent inside the quartic source field.
lessons_before.boundary: PF2RULED56 proves the coprime power-difference basepoint theorem in all polynomial degrees and exponents and excludes all globally monogenic normal cubic resolvents for the entire actual quartic packet. It does not force monogenicity or prove Picard3 vanishing. The explicit A1 A5 torus curve has an inner basepoint and a non-etale sign triple at its singularity; Oka Cstar covers remain allowed. 59 exact controls support written unbounded proofs, not formal or independent full verification.
lessons_before.reopen_when: Couple the unavoidable cubic order index to the marked quartic source and PF53 trace-dual algebra, or test actual Picard/linking data. A full contradiction needs a separately proved normal monogenic resolvent or another obstruction to every allowed index. Higher Keller degrees need separately justified cover data. Do not replace those missing geometric implications with a coefficient sweep.

lessons_before.title: Use Taylor branches and actual radical certificates without centralizer finite generation
lessons_before.when: A commuting scalar quantum tuple has polynomial classical joint centralizer and one wants a positive completion certificate or an all-partner obstruction, with no finite presentation of its actual centralizer.
lessons_before.use: Use commuting translation derivations and the injective Taylor map at an arbitrary maximal ideal. Flatness of its coordinate map retains an unramified valuation over every base divisor in every finite intermediate centralizer field. No nontrivial finite Galois factor can survive. Birationality then forces the actual centralizer polynomial, without finite generation, and actual generic mates yield finite integral full completion. For an obstruction it suffices to exhibit actual commutants b,c and q(F)b^k=p(F)c^k with p/q not a kth power; this certifies a forbidden radical in Frac B without computing all B. Monodromy point stabilizers must normally generate their group.
lessons_before.avoid: Requiring centralizer finite generation before the birational, Galois-factor or radical tests; inferring finite-type etaleness without that hypothesis; replacing Frac B membership by arbitrary rational commutation; confusing total order at a singular point with a divisorial valuation; or inferring a common global sheet from local inertia fixed points. QPD1 supplies unit and field hypotheses automatically for rank-one finite projective Weyl orders; verify them separately outside that class.
lessons_before.boundary: The unit condition remains essential, as infinite differential localizations demonstrate. H may be an infinite algebraic extension; the theorem normalizes only each specified finite intermediate field. The scalar radical descent uses constant root-of-unity extension and actual centralizer membership. S3 cubic fields can survive; D4 quartics fail because of a quadratic Galois factor. No actual new Long field or radical certificate is supplied. QET1's finite-type etale description retains its finite-generation hypothesis. QPD1 automatically verifies the unit, algebraicity and horizontal-constant hypotheses for a commutative centralizer in a rank-one finite projective Weyl order. Every rational commutant clears by a polynomial in the complete commuting images, so Frac B membership is automatic there. Radical and Galois-factor certificates can therefore be tested in the full Weyl division realization before a scalar free frame. Other endomorphism algebras retain separate hypotheses. QCI1 proves H/C finite for any actual full tuple with finite whole division indices, even when B is not finitely generated. Its degree d divides both N_l,N_r and N=d*M. For Long, residual M>=3 and the no-Galois-factor theorem makes nontrivial d>=3, hence N>=9. The commutative valued-field tower is only a control, not a Weyl or Long construction. QCI1 exhibits rational full pairs with birational chosen-position centralizer and genuine residual degree m, but no finite carrier in any diagonal finite rank. The all-rank obstruction is bounded matrix powers, not a forbidden Galois factor. Its source exchange changes (d,M) from (1,m) to (m,1), and the displayed rational family does not meet the actual-order hypotheses of the Taylor theorem. QGD1 supplies a separate Galois obstruction for the whole noncommutative image division ring, not H/C. Its finite quotient residue must be Galois after accounting for all valuation branches; the full classical Long cubic is not. No centralizer finite generation or chosen position field is needed for that whole-field theorem. A larger S3 normal closure with a subgroup-fixed source remains outside the direct-quotient exclusion.
lessons_before.reopen_when: A new actual Long pair admits a birational centralizer field proof and actual individual mates, an exact forbidden radical/Galois-factor certificate, or a finite intermediate monodromy field violating stabilizer normal generation or local fixed-sheet conditions.

lessons_before.title: Use shared principal factors and cancel every weighted top source
lessons_before.when: A complete rational twisted reduction has coefficient factors shared across its principal projections, or a weighted phase has independently variable top coefficients.
lessons_before.use: Inspect the whole principal division before multiplying its leading coefficients. In ordinary-node normal form A=aD,B=dD,E=DLe,F=DLf, clear D only once, keeping exact combined divergence cofactors and all old coefficient opens. Use a formal degree grading before substituting linear D,Le,Lf. For cusp/tangent choose two weighted Euler coefficients to cancel both top source terms, including their volume divergence and their derivatives on every later amplitude. Retain actual-seed rank, basis grades and scalar valuations; add all frame branches before taking a global maximum.
lessons_before.avoid: Assuming principal coefficients have unrelated denominators; removing a shared D without verifying all complete cofactors; introducing coprimality or D(0)!=0; bounding separate fourth-operator products after their leading cancellation; changing only the scalar source while dropping amplitude derivatives; omitting volume terms; calling complement227 or254 a full gate; lowering even258 to257 by parity; rewriting hash-bound earlier proof bodies.
